about: Findings about hoi3_tfh.exe from BiceLib's headers, hooks and reversing notes. rva is module relative. Checked against the executable by buildFindings.py. A global may carry a type, which the script gives the data there ("string" for a C string).

addresses.name: CSubUnit::SettleDamage
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSubUnit::SettleDamage(CSubUnit* subunit@ESI, int unused@stack:4)
addresses.comment:
**Spends a subunit's pending damage and clears it.** The receiver is in ESI and the one stack argument is not read. Four callers: CCombatant::ApplyLosses (0x166298) and three in the 0x1C38xx-0x1C3Exx range.

    ebx = min(pending organisation, organisation)   ; 0x1ABAE1, a cmovg
    strength     -= pending strength                ; 0x1ABAE4, unclamped
    organisation -= ebx                             ; 0x1ABAE7, clamped
    pending strength = pending organisation = 0     ; 0x1ABAF7, 0x1ABAFD

**The clamp is the thing worth knowing.** A tick's organisation damage is capped at what the subunit still has, so the total CUnit::TakeDamage accumulated is damage *attempted* and this is damage *dealt* - they differ by a lot in a one-sided fight. A tooltip built on the raw total showed a division with about sixty organisation taking several hundred, which is what sent the watch here.

Found by a hardware write watch on a fighting subunit's +0xAC: 488 writes adding from CUnit::TakeDamage and 49 clearing from here. Nothing static had reached it - see BiceLib/Reversing/WriteWatch.hpp.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::Attack
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombatant::Attack(CLandCombatant* this, CCombatant* other)
addresses.comment: **One side's shooting for a tick**, CCombatant slot 15, which CCombat is pure virtual for. Walks this side's front line - the CList at CCombatant +0xB0 - and calls CLandCombatant::FireUnit once per unit on it. Everything before that is set-up: it refreshes the doctrine figures out of LAND_DOCTRINE_INCREASE and seeds the tick's random stream.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::FireUnit
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CLandCombatant::FireUnit(CLandCombatant* side@stack:4, uint* random@stack:8, CUnit* attacker@ESI, CCombatant* enemy@ECX)
addresses.comment:
**One attacking unit's shots for a tick.** The attacker is in **ESI** and the side being shot at in **ECX**, neither loaded from the frame; the two stack arguments are this side and the tick's random state. Read off the call site in CLandCombatant::Attack (0x16B3B0..0x16B3BE), not off the decompiler - which showed the enemy as EDI, the register FireUnit copies ECX into at 0x16ADE3 for CCombatant::PickTarget's benefit.

It draws **one** target for the whole tick - CCombatant::PickTarget, a uniform random pick from the enemy's front line - and then works out how many shots to fire:

    hard = attacker.definition.hard_attack * (1000 + owner.HARD_ATTACK) / 1000
    soft = attacker.definition.soft_attack * (1000 + owner.SOFT_ATTACK) / 1000
    s    = target.definition.softness
    hard = hard * (1000 - s) / 1000      soft = soft * s / 1000
    shots = (attacker.+0xEC * attacker.+0xF4 / 1000) * (soft + hard) / 1000 / 1000
    and the remainder is a chance at one more shot

**So the split between soft and hard attack is the target's softness**, and the combat modifier the tooltip prints multiplies the shot *count* rather than the damage per shot.

Each shot then runs while the target is not already finished (CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight): the defence is the target's toughness when this side is defending and its defensiveness when attacking, times the target's own defend product; CUnit::RollToHit decides; and on a hit the damage is scaled by the combat's doctrine figure plus CUnit::StrengthDamageFactor, halved through LAND_COMBAT_STR/ORG_ARMOR_DEFLECTION_FACTOR when the attacker's piercing_attack is below the target's armor, scaled again by LAND_COMBAT_STR/ORG_DAMAGE_MODIFIER, and handed to CUnit::TakeDamage.

addresses.name: CCombatant::PickTarget
addresses.signature: CUnit* __stdcall CCombatant::PickTarget(uint* random@EDX, CCombatant* side@EDI) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**Draws one of a side's front line units at random**, uniformly: `r % side->front_line.count` nodes along the CList at +0xB0, or 0 when the count is below 1. The side is in EDI, the random state in EDX and the result comes back in EAX - which has to be said, because a signature that places any parameter switches Ghidra to custom storage and then the **return** needs a place as well or it decompiles as an undefined4 at every call site. ECX is live at the call but the body never reads it, so it is not an argument.

The generator is the MSVC one, `x = x * 0x343FD + 0x269EC3` twice per draw with the top bits multiplied together, and its state is threaded through the whole tick from CLandCombatant::Attack - so one stream decides every target and every fractional shot in a round.

addresses.name: CUnit::RollToHit
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CUnit::RollToHit(CUnit* target, int defence)
addresses.comment:
**Whether one shot lands, and it spends the target's defence.** `defence` is thousandths; its whole part is how many shots the target can still defend against this tick and the remainder is a chance at one more.

    if (slots <= target->defences_used)  avoid = CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF
    else { avoid = BASE_CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT
           if (target->IsLand()) avoid += the owner's TechnologyStatus +0x8
           ++target->defences_used }
    avoid = min(avoid, 99000)
    return avoid / 1000 <= rand() % 100

**So a unit does not dodge by chance alone - it runs out.** Once `defences_used` reaches what its defence value bought, every further shot that tick is judged by the much worse no-defence figure, which is what makes being outnumbered compound.

addresses.name: CUnit::StrengthDamageFactor
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CUnit::StrengthDamageFactor(CUnit* this, int* out)
addresses.comment: **How hard a unit hits for the men it still has.** Totals its subunits' strength, divides by GetMaxStrength (slot 23), and returns roughly that percentage over a hundred - floored at 1, so even a shattered division still throws something - times the global at rva 0x1A8874C. Added to the combat's doctrine figure by CLandCombatant::FireUnit to scale a landed shot.

addresses.name: CUnit::TakeDamage
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnit::TakeDamage(CUnit* unit@EAX, int strength@stack:4, int organisation@stack:8)
addresses.comment:
**Spreads one landed shot over every subunit of the unit hit.** The unit is in EAX. Strength damage is shared in proportion to each subunit's own maximum - `share = subunit.GetMaxStrength * 1000 / unit.GetMaxStrength` - while organisation damage is split evenly, one part per subunit.

Nothing is subtracted here. It accumulates into CSubUnit +0xA8, which CCombatant::ApplyLosses spends against `strength` at the end of the tick, and into +0xAC, **whose consumer has not been found** - see that field. That is what lets CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight tell a unit already killed this tick from one still worth shooting at, before any of it has been applied.

addresses.name: CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight(CUnit* unit@EAX) @AL
addresses.comment: **True when every subunit is already dead on this tick's arithmetic**, which is what stops a unit being shot at twice over. For each subunit it takes `strength - pending_strength_damage` - or `strength - global(0x1A8868C) * pending / 1000` where the subunit answers either of slots 9 or 11 - and returns 0 the moment one of them is still above zero. The unit is in EAX.

addresses.name: CNavalCombat::Tick
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalCombat::Tick(CNavalCombat* this, int unused)
addresses.comment: **The naval per-tick resolution**, CCombat slot 15 overridden. Nothing to do with the land one at 0x16EBE0 beyond the slot: it makes no virtual call in its first 0x300 bytes and in particular never reaches CCombatant slot 19, so a ship's CUnit +0xDC modifier list is neither filled nor cleared. Confirmed live - a write watch on +0xE4 through a whole naval battle caught nothing at all, where a land battle caught the reset 4990 times.

addresses.name: CAirCombat::Tick
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAirCombat::Tick(CAirCombat* this, int unused)
addresses.comment: **The air per-tick resolution**, CCombat slot 15 overridden, and shared by CGroundBombing, CLandBombing and CNavalBombing - so one body covers every kind of air action. It calls slots 15, 17 and 18 through the vftable and never 0x4C, which is CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers, so no air unit gets a combat modifier list. Confirmed the same way as the naval one.

addresses.name: CUnit::AddCombatModifier
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnit::AddCombatModifier(CUnit* unit@ESI, CombatModifier id@stack:4, int attack@stack:8, int defend@stack:12)
addresses.comment:
**Adds one modifier to a unit's list and folds it into the running product.** `ret 0xC` for the three stack arguments; the unit arrives in **ESI** and is never loaded from the frame, which is why a byte search for stores to +0xDC through a named pointer never found this.

It allocates twice: a 12 byte record holding the id at +0, the attack delta at +4 and the defend delta at +8 - which is what the battle tooltip reads and prints as `x%/y%` when the two differ - and a 16 byte CListNode for it. Then `last = node`, `++count`, and `first = node` only when the count was zero, which is why watching +0xDC caught resets and no additions: the head is written on the empty-list branch alone.

**Then it multiplies.** `unit->+0xEC = unit->+0xEC * max(attack + 1000, floor) / 1000` and the same for the defend side into +0xF0, with `floor` read from the global at 0x1A8873C (zero in the image, so presumably set at load). So a modifier's value is a **delta** - +22.5% is 225 - turned into a factor by the `add eax, 0x3e8`, and the two fields hold the running product of everything on the list. That is what the tooltip prints as its Attack and Defend Modifier, and why CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers seeds both with 1000.

Found with a hardware write watchpoint on a live unit's +0xE4, the list's count - see BiceLib/Reversing/WriteWatch.hpp. Nothing static had reached it.

addresses.name: CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers(CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment:
**Empties a unit's combat modifiers and puts the four multipliers back to neutral.** Frees every node of the CList at +0xDC, zeroes its three fields, and writes 1000 into +0xEC, +0xF0, +0xF4 and +0xF8 - which is what settles that all four are multipliers rather than two values and two multipliers.

Two callers: CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590), which clears before it rebuilds, and CUnit::~CUnit (0x1B5560). Found with a hardware write watchpoint on a live unit - see BiceLib/Reversing/WriteWatch.hpp - after a byte search for stores to +0xDC had turned it up and a range filter had thrown it away for sitting in CUnit's code rather than the combatant's.

addresses.name: CUnit::~CUnit
addresses.no_signature: A destructor's own shape - it writes the vftable at +0 and +8 and takes no argument beyond its receiver - but which of the three unit classes Ghidra should attach it to has not been checked, and a wrong `this` type reads every field at the wrong offset.
addresses.comment: **CUnit's destructor**: writes CUnit::vftable into +0 and +8, releases the orders and plans, calls CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers to free the combat modifier list, then walks the regiments. Reached while looking for what *builds* that list, which it is not.

addresses.name: CCombat::Tick
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombat::Tick(CCombat* this, int unused)
addresses.comment: **The land per-tick combat resolution**, CCombat slot 15 - and CLandCombat's, which shares this body. **Not naval or air**: both override the slot, with 0x17BA00 and 0x17BC50, and neither reaches slot 19 at all. Increments `duration` (+0x20), swaps tactics when TACTIC_SWAP_FREQUENCEY divides it or either side has none, then calls CCombatant slot 19 on `attacker` (+0x10) and `defender` (+0x14) and CCombatant slot 15 on each, and finally ApplyOwnCombatModifiers on each. The one stack argument is **never read** - `[ebp+8]` appears nowhere in the function - so it is named for the space it takes.

addresses.name: CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment: **Slot 19, the shared part**: the per-kind overrides call this first. Writes the two multipliers onto each of this side's units, CUnit +0xF4 for attack and +0xF8 for defence. `flag` is zero at both call sites in CCombat::Tick and its meaning is not known.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CLandCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment: **Slot 19 for a land fight**, and the readable example of the family. Walks `units` (+0x40), and for a unit that is invading over water interpolates between AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_ATTACK_LOW and _HIGH into CUnit +0xF4 and between the defend pair into +0xF8. Calls the base at 0x165590 first.

addresses.name: CCombatant::ApplyLosses
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCombatant::ApplyLosses(CCombatant* combatant@EDI, int* lossesOut@stack:4)
addresses.comment:
**Applies a tick's damage to this side's subunits and totals what it cost.** 790 bytes; the receiver is in EDI and the single stack argument is an out parameter that receives the strength lost by this call (`mov [eax], ecx` at 0x1661CE).

The accounting, at 0x16625F, is the part worth hooking. ESI is the **CSubUnit** taking the hit and EDI its combatant:

    edx = subunit->strength (+0x5C) - damage
    type = subunit->definition(+0x58)->index(+0x24)
    if (edx < 0)   combatant->destroyed[type] += 1000; combatant->losses += 1000
    else           combatant->damaged[type]  += the damage

So losses are kept **per side** (+0x84) and **per subunit type** (+0x88 destroyed, +0x98 damaged) and **never per unit** - though the subunit is in hand at that instruction, and CRegiment +0xB0 leads to its CUnit, which is what makes per-unit tracking possible from here.

Two earlier names for this function were wrong, both from partial readings: it is not `ApplyUnitStrengths` and not `ApplyOwnCombatModifiers`. Ghidra had it as a one byte body - reversing/ghidra/RepairFunctionBody.java fixes that - so every reading before the repair saw a fraction of it.

addresses.name: CCombatView::BuildUnitTooltip
addresses.no_signature: Three arguments and `ret 0xc`, but the second is untouched on every path read and the first is a window of some kind, so typing them would be guessing at two of the three.
addresses.comment: **The tooltip for a unit hovered in a battle.** Its only caller is 0x331C77. Writes, in order: the leader line (LEADER_COMMAND_INFO, or NO_LEADER_FOR_THIS_1/_2 where there is none), UNIT_COMBAT_WIDTH, CURR_COMB_STR, BATTLE_ATTACKMOD, BATTLE_DEFENDMOD, CURR_COMB_ORG, and then the variable part - a walk of the CList at CUnit +0xDC, one node per combat modifier, each turned into a BM_* localisation key by the switch at 0x164060.\n\n**The unit is in EDI** through the whole second half. Not assumed: [edi + 0x12C] is read for the leader line and is CUnit::leader_ptr, and [edi + 0x40] is compared against 1 to choose the wording, which is the count of CUnit::regiments. BiceLib's hook checks the vftable regardless.

addresses.name: CombatModifierKey
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CombatModifierKey(Hoi3CString* out@ECX, CombatModifier modifier@EAX)
addresses.comment:
**Turns a combat modifier id into its localisation key**, and is the only place that enum is written down. `reversing/combatModifiers.py` reads all 30 names off the jump table at 0x16429C and buildFindings makes them the `CombatModifier` enum, so the arms do not have to be transcribed - which is how this entry was twice wrong before, once putting BM_NIGHT_MODIFIER at 0x1C when it is 0x1B, and once putting BM_SURPRISE_BONUS at 0x1E, one past the end.

**The bound is the function's own**: `cmp eax, 0x1d; ja <default>` at 0x164067, so the ids are 0..0x1D and anything else gets the fallback. The id arrives in **EAX** and the string to build into in **ECX** (`mov esi, ecx` at 0x164065); `ret 0`, so nothing is passed on the stack at all - an earlier reading here said the string was a stack argument, and checkSignatures caught it against the ret.

addresses.name: std::string::operator=
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::string::operator=(Hoi3CString* this, Hoi3CString* source@EAX)
addresses.comment: Four instructions: `assign(source, 0, npos)`. **The source arrives in eax** - the compiler gave this thunk a convention of its own - and the destination in ecx as usual. Eight call sites. What CCountry::SetOobFile is made of.

addresses.name: std::string::clear
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::string::clear(Hoi3CString* this)
addresses.comment: Gives the buffer back where the string had one - `if (capacity >= 0x10) free(data)` - and leaves it empty: capacity 0xF, length 0, first byte 0. The destructor's body as well as `clear()`, which is why it turns up at the end of every function that built a string.

addresses.name: std::string::assignString
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall assignString(Hoi3CString* this, Hoi3CString* text, unsigned int from, unsigned int count) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Replaces** this string with part of another - the same three arguments and the same bounds check as `appendString` (`0x33E30`), and the pair are easy to mistake for each other. **5489 call sites.** The requirement renderer uses this one to hand its finished text back through the out parameter.

addresses.name: LogRecord::Make
addresses.signature: LogRecord* __cdecl LogRecord::Make(LogRecord* this@ECX, Hoi3CString* file, int line, int channel)
addresses.comment:
**Builds one log record**, and first makes sure there is a sink: if `g_log_sink` (`0x17162A4`) is still null it allocates the four byte do-nothing sink whose vftable is `0x11FCEA0` and installs that, so a message logged before `InstallLogSink` is discarded rather than queued. Then calls the register-convention forwarder `LogRecord::Construct` (`0x6649D0`) with the file, the sink, the line and the channel. There is **no channel test here or anywhere after it** - every record built is flushed to the sink. `this` arrives in ECX and is returned in EAX; the three stack arguments are cleaned by the caller (bare `ret`, `add esp, 0xC` at the call site), so the convention is `__cdecl` with a register `this`, not `__thiscall`.

**`file` is an `Hoi3CString*`, not a `const char*`.** The constructor hands it to `std::string::assignString` (`0x1BD0`), which takes a string, and every call site builds one first: `mov edx, 'battleplan.cpp'; lea esi,[ebp-0x74]; call std::string::fromCString` and then pushes that temporary (0x404743..0x404768).

addresses.name: LogRecord::Flush
addresses.signature: void __cdecl LogRecord::Flush(LogRecord* record@EAX)
addresses.comment: **The complete destructor of the record, and where a log line is decided.** Every message in the game arrives here in a record holding its file, line and channel, and this is what does or does not write it - `[persistent.cpp:39]`, `[countryhistory.cpp:450]` and the 597KB of setup.log all pass through it. Takes the record in eax, pushes `record+0x78` (the `std::basic_ios` virtual base) into `LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct`, then puts the `ios_base` vftable `0x15A7B8C` at `record+0x78` and runs `~ios_base` (`0x794BAE`). Nothing is returned: eax at the `ret` is whatever `~ios_base` left there and no caller reads it. **The one place worth hooking to see everything the engine complains about**, including the channels that produce no file.

addresses.signature: CCombatHistoryEntry* __stdcall CCombatHistoryEntry::CCombatHistoryEntry(CCombatHistoryEntry* this@ESI, CCombat* combat@ECX, int* tick@EAX)

addresses.name: std::string::appendChars
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall appendChars(Hoi3CString* this, const char* text, unsigned int length) @EAX
addresses.comment: Adds \p length characters to the end of a string, growing it. **358 call sites.** The name is BiceLib's: this is one of `append`'s overloads and the game keeps no name for it. addresses.name: DoNothing_4Args
addresses.signature: void __stdcall DoNothing_4Args(void* a, void* b, void* c, void* d)
addresses.comment: `ret 0x10` and nothing else, so the linker folded it: this one address fills a virtual slot in 38 unrelated classes and belongs to none of them. It was recorded as LogSink::WriteNothing, which is one of the 38 - the fallback sink's slot 1 does point here, but so does everything else that needed a four argument no-op. Slot 1 of the **fallback** sink's vftable (rva `0x11FCEA0`, VA `0x015FCEA0`), and it is `ret 0x10` and nothing else. That sink is the one `0x2410` makes if the global is still null, so a message logged before the real sink is installed is discarded outright rather than queued. **The body is not the fallback sink's own** - the linker folded it with every other four-argument do-nothing virtual in the program, and it sits in 38 RTTI classes' tables.

addresses.comment: Slot 1 of CPersistent, and the whole of an object's braces: it writes `{`, calls slot 2 for the class's own keys, then indents and writes `}`. addresses.name: GetTotalBuildCost
addresses.signature: void __cdecl GetTotalBuildCost(CSubUnitDefinition* definition, CCountry* country, longlong* ic, longlong* manpower)
addresses.comment: What a unit type will cost this country in all - the whole build, not a day of it. Four arguments: the definition, the country, and somewhere to put an IC figure and a manpower one, either of which may be null to skip that half; both come back as fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>. It adds up CTechnologyStatus +0x218 over the definition's own technology list (+0x44..+0x48), hands that total to CCountry::GetBuildTime (0xE19A0) for the days, works the daily cost out with the same terms as CCountry::GetBuildCostIC - but without its reserves step, which this does not have - and multiplies the two. The manpower half does the same from +0xFC with CTechnologyStatus +0x25C and a floor from a global. Its three callers all add the two figures onto running totals. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CGainableTrait::LoadKey

addresses.name: CTraitGainTracker::SaveContents

That this class has a SaveContents of its own, rather than the shared empty one at `0x20CD50`, is what says the progress is game state rather than a definition. **Read live**: a leader's history holds the tracker, at `CLeaderHistory + 0x40` - 399 of 400 histories in a running game point at one. addresses.name: CBrigadeConstructionDefinition::SetName
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CBrigadeConstructionDefinition::SetName(CBrigadeConstructionDefinition* this@EDI, Hoi3CString* name@ESI)
addresses.comment: Assigns the brigade's name at +0x18 (`lea ecx,[edi+0x18]`, std::string::assign with 0 and -1) and then hands the owning country and that same string to 0xCB450. Both arguments are registers and it takes nothing on the stack - no frame beyond `push ecx` for one local, and a bare `ret`; the caller at 0x82E4D sets `esi` from std::string::fromCString and `edi` from the object. **The lookup is a country lookup, not a string one**: `lea ecx,[edi+8]; call 0x402610` reads +8 and +0xC as a CCountryTag and returns `countries[id]`. project.json records +0x8 as `display_name Hoi3CString`, which cannot be right - a Hoi3CString is 0x18 bytes, so one at +8 would swallow +0x10, +0x14 and the name at +0x18. The field was left alone here rather than renamed on the strength of one call site.

addresses.name: CMap::CMap
addresses.signature: CMap* __stdcall CMap::CMap(CMap* this) @EAX
addresses.comment: CMap constructor (object 0x2A94 bytes), and the only place the whole layout is visible at once - it has exactly one caller, 0x488243. `this` arrives on the stack, not in ecx (`mov edi,[ebp+8]`, `ret 4`), and comes back in eax. It writes CMap's primary vftable (rva 0x11BE3EC) at +0 and CMap's secondary vftable (rva 0x11BE408) at **+8**, with the CPersistent meta word 0x18D at +4; the +8 sub-object is built first with a base vftable at VA 0x15FDB48 and holds an Hoi3CString at +0xC set to `default.map`. It then constructs 512 CLists at +0x50 (through the CRT vector-constructor iterator, element ctor 0x9CE0, dtor 0x4A30D0), empties the twelve file-name strings from +0x2054 to +0x219C, zeroes the province and terrain vectors, memsets +0x2220 (0x400 bytes, to 0) and +0x2620 (0x400 bytes, to 0xFF), builds the engine string hash table at +0x2A50 with 0x1FF buckets, defaults +0x2A80 to 400 and the player tag at +0x2A88 to `---`/0, and finally reserves **14500** entries in the province vector at +0x2200. It also fills six global Hoi3CStrings with the map paths it will read: `default.map`, `cache/time`, `cache/navaldist.bin`, `cache/climate.bin`, `cache/provincecache.bin`, `cache/bboxcache.bin` at VA 0x170C750, 0x170C76C, 0x170C788, 0x170C7A4, 0x170C7C0, 0x170C7DC.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDefinition::IsCarrier
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CSubUnitDefinition::IsCarrier(CSubUnitDefinition* this) @AL
addresses.comment:
`cmp [ecx+0x190], 0; setg al; ret` - three instructions. A carrier is a ship whose `carrier_size` (+0x190) is **above** zero, not a flag byte like the other kind tests, so a definition with a zero or negative carrier_size is not one.

Nothing calls it directly. Its one reference in the image is at 0x8EDDF8, where its address is pushed next to the literal `IsCarrier` in a run of (name, address) pairs alongside `IsValid`, `IsSecondRank` and `GetCompletionSize` - a luabind class registration. So the name is the game's own, the receiver really is the definition in ecx, and the function exists for script rather than for engine code.

addresses.name: CProvince::SaveContents
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CProvince::SaveContents(CProvince* this, CSaveWriter* writer)
addresses.comment: Province save writer, slot 2 of CProvince and of CMapProvince. Slot 2 of CPersistent, which the rest of the family calls SaveContents; BiceLib had it as WriteSave, kept as a label. **It is the province's field list in save order**: flags (+0xC4), owner (+0x32C, only when the tag id at +0x330 is set), controller (+0x334, gated on +0x338), underground_owner (+0x38C, gated on +0x390), underground_action (+0x394, skipped when it is 2), one `core` per node of the list at +0x344 (the node *is* the tag, next at node+0xC), capital (+0x2B0, only when true), manpower (+0x320) and leadership (+0x324) when positive, revolt_risk (+0x328) when positive, strategic_resource (the object at +0x18, its name string at +0x30), every building at +0x310, history (+0xD8) when +0xEC is positive, points (+0x34), nationalism (+0x24) when non-null, then the seven goods pools - pool (+0x15C), throughput ([+0x1F8]), last_throughput ([+0x1F4]), drawn ([+0x1A8]), last_drawn ([+0x1A4]), current_producing (+0x268), max_producing (+0x28C) - each skipped when all seven of its goods equal the global at VA 0x1A87818, then weather (+0x68), last_convoy_attack (+0x1C) when the date is more than a year old, out_of_supply_days (+0x20) when positive, and one `modifier` per node of the list at +0x13C. It does *not* write +0x180 (last_pool) or the drawn/throughput buffers directly, only through the two pointers each.

addresses.signature: int* __stdcall SupplyCapacity(CMapProvince* province, int* out)

addresses.name: SupplyLoss
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall SupplyLoss(CMapProvince* province@EAX, int* out)
addresses.comment: Fills the supplies lost crossing one province, which the daily supply pass adds to the demand it carries to a neighbour and subtracts again on delivery. Starts from defines->supply(+0xAC)(+0x34), **halves it where the province's owner id (+0x330) equals its controller id (+0x338)**, adds a partisan term built from defines->supply(+0x38) and the province's +0x84 when +0x88 is zero, scales the whole thing by the controller's +0xDF8(+0xC), and floors the result at zero. Against the mod's own common/defines.lua the two defines are SUPPLY_TAX and PARTISAN_EFFECT_ON_SUPPLY_TAX.

addresses.name: SupplyNeed
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SupplyNeed(CMapProvince* province, int* suppliesOut, int* fuelOut@EDI)
addresses.comment: Fills the per-province supply and fuel need the daily supply pass writes into CMapProvince::need. **Two out parameters and only one of them is on the stack**: the supplies total goes through the stack pointer at [ebp+0xC] and the fuel total through EDI, which the callers keep as a moving pointer into the fuel array. Both are zeroed on entry. It sums CUnit::SupplyConsumption (0x1BB560) and CUnit::FuelConsumption (0x1BB7A0) over the province's `units` (+0x2B8) and over two further unit lists at CMapProvince +0x54 and +0x58 whose meaning is not established. A unit is skipped where the province's controller id is a country at war with the unit's owner, and where either tag is REB; a virtual call on the unit's slot at +0x3C also has to return true.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildCost
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CCountry::GetBuildCost(CCountry* this, CFixedPoint* out, CBuilding* building)
addresses.comment:
What this country pays for a building: the building's own cost (CBuilding +0x58) scaled by the discount its technology category earns, cost x (1000 - discount) / 1000. The slot 2 call on the category that guards it is the folded `mov al,1; ret` at 0xA92590, true for a real category and for the nocategory object alike, so the discount is always applied. That matters for a building whose category is nocategory - its index is 0, where every country's ability is 0, and an ability below 5.000 raises the cost: A building whose category is nocategory therefore costs about half as much again.

**Signature**: out is the hidden first stack argument and comes back in eax; `this` is in ecx, which is why the `ret` is 8 and not 12.

Reads the two as fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>, so the shifts by 15 and 30 and the 0x1F40000 are only the fixed point arithmetic.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildCostIC
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CCountry::GetBuildCostIC(CCountry* this, CFixedPoint* out, CSubUnitDefinition* definition, int technologyBonus, bool reserves)
addresses.comment:
What a unit type costs this country. base is the definition's BuildCostIC (+0xF8); the multiplier is 1000, plus CTechnologyStatus +0x24C for the type, plus the third argument times 10 (so 1% a point), less the discount the definition's technology category (+0x3C) earns - the same 0xE1AC0 buildings use. Then, where the fourth argument is set, times (1000 + the country's RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE modifier, 77) over 1000. The third argument is the caller's: the game works it out at 0x63D40 by adding up CTechnologyStatus +0x218 over the definition's own technology list (+0x44..+0x48). Only Lua calls this entry point; the game's own path is GetTotalBuildCost (0x63D40), which works the same cost out inline without the reserves step and multiplies it by GetBuildTime.

**Signature**: four stack arguments (`ret 0x10`) with out hidden first and returned in eax; the flag at [ebp+0x14] is tested as a byte, so it is a bool.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildTime
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CCountry::GetBuildTime(CCountry* this, CSubUnitDefinition* definition, int technologyBonus)
addresses.comment:
How long a unit type takes this country to build. The definition's BuildTime (+0x100) times two factors over a million. The first is 1000, plus CTechnologyStatus +0x26C for the type, plus the second argument times 10, plus the country's UNIT_RECRUITMENT_TIME modifier (51), less the discount the definition's technology category earns (0xE1AC0, the same one the costs use); it is floored at 50. The second is 1000 plus one build speed modifier, chosen by the definition's kind flags in this order: is_rocket (+0x33) ROCKET_BUILD_SPEED, is_tank (+0x34) TANK_BUILD_SPEED, is_air (+0x2C) AIR_BUILD_SPEED, is_ship (+0x2E) NAVAL_BUILD_SPEED, else LAND_BUILD_SPEED.

**Signature**: unlike the costs this one answers a plain int in eax - divided by 1000 at 0x4E1AA5, and the callers multiply it back up - so there is no hidden out pointer and the `ret` is 8, not 12.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount(int* out@ESI, CCountry* country@stack:4, CTechnologyCategory* category@stack:8)
addresses.comment:
The discount a technology category earns, in thousandths, which the build cost is scaled by as (1000 - this). Takes the country's ability in that category - its own level at +0x698, or the sharer's if a tag at +0x6A8 names one with a higher level, the same lookup GetAbility makes - floors it at 0 and measures it against 5.000: below that the result is negative and the cost goes up, at 100 per point; above it 50 per point with everything past 1.000 halved first. Then adds the country's INDUSTRIAL_EFFICIENCY modifier (74) and CTechnologyStatus +0x94, and caps the whole at 990, so at most 99% off. The name is BiceLib's.

**The out pointer travels in ESI, not on the stack** - that is the whole of why the recorded signature wanted ret 12 and the function does ret 8. Only two things are pushed, the country and the category; ESI is never written in the body, only read (every store is `mov [esi], ...`), and the return is `mov eax, esi` at 0x4E1BCA.

addresses.name: CCountry::RebuildNeighbours
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCountry::RebuildNeighbours(CCountry* country)
addresses.comment:
Fills a country's two neighbour sets and the two CCountryList they stand for. It clears both, walks OwnedProvinces marking the owner of every adjacent province that nobody is occupying, then walks ControlledProvinces marking the controller of every adjacent province owned by somebody else. It is what says which set means what.

**Signature**: __stdcall, not __thiscall - the country is [ebp+8], ecx is never read, and the single `ret 4` is the callee cleaning it.

addresses.name: CCountry::LoadOobFile
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCountry::LoadOobFile(CCountry* country)
addresses.comment:
**Reads the order of battle named at `CCountry::oob_file`** and puts it in the country. It builds `<base>/units/<path>` - the base chosen by `[0x1685558 + 0x50]`, which has three values - and tries it with FileExists; then allocates a CParseContext (0x360 bytes) and a Tokenizer (0x114) over the file and calls **the country's own slot 3, `CPersistent::Load`**, with that context, before deleting it.

So **an order of battle is read as a piece of a country's save block**: Load pulls keys and hands each to `CCountry::LoadKey` (`0xCCDA0`), the same one a savegame goes through, and every keyword in the file is a SaveToken - `theatre` 1125, `armygroup` 1126, `corps` 1127, `division` 1128, `navy` 593, `air` 1088, `regiment` 594, `location` 544, `leader` 616, `military_construction` 637. **This is where the units are made.** The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CGoodsPool::ReadSave
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGoodsPool::ReadSave(CGoodsPool* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: Goods pool save reader, slot 4 of CGoodsPool - the LoadKey of the CPersistent family under the name BiceLib gave it. One jump table over seven contiguous token ids, 0x469..0x46F, each case handing the parse context's value token (`parse + 0x228`) to TokenToFixedPoint with the address of the matching field: supplies +8, money +0x10, crude_oil +0x14, fuel +0xC, metal +0x18, energy +0x1C, rare_materials +0x20. **It names every field of the struct and confirms the seven already recorded, with no gaps and nothing left over** - the 0x24 stride is the vftable at +0, the CPersistent meta word at +4 and those seven goods. addresses.name: CCombatant::CCombatant
addresses.signature: CCombatant* __stdcall CCombatant::CCombatant(CCombatant* this@stack:4, bool attacker@stack:8, CCombat* combat@ECX) @EAX
addresses.comment: The base constructor every combatant kind runs. `this` and the attacker flag come on the stack and it cleans them (`ret 8`); the combat comes in ecx and is stored at this+0x3C, which is the back-pointer to the combat. Writes, in order: +0x04 = 0x18D, +0x00 = the CCombatant vftable 0x11C4CA4, four CLists at +0x28, +0x40, +0x54, +0x64 (three words and a byte each), three empty vectors at +0x74, +0x88 and +0x98, +0x84 = 0 (losses), +0xAC = 0 (tactic), +0x50 = 0 (dice), +0x38 = the flag, +0x3C = ecx, byte +0xA8 = 0 (unnamed), and finally +0x08..+0x25 zeroed with three movq, a dword and a word (all unnamed). It then pushes one zero into each of +0x74, +0x88 and +0x98 per entry in g_CSubUnitDataBase's definition vector (count = ([db+0x20]-[db+0x1C])/4), so those three are indexed by subunit type by construction - and it creates g_CSubUnitDataBase inline, with a 511-bucket table, if it is null. Returns this in eax.

addresses.name: CLandCombat::CreateCombatants
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombat::CreateCombatants(CLandCombat* this)
addresses.comment: CCombat slot 6, land. Two `operator new(0xE4)` calls, each followed by CLandCombatant::CLandCombatant (0x168DB0) with the attacker flag in al (1 then 0) and this in ecx; the results go to this+0x10 (attacker) and this+0x14 (defender). A failed allocation stores null and skips the constructor - the only branching in it. It reads nothing at all off the combat: the object is still blank at this point, because both call sites run slot 6 immediately after the constructor and before anything else is set. The SEH frame (state -1/0/1) exists only to destroy the first combatant if the second allocation throws.

addresses.name: CNavalCombat::CreateCombatants
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalCombat::CreateCombatants(CNavalCombat* this)
addresses.comment: CCombat slot 6, naval. Same shape as the land one, but CNavalCombatant has no constructor of its own - it is inlined here: `operator new(0x10BC)`, CCombatant::CCombatant(object, 1 or 0) with this in ecx, then `[object] = 0x11C4D8C` (the CNavalCombatant vftable) and zeroes at +0x10B4 and +0x10B8. So a naval combatant is 0x10BC bytes and adds exactly two words to CCombatant, the first of which is `positioning` (CNavalCombatant::LoadKey at 0x168D80 takes key 0x39B into [ecx+0x10B4] as a %d). addresses.name: CLeader::AddExperience
addresses.signature: void __stdcall AddExperience(CLeader* leader@ESI, int factor@stack:4, int amount@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **Gives a leader experience and promotes him when he has enough.** Does nothing at all while `skill >= 12`; scales the gain by `1 + (max_skill - skill)^2 / 5`, so a leader far below his maximum gains much faster, and divides the result by 3 once he is at or past it; then adds to `current_experience` as a 64-bit pair and compares that pair against `g_LeaderSkillThresholds[skill]` shifted left 15. The promotion is a plain `skill + 1` with an overflow guard.

addresses.name: CLeader::ResetToStarting
addresses.signature: void __cdecl CLeader::ResetToStarting(CLeader* leader@EAX)
addresses.comment:
Puts a leader back to the state he was defined with. The leader arrives in **eax** and costs no stack - a bare `ret` - and nothing comes back.

`rank` (+0x6C) to 0; `skill` (+0x70) to `starting_skill` (+0xC8) but only where that is not negative, so a leader defined with -1 keeps the skill he has; `current_experience` (+0x78, 64 bit) to `starting_experience` (+0xCC) scaled by 32768/1000, computed as `__alldiv(exp << 30, 0x1F40000)` - 2^30 over 1000*32768, which is the same ratio without losing the low bits.

Then a step the earlier note missed: the new experience is **clamped down** to `table[0x170AEE0][skill] << 15`, the experience ceiling for the skill just written, so resetting can lower the experience as well as raise it. Finally, where +0xC4 is non-null it is passed in edi to 0x74140, which walks a list off its +0xC.

One caller: a loop at 0x4D2DE3 over the list at `[ebx+0xE10]`, taking each node's +0 into eax and stepping by +8.

addresses.name: CHistoricalModelSet::MakeSubUnit
addresses.signature: CSubUnit* __stdcall CHistoricalModelSet::MakeSubUnit(CHistoricalModelSet* models)
addresses.comment: **Builds a throwaway regiment to compare models against.** From the set's definition it news a CRegiment, a ship or an air unit by the two flags at `CSubUnitDefinition +0x2C` and `+0x2E`, calls CSubUnit::SetType, then walks the definition's `technologies` vector (`+0x44..+0x48`) and writes each one's researched level - `CTechnologyStatus::level_by_technology[technology->index]` of the country the set's tag names - into the matching node of the new regiment's `technologies` list, and finishes with CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies. Its only caller destroys it immediately. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CHistoricalModelSet::PickCurrentModel
addresses.signature: CHistoricalModel* __cdecl CHistoricalModelSet::PickCurrentModel(CHistoricalModelSet* models@EAX) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The model a country would build right now**: MakeSubUnit for a regiment carrying the country's current research, PickBestModel against it, then the regiment's deleting destructor. Takes its one argument in eax and answers in eax, an LTCG convention. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel
addresses.signature: CHistoricalModel* __stdcall CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel(CHistoricalModelSet* models@ECX, CSubUnit* raised@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Which of a unit type's models a country would build today.** `ret 4`, so it takes **one** stack argument, not two: ecx is the CHistoricalModelSet whose first three words are the model vector, and the stack argument is a CSubUnit whose `technologies` list at `+0x84` says what the country has researched. It scores every model as the sum, over the model's own CSubUnitTechnology entries, of `|the regiment's level - the level the model wants| * 1000`, **counting only technologies whose `CTechnology::change` is set** (789 of 1175 in this mod), and answers the model with the smallest total - starting from 999,999,000, and null for an empty set. **The absolute value is what `Patches::historicalModelLogicFix` replaces**, so that a model asking for more than is researched is penalised rather than treated as equally close. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: Patch_HistoricalModelLogic_1
addresses.comment: **A BiceLib patch site.** `neg ecx` - the absolute value that makes a model wanting more technology than the country has score the same as one wanting less by as much. historicalModelLogicFix writes `jmp +0x2A` here, into the padding after CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel.

addresses.name: Patch_HistoricalModelLogic_2
addresses.comment: **A BiceLib patch site**, six bytes of the padding after CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel: historicalModelLogicFix writes `mov ecx, 0x100000`, the flat penalty a model the country cannot yet field takes.

addresses.name: Patch_HistoricalModelLogic_3

addresses.name: CStrategicRedeploymentOrder::RouteUnit
addresses.signature: bool __cdecl CStrategicRedeploymentOrder::RouteUnit(CStrategicRedeploymentOrder* order@EDI) @AL
addresses.comment:
The body of the order-side re-route. **Not a virtual and not CMoveCommand::RouteUnit's slot-mate**: it is a private helper reached in three places, one of them the `push edi; mov edi,ecx; call` thunk at 0x188440 that occupies CStrategicRedeploymentOrder vftable **slot 13**, where CMoveCommand::RouteUnit is slot 6 of the CCommand hierarchy (and slot 6 is CCommand::Execute). Two different hierarchies, two different slots; what they share is the work, not the dispatch.

The order arrives in edi and costs no stack - a bare `ret` at both exits - and the answer is a bool in al. What it does, in order:

1. Touches `g_CCurrentGameState`, creating it (0xDA8 bytes, CGameState::CGameState then the CCurrentGameState vftable) if it is still null - the singleton accessor inlined.
2. **Gives up early, answering true, when the unit is not due yet**: `if (gamestate[0xBDC] < order->unit->[0xCC]) return true`.
3. **Gives up early, answering true, when the unit is already heading the right way**: where the unit has a path (count at +0x140 > 0), its first province (`g_CMap->[0x2200][ path[0] ]`) is compared against the order's target province at +0xC, and an equal one means there is nothing to redo.
4. Otherwise builds a **CVerySafePathFind** in the frame (vftable 0x15C5B6C written at 0x1887FE) - always that finder, never the plain or merely-safe one CMoveCommand picks between - and calls CPathFind::Find with the unit, the unit's +0x130 and the order's target province.
5. On success calls SetUnitPath(unit, path, 1) and answers true; on failure it destroys the finder and answers **false**, which is the only way this returns false.

So "routing" here is: decide whether the unit still needs a new path, work one out with the most cautious finder, and hand it to the unit.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAirOrder::LoadKey(CAirOrder* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
CAirOrder vftable slot 4, and the image's ordinary LoadKey shape: `this` in ecx, `CParseContext*` at [ebp+8], the four byte SaveToken at [ebp+0xC], every exit `ret 8`.

Three keys of its own. `provinces` (0x1DC) reads the value with `sscanf(parse+0x22C, "%i", &n)`, turns `n` into a CMapProvince* through `g_CCurrentGameState->[0xB8C][n]`, and appends a 16 byte node {province, prev, next, flag} to the list at +0x44/+0x48/+0x4C - so `provinces = N` may be repeated and accumulates. `return_to_base` (0x6DF) is ParseBool into the **base's** +0x18, and `priority` (0x8A) is `sscanf "%i"` into the base's +0x1C; unlike CNavalOrder it does not give those two fields of its own.

Every other key is taken as **a unit type name**: the raw key text at `parse+0x24` is copied into a std::string and looked up with StringHashFind in the database returned by 0x1ADE80, and where that hits, the value is read as `%i` and stored into the int array at +0x34 at that type's index (`type+0x24`). Only a key that is not a unit type either reaches COrder::LoadKey. A failed sscanf calls ReportParseError, so a bad value is reported but the key is not.

The body is slot 4 of CAirOrder and of its thirteen subclasses, which all inherit it.

addresses.name: CPathFind::Find
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CPathFind::Find(CPathFind* finder, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, CList* path)
addresses.comment:
The A* search itself, and **not a member call**: the finder is the first stack argument, not a receiver. The call site at rva 0x1D8F08 pushes five and adds nothing back (the body does `ret 0x14`), and ECX there holds the unit's own province from CUnit +0x130 - so nothing puts the finder in a register.

What it does: refuses unless unit, from and to are all non-null, then asks the finder's slot 1 (MayUse) whether it may run at all. It allocates three arrays the size of the game state's province vector - a visited byte per province, a 16-byte open-list record per province and a came-from index per province - and loops: take the cheapest open province, ask slot 3 (IsGoal), and for each edge of its template (CProvince +0xD4) ask slot 2 (MayStep) and then slot 0 (StepCost). The heuristic added on top is the straight-line distance between the two templates' +0x2C/+0x30 coordinates, wrapped at the map width in CMap +0x2A74 and scaled by [0x1688618]. On success rva 0x1A11F0 fills `path` with 16-byte nodes holding province **ids** (the CList head is first/last/count/flag, the nodes are data/prev/next/flag).

addresses.name: CPathFind::MayUse
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::MayUse(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 1: whether this finder may be used for this unit at all. CPathFind::Find asks it once, before allocating anything, and answers false when it does. `this` is not read - see CPathFind::StepCost for why the convention is still __thiscall - and `ret 0xC` covers the three stack arguments.

False unless the unit's own slot 34 (vftable +0x88) accepts `to`. If the unit's slot 16 (+0x40) then says nothing, true; if it does, the test at rva 0xA7D70 - `to` in ECX, `from` in EAX, `&unit->owner` pushed - has to agree as well.

addresses.name: CPathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::MayStep(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 2: whether `unit` may step from `from` to `to` along `edge`, with `goal` the search's destination (which the base ignores and both safe finders use). `this` is not read; `ret 0x14` covers the five stack arguments.

Refuses when the edge's kind is 3, when `from` is `to`, when `goal`'s template flag +0x13D is clear, and when the helper at rva 0x1A2600 says a kind-1 edge is blocked - that one reads the province the edge crosses (edge +8) and refuses if its controller is hostile or a foreign unit that is not retreating stands in it. Then the two provinces' templates have to agree: the byte at template **+0x22, unnamed**, may not be set on both, and where it is set on one, that template's **+0xA4, unnamed**, must be the other province's id. What follows is the supply gate: with the destination's controller hostile (rva 0x2F1B0) it refuses a unit whose supply_received_percentage is zero and whose CUnit::SupplyConsumption is positive, and likewise fuel_received_percentage against CUnit::FuelConsumption; and last, the unit owner's relation record for `from`'s controller (country +0xE28 indexed by tag id, byte **+0x4C unnamed**) together with **+0x20** on the record for `to`'s controller refuses the step.

addresses.name: CPathFind::StepCost
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CPathFind::StepCost(CPathFind* this, CFixedPoint* out, CProvinceTemplate* from, int edge, CMap* map, CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 0: the cost of stepping out of `from` along its edge number `edge`. **The name is right and the receiver is in ECX.** The body belongs to CPathFind - vtable.py --holding puts it at slot 0 of CPathFind, CSafePathFind, CVerySafePathFind and CPlannedPathFind, which inherit it, while CSafeNavalPathFind overrides it at 0x1A2E00 - and CPathFind::Find loads ECX with the finder at every one of its four dispatch sites (0x1A12E5, 0x1A1390, 0x1A143A, 0x1A145C). The body never reads ECX because these finders are four-byte objects holding nothing but a vftable pointer; that is a `this` that is not needed, not a missing argument. `ret 0x14` accounts for the five stack arguments exactly.

The cost is `from->edges_begin[edge].distance`, in thousandths. Then, if the country controlling `map->provinces[from->edges_begin[edge].to_province]` is hostile to the unit's owner - the tag test at rva 0x2F1B0 - it is scaled by 1100/1000, or by 2000/1000 when that province's intel byte for the owner (CProvince +0x370, bounds-checked against +0x374) is 2 or more **and** units are standing in it (+0x2C0). The two constants are the floats at 0x160A5F0 (1100.5) and 0x160A5F4 (2000.5), truncated to int. Returns `out` in EAX, MSVC's struct return.

addresses.name: CSafePathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CSafePathFind::MayStep(CSafePathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment: CSafePathFind slot 2. Forwards all five arguments unchanged to CPathFind::MayStep (0x5A2AFB-0x5A2B00, no ECX set, callee cleans) and refuses on top of it. Allows the step outright when `to` is the goal - the last step into the destination is exempt. Otherwise it weighs the destination: when the unit's slot 16 or 17 answers true it takes rva 0x1D6900 over `to`'s unit list with the unit's owner tag and multiplies by 1000; when neither does it walks that list itself and adds rva 0x1C3120's value for each unit there whose owner is hostile (rva 0x2F1B0), skipping a `REB` owner when the province's owner tag id (CProvince +0x330) is the unit's own. Either way it refuses when that total is greater than the sum of +0x5C over the unit's own list at CUnit +0xB8.

addresses.name: CVerySafePathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CVerySafePathFind::MayStep(CVerySafePathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment: CVerySafePathFind slot 2, the same shape as CSafePathFind's: forwards all five arguments to CPathFind::MayStep (0x5A2C5B-0x5A2C60), exempts the last step into the goal, and refuses otherwise. It differs in what it does when the unit's slot 16 and slot 17 both say nothing - where the safe one still weighs the units in the destination, this one refuses as soon as the destination's controller is hostile (rva 0x2F1B0) or rva 0xA6010 objects to the province. When either slot does answer it compares rva 0x1D6900 over the destination's unit list (x1000) against the sum of +0x5C over CUnit +0xB8, exactly as the safe one does.

addresses.name: CPlannedPathFind::MayUse
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPlannedPathFind::MayUse(CPlannedPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to)
addresses.comment: CPlannedPathFind slot 1, two instructions: `mov al,1; ret 0xC`. It always allows the finder to run, whatever the unit and the two provinces are, which is what a planning finder wants - the base refuses outright for units whose slot 34 turns the destination down. The body is in CPlannedPathFind's table only, so it is not one the linker folded.

addresses.name: CPlannedPathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPlannedPathFind::MayStep(CPlannedPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment: CPlannedPathFind slot 2, and the only override that does **not** call the base. It keeps the base's first tests and drops everything after them: refuses a kind-3 edge and `from == to`, applies the same template rule (the byte at template +0x22 may not be set on both, and where it is set on one, that template's +0xA4 must be the other province's id), and asks the unit's slot 16 (+0x40), slot 15 (+0x3C) and slot 34 (+0x88, with `to`). No supply, fuel, intel or relation test - a plan is drawn without them.

addresses.name: CSafeNavalPathFind::StepCost
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CSafeNavalPathFind::StepCost(CSafeNavalPathFind* this, CFixedPoint* out, CProvinceTemplate* from, int edge, CMap* map, CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment: CSafeNavalPathFind slot 0: the base cost, then a multiplier for what is on the shore. Forwards all five arguments to CPathFind::StepCost (0x5A2E30-0x5A2E35, no ECX set), then takes the edge's destination `from->edges_begin[edge].to_province`, makes sure the CCurrentGameState exists (creating it if not - 0xDA8 bytes, CGameState::CGameState, vftable 0x15CF674), and walks that province's own template edges. For each neighbour whose controller is hostile to the unit's owner by the relation record at country +0xE28 (+0x20 set), it multiplies the cost by 3000/1000 once if the neighbour's **CProvince +0x300, unnamed** has a level above zero and once if **+0x304, unnamed** does - two specific buildings, which the province's building array at +0x310 would name. The loop stops once both multipliers have been applied, and is skipped entirely when the destination's template flag +0x22 is set. Returns `out` in EAX.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::GetMaxStrength
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CSubUnit::GetMaxStrength(CSubUnit* this, int* out, bool penaltyWhenOwnerAcc, bool penaltyAlways) @EAX
addresses.comment:
Virtual slot 12, `ret 0xC`: `this` in ecx, a hidden return pointer at [ebp+8] and two bool flags at [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10]. The answer is written through the pointer and the pointer comes back in eax, the same shape as CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation next door.

`*out` starts as the definition's `max_strength` (`this->sub_unit_definition_ptr(+0x58)->+0xEC`). Where the subunit's `is_reserve` byte (+0xA4) is clear that value stands. Where it is set, the owner is fetched (0x1ABCF0, subunit -> unit_ptr +0xB0 -> country) and the RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE modifier is applied as `*out = max_strength * (1000 + owner->global_modifier.values->RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE) / 1000` - but only past a gate: `penaltyAlways` ([ebp+0x10]) applies it unconditionally, otherwise owner+0x94 set skips it, otherwise owner+0xACC clear applies it, otherwise `penaltyWhenOwnerAcc` ([ebp+0xC]) decides. Both flags are 0 at the call sites looked at (0x5AC1CD pushes 0 and 0), so the everyday answer is: reserves take the penalty unless the owner's +0x94 says otherwise.

**Which modifier it is, is settled.** `owner->[0xDA8]` is CCountry +0xD90 `global_modifier` plus CModifier +0x18 `values`, so `[edx+0x268]` is entry 0x268/8 = 77 of the values array, and entry 77 is RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE by two independent routes that agree: the live walk of a country's array that named all 143 entries off each entry's CModifierDefinition key, and the global initialiser at rvas 0x56E10..0x59320, whose 77th CModifier is built from the literal MODIFIER_RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE with 77 in edx (reversing/modifierIds.py). What the code does with it agrees with the name: it scales a **reserve** subunit's max strength by (1000 + value)/1000, and nothing else in the function reads it.

Finally `*out` is **floored** at the global at 0x1A8869C - a minimum strength, not a maximum.

**The name is BiceLib's and may sit one class too low**: the body is slot 12 of CSubUnit's own table as well as CRegiment's, CShip's and CWing's, so it is CSubUnit that declares and implements it and the other three inherit. Left as recorded rather than moved, because moving it is a rename and this wave is not one.

addresses.name: CSupply::DailySupplyPass
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSupply::DailySupplyPass(CCurrentGameState* state, int* capacity, int* fuelNeed, int* supplyNeed, int* stepLoss)
addresses.comment:
The daily supply distribution, for Normal (non-arcade) games only: both callers skip it when CCurrentGameState::arcade_mode (+0xC9C) is above zero, the same switch CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel takes its arcade branch on. Five stack arguments, `ret 0x14`, no `this`; the four arrays are one entry per province id, _alloca'd and zeroed by the caller and filled only for provinces whose CProvinceTemplate +0x13D is set - `capacity` from SupplyCapacity (0x9DD00), `supplyNeed` and `fuelNeed` from SupplyNeed (0x9E020), `stepLoss` from SupplyLoss (0x9DE80).

It sweeps CCurrentGameState::provinces_by_supply_order (+0x54) forward to pull supply inwards and backward to push surplus home. Two provinces are on the same network exactly when supply_depot_id (+0x48) matches; the pass only ever compares that field for equality, so it is the network label, and supply_depot_distance (+0x4C) is the hop count, 0 at the depot. A neighbour only counts when it carries the same depot id and is strictly closer.

**Phase 1** (0x2872F0): for every flagged province, swap drawn_ptr with last_drawn_ptr and throughput_ptr with last_throughput_ptr, zero today's drawn and throughput and zero `need`. So last_drawn/last_throughput are yesterday's, which phase 2 reads.

**Phase 2** (0x2874D2), forward: SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS is read once through the inlined GetDefines() as defines->supply(+0x3C)/1000, floored at 1 - 35. A province that is its controller's acting capital (CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation) is skipped but for copying pool into last_pool: the national stockpile is the end of the chain, not a link in it. For every other province: need.supplies = supplyNeed[id] and need.fuel = fuelNeed[id], each raised to 1000 when it is between 0 and 1000 and the matching pool good is under 5000; want = need*35 - pool; local = min(need, current_producing) is added to the unnamed CGoodsPool at CCountry +0xA1C (+0xA24/+0xA28) and subtracted from want; want is floored at 0, capped at need*2 and added to `drawn`. `drawn` then holds this province's own shortfall plus all the demand provinces farther out already pushed on to it. One step's stepLoss[id] is added to the demand carried to the neighbours and taken off again on delivery.

Then three sweeps over the template's ProvinceEdge vector (+0x90..+0x94, stride 20, neighbour id at +4), each considering only same-network, strictly-closer neighbours. (1) Take goods: available = min(neighbour->last_pool, capacity[nid]), scaled by this province's share of yesterday's demand where the neighbour's last_drawn exceeded its last_throughput (congestion rationing, capped at 1), then capped by the neighbour's current pool; the take is added to the neighbour's drawn and throughput, taken off its pool, and `max(take - stepLoss[id], 0)` added to this province's pool - and where the neighbour is a capital, to CCountry::usage. (2) Split what is still wanted evenly over the qualifying neighbours, each share capped by that neighbour's capacity minus its drawn, into its `drawn`. (3) Dump anything still unmet into each closer neighbour's drawn, capped at capacity[nid]. Sweeps 2 and 3 move demand, not goods, which is what the farthest-first sort order is for. Then last_pool = pool, all seven goods.

**Phase 3** (0x287CD3), backward: the controller's acting capital is skipped where its distance is 0, and a province short of what was drawn from it in both supplies and fuel keeps everything. Otherwise surplus = pool - (need*35 + drawn). At a depot (distance 0) the surplus is shipped to the controller's acting capital province, limited by the sum over the province's convoys (CMapProvince +0x38..+0x3C, counting only those that end here and start in the capital's `area`) of NavalBaseCapacity(province) * CConvoy::GetEfficiency / 1000, capped by NavalBaseCapacity itself, and recorded in CCountry::sent_back. Anywhere else the whole surplus goes to the first neighbour found on the same network and closer to the depot, with no capacity limit.

So `drawn` is what was asked of a province today and `throughput` is what actually moved through it, and phase 2 rations next day's takers by exactly that ratio. **No supply is produced here**: current_producing only reduces what has to be fetched, and every increase to a pool is a transfer out of another pool.

addresses.comment: What the GUI calls to issue a move; hardcodes mode68 = 1 and forwards its fourth and fifth arguments as safe and very safe; `ret 0x18`. The unit is the first stack argument (+0x158 gate, virtual +0x8C asked whether the province is reachable); `provinceId` indexes the game state's province vector at +0xB8C; when `recordOnly` is greater than zero it only writes the province to the unit's +0x2CC and returns; the sixth stack dword is never read on any path. **The receiver in ecx is not a CMoveCommand** - it is only ever handed on, as the first argument of 0x49ABD0 (issue a command of type id, 0x18D here or 0x5A4 for the sibling path) and of 0x499E50, which does `add ecx,0x20; call 0x402610`, so the object carries a CCountryTag at +0x20: the per-player interface the order is issued through. Its class was not identified.

addresses.name: CKillLeaderEffect::GetText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CKillLeaderEffect::GetText(CKillLeaderEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString unread, int unknown1, int unknown2)
addresses.comment: **The shape every effect's text builder has**, slot 9: it builds the sentence into `out`, answers it in eax, and takes forty bytes of arguments (`ret 0x28`). Of those the scope is read by 66 of the 99 effect classes that have a slot 9, and the string at `+0x10` by 75 - but only to destroy it, never to read its characters, so `unread` is what it is called here. The last eight bytes are read by none of the 99; they are written out so the stack adds up. This one names the localisation string `KILL_LEADER_EFFECT`, finds the leader in the scope country's active list and puts "\xa7Y<name>\xa7W" in place of its $NAME$. BiceLib stands in for two of its calls to add $UNIT$, $LOCATION$ and $WHERE$ - see Hooks/EffectText/KillLeaderText.cpp.

addresses.name: KillLeaderText_FormatName
addresses.comment: **A BiceLib patch site.** The call that formats the leader's name for $NAME$, and the last instruction that still has the leader in esi - the register is reused two calls later. The stub keeps esi and reproduces the call. Hooks/EffectText/KillLeaderText.cpp.

addresses.comment: Loads the order of battle the effect names: `CStringEffect::text` is written onto the country by CCountry::SetOobFile, and CCountry::LoadOobFile is called on it. addresses.name: CLoadOOBEffect::GetText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CLoadOOBEffect::GetText(CLoadOOBEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString unread, int unknown1, int unknown2)
addresses.comment: **The shape every effect's text builder has**, slot 9: it builds the sentence into `out`, answers it in eax, and takes forty bytes of arguments (`ret 0x28`). addresses.name: CTrigger::GetBlockText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CTrigger::GetBlockText(CTrigger* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, bool redWhen, int depth)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 9, and the whole of how a requirement tooltip is drawn.** One line per child:

    indent(depth) + icon + the child's content

where the icon is `(§R*§W)` or `(§G*§W)` by comparing the child's `Evaluate` against **`redWhen`** - the result that counts as unmet, 0 normally and 1 inside a `not`. The parent indents the line, icon and all.

This base walks the children and calls each child's **GetText** (slot 8) for its one line; a child that is itself a block answers empty there, and the walk falls back to the child's own slot 9. A trigger with no children answers the empty string, which is what makes that fallback work.

**Three BiceLib patches land in its `and` and `or` overrides** - see Hooks/EffectText/TriggerIndentText.hpp.

addresses.name: CNotTrigger::GetBlockText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CNotTrigger::GetBlockText(CNotTrigger* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, bool redWhen, int depth)
addresses.comment: **`not` renders by flipping the polarity and standing aside**: `cmp byte [ebp+0x10], 0 / sete dl` turns `redWhen` into its opposite and hands the same call to `CTrigger::GetBlockText`. So everything under a `not` is drawn green when it is false. That is what proves the third argument is the polarity and not, say, a count.

addresses.name: AndBlockNoHeaderAtTop
addresses.comment: **An `and` at depth 0 draws no header.** `jne` past this and it renders `AND_TRIGGER_STARTS` and its children; fall through and it hands the whole call to `CTrigger::GetBlockText` instead. That is why a technology's `allow`, which is an implicit `and` at the top, lists its conditions without an `All of the below:` above them.

addresses.name: OrBlockOwnIconAtTop
addresses.comment: **An `or` draws an icon for its own header only at depth 0**, where nothing above it has drawn one; `jne` skips it at any other depth. The test reads the same register the header's indent loop counts down, which is why BiceLib's indent patch has to disable that loop rather than zero the register - zeroing it made every nested `or` draw a second asterisk.

addresses.name: AndHeaderIndentLoop
addresses.comment: The `jle` past an `and` header's own indent loop. **A BiceLib patch site**: one byte to `jmp`, because the parent has already indented this line and the header indenting itself again is what pushed the text right of its icon.

addresses.name: OrHeaderIndentLoop
addresses.comment: The same for `or`. **A BiceLib patch site**, one byte to `jmp`.

addresses.name: AndPerChildIndent
addresses.comment: Where an `and` reads its depth as the number of indents to put before each child's line. **A BiceLib patch site**: it wants `depth + 1`, since the children sit *inside* the block, and using the block's own depth left every condition level with its header.

addresses.name: OrPerChildIndent
addresses.comment: The same for `or`. **A BiceLib patch site.**

addresses.name: CWar::AddAttacker
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CWar::AddAttacker(CWar* war, bool arg2, bool arg3, char tag[4], int countryId)
addresses.comment: Adds a country to a war's attackers, the vector at +0x2C. The loader calls it for every `attacker=` line, after refusing a tag the country database does not know. **Everything is on the stack** (`mov esi,[ebp+8]`, `ret 0x14`) and the last two dwords are one `CCountryTag` passed by value - char[4] then id - spelled out as two parameters here so the arithmetic checks: the id at [ebp+0x18] is what the search over the existing 8-byte entries compares, and `lea ecx,[ebp+0x14]; call 0x402610` resolves the pair to a CCountry. The two flags are bytes: [ebp+0x10] (arg3) is cleared when the first existing attacker's country has a zero byte at +0xF34 and, once zero, skips the bulk of the function; [ebp+0xC] (arg2) is tested near the end. What the two mean was not settled - across the call sites arg2 is 1 or 0 and arg3 is 0 or a zeroed register at every one of them.

addresses.name: std::string::operatorPlus
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall std::string::operatorPlus(Hoi3CString* this, Hoi3CString* out@ESI, Hoi3CString* right@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**`std::operator+(const std::string&, const std::string&)`, in its named-return-value form** - previously recorded as `TextBuilder::Append`. There is no TextBuilder: `ecx` is the left-hand string, not a builder object. It calls `std::string::concat` (`0x65CC70`) into a local temporary, tidies `out` (the NRV slot, in esi) to empty and `assignString`s the temporary into it, frees the temporary's heap buffer when its capacity reached 0x10, and answers `out` in eax. `ret 4`.

Call sites chain it exactly the way `a + b + c` compiles: `std::string::operatorPlusChars` produces the first temporary in eax, that becomes this function's `ecx`, and a fresh stack slot is handed in esi for the result (0x40D70E-0x40D726). The `\xa7Y...\xa7W` colour runs the old name described are just one of the things callers happen to concatenate.

addresses.name: std::string::operatorPlusChars
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __cdecl std::string::operatorPlusChars(Hoi3CString* out@ECX, const char* left@EDX, Hoi3CString* right@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**`std::operator+(const char*, const std::string&)`** - previously recorded as `TextBuilder::Begin`. There is no TextBuilder: `ecx` is the string the result is built into (the named-return-value slot), `edx` is the literal on the left, and the string on the right is pushed. It inlines `strlen` on `edx`, builds a local Hoi3CString from it with `std::string::assign` (`0xA160`), calls `std::string::operatorPlus` (`0x65B0D0`) with that temporary as the left operand and `out` still in esi, frees the temporary and answers `out` in eax. **The caller cleans the stack** (bare `ret`, `add esp, 4` at the call site), which is why this is written as cdecl with the registers spelled out rather than as fastcall.

This is the head of every `"literal" + str + ...` chain in the game, including the `"\xa7Y" + name + "\xa7W"` colour runs the old name was taken from and the `"File exception: " + what()` at 0x404723.

addresses.name: CParseContext::FreeMessages
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CParseContext::FreeMessages(CParseContextMessageList* messages)

Walks the message list freeing each node and its two strings, then clears first, last and count. The destructor calls it, and **nothing is logged on the way out** - which is why the mod's `common/` files never produce a line however many unknown keys they carry.

**It has no receiver anywhere.** ECX is dead at entry - the first instruction is `mov eax,[ebp+8]` - and dead at the call: CParseContext::~CParseContext (0x67A630) passes `this+4` on the stack having clobbered ECX in a `free` two instructions earlier, and `ret 4` cleans that one argument. The list itself **is** a CParseContext field: the destructor's argument is `this+4` and the site at 0x67C354 passes `[ebp+8]+4` of a CParseContext it is handed, so the head is messages_first/messages_last/messages_count at CParseContext +4/+8/+0xC. addresses.signature: void __thiscall CReferenceObject::LoadKey(CReferenceObject* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **One key, `id` (token 11)**, read as an object id pair into `this + 8`; everything else goes straight to ReportUnknownKey. Nineteen classes inherit it, CMinister and CRebelFaction among them, which is where their `id_type` at 0x8 and `id` at 0xC come from.

addresses.name: FindPersistentById
addresses.signature: void* __cdecl FindPersistentById(int* keys@EAX, void* table@ECX) @EAX
addresses.comment:
Looks a saved object up by its type and id - the two halves of the `id = { type = N id = N }` pair the save writes. Type 0x25 is a leader: CKillLeaderEffect::GetLeader calls it with that and the id from the event file. The name is BiceLib's.

**It takes both arguments in registers and nothing on the stack.** EAX holds the address of the key pair - two dwords, `{type, id}` - and ECX holds the hash table; the result comes back in EAX and is NULL when nothing matches. All 427 call sites set EAX with a `lea` of a stack local in the instruction immediately before the call and push nothing at all, and none of them cleans any stack afterwards.

The body: `edi = [eax]` (type), `esi = [eax+4]` (id), hashes `(type << 16) + id` by dividing it by `[ecx+4]` (the bucket count) and indexes `[ecx+8]` (the bucket array) with the remainder, then walks the chain - `[node]` is the stored pointer, `[node+4]` the next node - comparing `[stored+8]` against the type and `[stored+0xC]` against the id. So the registered object keeps its own copy of the key pair at +8/+0xC, which is where CReferenceObject's unread +0x8 and +0xC most likely go - that last step is inference, not something checked.

The table is one of two globals, `[0x1A857F4]` and `[0x1A857F0]`, and 374 of the 427 sites choose between them with `cmp <type>, 0x1268` immediately before - so the type space is split into two registries at 4712. 132 of the 427 sites follow the call with `add eax, -8` before using the result; what that adjustment reaches has not been settled here.
