addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 6 of them, one case each: `color`, `color_override`, `colorcodes`, `effect`, `fontName`, `name`. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: DestroyStringsInRange
addresses.signature: void __cdecl DestroyStringsInRange(void* first@EAX, void* last@EDI)
addresses.comment:
**Empties the string at the start of every record in a range**, walking `[first, last)` in steps of **0x20** and giving each string's buffer back where it had one - `if (capacity >= 0x10) free(data)`, then capacity 0xF, length 0, first byte 0. Both ends arrive in registers, first in eax and last in edi. `ret`.

It is a destructor loop the compiler wrote once and **1552 call sites share**: every record type of 0x20 bytes that begins with a string folds onto this one body, which is why its callers have nothing to do with each other. The stride is baked in, so it is only correct for that shape.

BiceLib meets it tearing a text object down: after ReleaseTextReplacements has destroyed the object each replacement points at, this empties the name each one carries, and the caller frees the block. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: LogSink::Write
addresses.signature: void __thiscall LogSink::Write(LogSink* this, int channel, Hoi3CString* file, int line, Hoi3CString* message)
addresses.comment: **Where every message in the game arrives.** The record's destructor pulls the four apart and calls this through the sink's vftable slot 1. It opens with a filter of its own - `call 0x40C3C0` on a global at `0x16052F0`, taking the message and dropping it when that answers true - and only then picks a file by channel. **Measured, 2026-09-20**, by catching a whole startup: `3` writes to `system.log`, `0x10000` to `setup.log`, `0x10002` to `game.log`, `0x10006` to `time.log`, and every channel the run produced reached a file. `0x10004`, which carries the three `Unknown History Command` sites, was never produced at all. **Hooked once, on 2026-09-20**, with a five byte jump over the prologue (`55 8B EC 6A FF`) - ahead of the filter, so every message built was seen. That capture matched `setup.log` and `game.log` line for line, which is how the filter was shown to drop nothing, and the hook was then removed as redundant. `ret 0x10`.

addresses.name: free
addresses.signature: void __cdecl free(void* block)
addresses.comment: A thunk to the CRT's free. Every string destructor in the executable calls it the same way - `if (capacity > 15) free(pointer)` - which is what BiceLib copies to give back a string the game allocated for it.

addresses.name: operator_new
addresses.signature: void* __cdecl operator_new(unsigned int size)
addresses.comment:
**`operator new`, and so every allocation the game's own code makes.** Ghidra calls it `FUN_00b9602f`, and it is the function behind a `push <size>` / `call` pair - `push 0xB0` before a log record, `push 0x57C` before a country database. The size is the object's, which makes a call site worth reading: it is how big the thing about to be built is.

The standard MSVC body, a retry loop: call `malloc` (`0x796CC3`); on success return it; on failure call `_callnewh` (`0x79F4F7`) to give the new handler a chance to free something and try again; when the handler answers 0, **throw `std::bad_alloc`** - its vftable is `0x119FCE8` - through `_CxxThrowException` (`0x79894B`). So it never returns null.

The `mov edi, edi` it opens with is the two byte hot patch pad, which is why the body starts at `+2`.

addresses.name: _purecall
addresses.signature: void __cdecl _purecall(void)
addresses.comment:
The CRT stub a class's own vftable holds for a method it leaves pure virtual - COrder's slot 16, the order type id, among many. It calls the installed _purecall_handler if there is one and otherwise ends the process through _amsg_exit(_RT_PUREVIRT), the R6025 "pure virtual function call" message, so reaching it is fatal. Nothing reaches it in a working game: every concrete class fills the slot. Three Lua registrations resolve here - CCommand::IsValid, CDiplomaticAction::IsValid and CDiplomaticAction::GetAIAcceptance - because those methods are pure virtual in the class that declares them; the findings used to name this address after them (Shared_GetAIAcceptance_IsValid) and no longer do.

**Read out in full**, because it is where a crash can be caught: `push [__pPurecall]` (`0x134D238`, kept encoded), `call [DecodePointer]`, `test eax,eax`, `je` past it, `call eax` with no arguments - and then `push 0x19`, **25 = `_RT_PUREVIRT`**, which is what identifies this function rather than one of the other handler wrappers in this CRT that also decode a pointer and call it.

**510 slots in the data sections hold this address and nothing calls it directly.** The game installs no handler, so reaching it is fatal as the comment above says; BiceLib installs one and saves the game before it goes - GameState/PureCall.cpp and reversing/FINDINGS-allocator.md.

addresses.name: malloc
addresses.signature: void* __cdecl malloc(unsigned int size)
addresses.comment: The CRT's `malloc`, and the only thing `operator_new` calls to get memory. Rejects a size above `_HEAP_MAXREQ` (`cmp ebx, -0x20`, so anything over `0xFFFFFFE0`), rounds a zero request up to one byte, and hands the rest to **`HeapAlloc(_crtheap, 0, size)`** - the heap handle is the global at `0x134D240`, created on first use. Answers 0 when the heap does; `operator_new` is what turns that into a throw.

addresses.name: _callnewh
addresses.signature: int __cdecl _callnewh(unsigned int size)
addresses.comment: Calls the installed **new handler** and says whether to try allocating again: 1 when the handler ran and returned non-zero, 0 otherwise. The handler is kept encoded at `0x134CC04` and put back with `DecodePointer`, so it cannot be read straight out of memory. The game installs none that has been found, which means the first failed allocation throws.

addresses.name: _CxxThrowException
addresses.signature: void __stdcall _CxxThrowException(void* object, void* throwInfo)
addresses.comment: The CRT's throw. Takes the exception object by address and a `_ThrowInfo` describing its type, and does not return - every caller has an `int3` after it. Reached from `operator_new` with a `std::bad_alloc`.

addresses.name: Return_1
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 1; ret` - the whole body, so the linker folded it and this one address fills a virtual table slot in several classes that have nothing to do with each other. It is slot 11 of CLandCombat, where it answers the combat kind 1, and that is written on CLandCombat's own slot rather than on the address.

addresses.name: Return_2
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 2; ret` - the whole body, so the linker folded it and this one address fills a virtual table slot in several classes that have nothing to do with each other. It is slot 11 of CNavalCombat, where it answers the combat kind 2, and that is written on CNavalCombat's own slot rather than on the address.

addresses.comment: A define, 10 - the floor of the float 10.5, taken at startup. Thousandths, so 0.010. Ten places read it and they do not agree on a purpose, so the name only says what it holds. addresses.name: set_purecall_handler_encoded
addresses.signature: void __cdecl set_purecall_handler_encoded(void* encodedHandler)
addresses.comment:
Stores its argument into `__pPurecall` (`0x134D238`) **without encoding it**, so it is the inner half of `_set_purecall_handler` and whatever calls it has to call `EncodePointer` first. The CRT startup at `0x79845B` is its only caller in the executable, and it passes an encoded null.

Named for what it does rather than `_set_purecall_handler`, because the function of that name in the CRT is the one that does the encoding.

addresses.name: __pPurecall
addresses.comment:
The pure virtual call handler, kept **encoded** with `EncodePointer` - so it cannot be read out of memory as a pointer, and a decode of null is what says none is installed.

Read only by `_purecall` (`0x7961D5`). Written only by the raw setter at `0x79F96E`, which has no caller, and by the CRT startup at `0x79845B` that encodes a null into this and four other handler globals. So it is empty in the game as shipped, and BiceLib is free to take it.

addresses.name: CAndTrigger::GetBlockText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CAndTrigger::GetBlockText(CAndTrigger* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, bool redWhen, int depth)
addresses.comment:
Slot 9 of the trigger vftable. One line per child - `indent(depth) + icon + the child's content` - where the icon is a red or green asterisk by whether the child evaluates to `redWhen`. **The parent indents the line, icon and all**, which is why a child that indents itself again comes out adrift.

**The root of a technology's requirements**: an `allow` block is an implicit `and`, so this is the call that has the whole finished tree in hand. Four BiceLib patches land in it - its header indent, its per-child indent, the depth it gives a block child, and its exit.

addresses.name: COrTrigger::GetBlockText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall COrTrigger::GetBlockText(COrTrigger* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, bool redWhen, int depth)
addresses.comment:
Slot 9 of the trigger vftable. One line per child - `indent(depth) + icon + the child's content` - where the icon is a red or green asterisk by whether the child evaluates to `redWhen`. **The parent indents the line, icon and all**, which is why a child that indents itself again comes out adrift.

Unlike the `and`, an `or` draws an icon for its own header when nothing above it has - which is why its header indent is skipped with a jump rather than by zeroing the depth the test reads.

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::GetBlockText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CContextTrigger::GetBlockText(CContextTrigger* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, bool redWhen, int depth)
addresses.comment:
The renderer behind **a plain country tag, `controller = { ... }` and `owner = { ... }`** - a scope that hands its conditions a real country to be evaluated against.

That is what makes it the exception among the scopes: BiceLib negates the depth it passes down (`0x5D20A1`), which is the engine's own way of saying "indent this, and still colour the conditions". The iterating scopes cannot have that - their conditions are about a province while the scope passes the country, so an asterisk there would always be red.

addresses.name: CAnyOwnedProvinceTrigger::GetBlockText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CAnyOwnedProvinceTrigger::GetBlockText(CAnyOwnedProvinceTrigger* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, bool redWhen, int depth)
addresses.comment: Its own indent loop, at the top of the renderer and before a word of its own text - so it indents a line its parent has already placed, and the text ends up adrift of its own asterisk. **BiceLib turns the `jle` that guards it into an unconditional `jmp`**, which skips the loop and leaves the depth register for the icon test that reads it next.

addresses.name: CAndTrigger::GetText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall GetText(CTrigger* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, int unknown1, int unknown2)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 8 for every container and every scope**: `CAndTrigger` declares it and `COrTrigger`, `CNotTrigger` and all six scope triggers inherit it, because they all derive from `CAndTrigger`. It answers the empty string.

That empty answer is the whole mechanism behind how a tree is walked: a parent asks each child for its one line here, and a child with no line of its own says nothing, which is what sends the parent to the child's block renderer at slot 9 instead.

`CTrigger`'s own slot 8 is `_purecall` (`0x7961D5`), so GetText is pure virtual on the base and this is the first real implementation.

addresses.name: BaseBlockChildBranch
addresses.comment:
`je` past the leaf line to the block path, inside `CTrigger::GetBlockText`. The block path draws **neither indent nor icon** - it goes straight to the child's own slot 9 - which is why a nested `and` or `or` inside a scope used to come out with no asterisk at all.

**BiceLib retargets this branch** (the condition is kept, only the destination changes) to a stub that draws the indent and the asterisk for a block child and then rejoins at `0x5D05DA`.

addresses.name: AndBlockChildDepth
addresses.comment: What an `and` passes as the depth when a child is itself a block. The game sends a constant, so a block inside a block restarted at the same level; BiceLib sends the `and`'s own depth plus one.

addresses.name: OrBlockChildDepth
addresses.comment: The same for an `or`, which sends its own constant - 1 rather than the `and`'s 0, which is why the two containers drifted differently.

addresses.name: ContextTriggerChildDepth
addresses.comment: Where `CContextTrigger` hands its conditions their depth: `inc ecx`, so `depth + 1`. **BiceLib makes it `not ecx`**, which is `-(depth + 1)` exactly - the same number, carrying the engine's own flag for "and these conditions can be coloured". The sign is read at the top of `CTrigger::GetBlockText`, which negates it back and remembers that it did.

addresses.name: NotTriggerEpilogue
addresses.comment:
The epilogue of `CNotTrigger::GetBlockText`, which BiceLib replaces whole.

A `not` flips `redWhen` and forwards to the base **with the depth unchanged**, so the base indents the condition inside it a second time - into the middle of a line the parent has already placed. No depth fixes that: the base draws the icon when the depth is 0 or arrived negative and the indent whenever it is above 0, so "neither" is not a value it can be given. The stub takes the leading indent off the finished text instead.

addresses.name: AndTriggerExit
addresses.comment:
`mov ecx, [esp + 0xE4]`, the last instruction of `CAndTrigger::GetBlockText` before its epilogue, and the point every path through the function converges on - two branches inside it land exactly here.

**BiceLib stands here to scroll a requirement tooltip too tall for the screen**: the finished text is in `esi` and the frame is still up, so lines can be taken off the front before the tooltip sees it. One instruction before the epilogue rather than over it, because the epilogue writes `fs:[0]` and reproducing that from inline assembly is a warning and a SAFESEH question nobody needs.

addresses.name: TriggerIndentUnit
addresses.comment: **Three spaces, and the whole of how a requirement tree is indented.** Every indent loop in every trigger renderer pushes this and 3 and appends it once per level, which is what makes the loops findable: scanning for this address is how the six scope triggers that indent themselves were found rather than guessed at.

addresses.name: CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute(CDistributeReinforcement* this, CFixedPoint* result@stack:4, __int64 available@stack:8, bool flag@stack:16)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 0 of its virtual table, and where the manpower tooltip's two numbers come from.** The class derives from `CDistributionSetting`, so this is the reinforcement slider spending what it has been allocated; every sibling distributor - supply, upgrade, production, research, consumer goods, lend lease, NCO, diplomacy, espionage - has its own body at the same slot.

It zeroes `CCountry +0xA98`, `+0xA9C` and `+0xAA0`, then walks the country's units and every subunit under each, and rebuilds all three from nothing. `this + 0x18` is the country throughout.

**The stack arguments are three, not one**, which is why the recorded signature wanted ret 4 and the function does ret 16: a hidden return pointer at [ebp+8] for the eight-byte fixed point it answers, the amount it has been given as a 64-bit `fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>` split across [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10], and a byte flag at [ebp+0x14]. This body ignores the flag; the consumer-goods (0x118C50) and production (0x119D10) bodies read it and skip their last step when it is set. `__int64` is written for the middle argument only so the arithmetic sizes - it is the same fixed point type as the return.

addresses.name: ReinforcementCountersCleared
addresses.comment:
The last of the three counters the pass clears before it walks anything, with `edi` zero and `esi` the country.

**BiceLib stands here to start its own day**: the split it keeps has to begin and end with the game's, or the parts would not add up to the total printed beside them. It is also the only thing in the game that happens once a day per country and that BiceLib stands on, so a day of troop rotation is closed here too.

addresses.name: ReinforcementManpowerUsedAdded
addresses.comment: `country->reinforcement_manpower_used += used`, which the tooltip prints as `$USED$`. The same value has just been taken off the country's manpower pool at `0x11C5C7`.

addresses.name: ReinforcementManpowerNeededAdded
addresses.comment:
`country->reinforcement_manpower_needed += need`, which the tooltip prints as `$NEED$`. `eax` is the country and `ecx` is what this one subunit's missing strength is worth.

**Which subunit that is, is still at `[esp + 0x44]`** - written at `0x11BF98` and read back as late as `0x11C43D`, with the stack unmoved, and the very next instruction reads `[esp + 0x48]` for the loop's own next node. That is what lets one hook here split the total into land, air and naval by the subunit's class.

addresses.name: CUnit::UpdateDaily
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::UpdateDaily(CUnit* this)
addresses.comment:
**`CUnit`'s virtual slot 32, the per-unit update.** `CArmy` and `CNavy` share it; `CAir` overrides it with `0x1D0B60`, and nothing else derives from `CUnit`.

It ages the timed entries at `this + 0x2A8`, asks the order two questions, digs in and rotates troops (land only), and then tidies three vectors.

**The name claims a period, and that part is inference.** What the code shows is the work: troop rotation here divides a thousandth-scaled annual rate by 365000 and applies it once a call, and dig-in advances by exactly one level a call. Both only make sense once a day. The caller would settle it and was not found - the slot is reached through a virtual table, and `+0x80` is 150 call sites in 119 functions, none of the three that also walk units being this one. So `Update` rather than `Daily` is the part to rely on.

addresses.name: CAir::UpdateDaily
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAir::UpdateDaily(CAir* this)
addresses.comment:
`CAir`'s own slot 32. **It does not replace `CUnit::UpdateDaily` - it ends by calling it**, on every path, after its own air-specific work.

So an air unit does reach the troop rotation code, and what stops it there is the `IsLand` test at the top, the same thing that stops a navy. That test is the single gate; no class avoids rotation by not running the function.

The period in the name is inferred, the same way and on the same evidence as `CUnit::UpdateDaily`.

addresses.name: UpdateDailyLandOnly
addresses.comment: `if (!this->IsLand()) ...` - slot 15, and **the whole of the gate on troop rotation**. All three unit classes arrive here: a navy shares this function, and `CAir::UpdateDaily` ends by calling it. So rotation is an army's alone, and so is the manpower it costs.

addresses.name: DigInRequiresWar
addresses.comment:
`if (!owner->isAtWar) goto 0x1BB146` - and `0x1BB146` is **the rotation code**, not the end of it.

**This test belongs to digging in, not to rotation**, which is the trap in this function: the name `peacetime_manpower_rotation` invites the opposite reading. The flow graph settles it - `0x1BB146` has seven incoming edges, six of them branches taken to skip the dig-in block - and the decompiler agrees, putting the whole of that block in one nested `if` whose body is `dig_in_level += 1000`.

addresses.name: PeacetimeManpowerRotationRead
addresses.comment:
**The only read of `peacetime_manpower_rotation` in the executable.** Checked by pairing all 153 fetches of a country's modifier array with a read of entry 50 within the next 0x200 bytes.

It is scaled up at `0x1BB184` where the unit is under-supplied, by `PEACETIME_MANPOWER_ROTATION_LOW_SUPPLY_FACTOR`, and then divided by 365000 per subunit - a thousandth-scaled annual rate applied daily.

addresses.name: RotationStrengthStored
addresses.comment:
Where rotation writes the reduced strength back. **The drain worked out above is clamped to nothing below zero and to the maximum above it**, so what actually went is `[edi + 0x5C]` before this instruction less `ebx` after it - which is where BiceLib stands, rather than on the figure the arithmetic produced.

`edi` is the subunit and `esi` is still the unit. The `jns` two instructions above lands on the first byte of this, so a jump written here is still what that branch arrives at.

addresses.name: GetManpowerDetailsText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __cdecl GetManpowerDetailsText(Hoi3CString* out, CCountryTag* tag)
addresses.comment:
**The only reference to `MANPOWER_DETAILS_IRO` in the image.** It reads the country's `+0xA9C` and `+0xAA0`, formats each with `FormatFixedPoint`, and replaces `$NEED$` and `$USED$`.

**The whole of it exists twice**, once at two decimals and once at one, chosen at `0x2D0639` by whether the need reaches 10000. It goes on to build `MANPOWER_DETAILS_DRO` in a second string.

addresses.name: ManpowerDetailsBuilt
addresses.comment:
The first call after both halves of the tooltip converge, and so the one point where the sentence is finished and nothing has been done to it yet. The frame still holds it at `[ebp - 0x80]` and the country at `[ebp - 0x4C]`.

**BiceLib stands here** to add `$LAND$`, `$AIR$`, `$NAVY$`, `$ROTATION$` and `$ROTATIONCOST$` beside the game's own two.

addresses.name: FormatFixedPoint
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall FormatFixedPoint(Hoi3CString* out, int value, int decimals)
addresses.comment:
**A CFixedPoint as text**: the value over a thousand, with as many decimal places as asked for, truncated rather than rounded and with no thousands separator. It constructs into the string it is given, so that one has to be empty.

What the whole interface formats its numbers with, and what BiceLib calls so its own figures read like the game's.

addresses.name: ApplyAttrition
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall ApplyAttrition(CUnit* unit, int* strengthLost)
addresses.comment:
**What attrition takes off a unit, once a day.** `CUnit::UpdateDaily` calls it.

Per subunit: the province's own `attrition` modifier, scaled by a global and by the subunit's maximum strength, over 30000 - a monthly rate applied daily. The strength lost is totalled into the second argument, which is also what it answers.

Two gates, both at the top and both the same ones rotation has: `combats.count` must be below 1, and the unit must answer `IsLand`. So attrition here is an army standing still out of combat, and neither fleets nor air commands take it.

addresses.name: AttritionStrengthStored
addresses.comment:
Where attrition writes the reduced strength back - **the same shape as rotation's store at `0x1BB25D`**, down to the clamp above it and the ceiling raised after, because both are a subunit losing strength.

`esi` is the subunit and `edi` what its strength is about to become, so what actually went is `[esi + 0x5C]` before this instruction less `edi` after. **The unit is not in a register**: `edi` held it at the top of the function and has been reused, so it comes off the frame at `[ebp + 8]`.

**BiceLib stands here** to price the loss in manpower and total it per country.

addresses.name: AddCasualtyTrickleback
addresses.comment:
**What comes back to the manpower pool from casualties.** The only reader of the `casualty_trickleback` modifier in the executable, at `0x1C3FB6`.

    manpower = casualties x build_cost_manpower / max_strength
             x (trickleback + a technology bonus) / 100000

The first half is the same pricing the reinforcement pass uses, so a casualty is valued at what replacing it costs, and the modifier decides how much of that returns. It credits the **expeditionary owner** where there is one (`+0x28C`) and the owner otherwise.

**No signature recorded**: the compiler gave it a register convention, taking the unit in `eax` and the casualties on the stack, so it cannot be written as an ordinary function - the same reason `CCountry::IsEnemy`'s second overload has none.

addresses.name: TricklebackCredited
addresses.comment: `country->Manpower += trickled back`, floored at zero by the two instructions after it, and the one write in the whole function. `esi` is the country and `eax` the manpower, **already in the units the tooltip prints** - nothing to price here, unlike attrition and rotation.\n\n**BiceLib stands here** to total what comes back per country.

addresses.name: CheckTransportOverload
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CheckTransportOverload(CNavy* fleet)
addresses.comment:
**Whether a fleet is carrying more than it can.** The last thing `CUnit::UpdateDaily` does, for naval units only - it downcasts through slot 11 and calls this.\n\n    carried = sum of transport_weight over fleet->carrying\n    if (carried > fleet->definition->transport_capacity / 1000) ...\n\nBoth halves are read off `CSubUnitDefinition`: `weight` at `+0x10C`, which the unit files call `transport_weight`, and `transport_capacity` at `+0x144`.\n\n**It throws cargo overboard until the load fits**, re-measuring each time round:

    do
        for each unit in fleet->carrying
            if (its province's info byte +0x22 is set)
                RemoveFromTransport(...); unit->EnterProvince(province)
            else
                RemoveRegimentFromUnit(its first regiment); delete it
                if that was its last, post {unit->type, unit->id} to the game
                    state's message ring at +0xBF8
    while (carried weight > capacity)

So a unit that **can** be put ashore is put ashore, and one that cannot is taken apart a regiment at a time. Which is which turns on a byte of the province's info object at `+0x22` - 246 places in the image read it, so it is something fundamental, but nothing here says which way round it means land.

addresses.name: SumTransportWeight
addresses.comment: Adds up `CSubUnitDefinition::weight / 1000` over a `CList<CUnit*>`, which is what a fleet's load is measured in.\n\n**No signature recorded**: the compiler passed the list in `eax` - the caller does `add eax, 0x2E4` on the fleet and calls straight in - so it cannot be written as an ordinary function.

addresses.name: DailyTickEndGate
addresses.comment: `cmp byte ptr [gamestate + 0xDA4], 0` - the gate on the last block of `CUnit::UpdateDaily`, which is attrition and, for a fleet, the transport overload check.\n\n**What the byte means is not known, and it matters.** It is zeroed when the game state is constructed, and `ApplyAttrition` has **exactly one caller** - the call this gates. So if nothing ever sets this byte, that attrition function never runs at all. Nothing that sets it was found, but the search is not conclusive: `+0xDA4` is a common displacement and the global is loaded in thousands of places, so the scan cannot be made clean. **It is settled in a game rather than here** - watch whether BiceLib's `$ATTRITION$` ever leaves zero. Sizing `CCurrentGameState` to its real `0xDA8` is what makes it read as `+0xDA4` at all - the structure used to end at `0xD9E`, so this came out as an index past the end of it.

addresses.name: RemoveRegimentFromUnit
addresses.comment: **Takes a regiment out of its unit.** It walks the unit's `regiments` for the node holding this one and unlinks it, then sets the regiment's `unit_ptr` (`+0xB0`) to zero - which is what says so rather than any guess. The caller deletes the regiment afterwards.\n\n**No signature recorded**: the compiler passed the unit in `edi` and the regiment on the stack.

addresses.name: RemoveFromTransport
addresses.comment: Takes a unit off whatever is carrying it: it writes `CUnit::carrying` (`+0x2E4`) at `0x1CF19F`, which is the fleet's list of passengers.\n\nCalled by `CheckTransportOverload` together with `CUnit::EnterProvince`, which is the pair that puts a unit ashore. Only the one write was read; the rest of the function was not.

addresses.name: CUnit::EnterProvince
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::EnterProvince(CUnit* this, CMapProvince* province)
addresses.comment: Puts a unit into a province: it writes `current_province_ptr` (`+0x130`) at `0x1BF4D3`.\n\n**Only that much was read.** The function is over 2.5KB and does a great deal besides - it reads the province's path node in half a dozen places - so the name is what it is *for* at the one call site traced here, not a full account of it. The convention is read off that call site: `ecx` is the unit and the province is pushed.

addresses.name: GetProvinceAttrition
addresses.comment:
**The only reader of the `attrition` modifier off a province's own modifier** (`[province + 0xFC + 0x18]`, entry 7, read at `0xA09CD`). `ApplyAttrition` calls it once per subunit at `0x1C75AE` and scales the result by a global and by the subunit's maximum strength.

Three callers in all: `0xA19BF`, `0x1C75AE` and `0x3593E3`.

**No signature recorded** - what it takes beyond the province, and how, was not read.

addresses.name: __alldiv
addresses.signature: __int64 __stdcall __alldiv(__int64 dividend, __int64 divisor)
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT signed 64-bit divide (lldiv.asm). Dividend at [esp+4..0xB], divisor at [esp+0xC..0x13]; result in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). Truncates toward zero, NOT floor: it takes the absolute value of both operands, divides unsigned, and negates the quotient only if exactly one operand was negative (edi counts the negations at 0xB9998D and 0xB999A9, and 0xB99A1A negates when edi==1). 2032 direct call sites. This is the helper every 'x * 1000 / y' in the game goes through - the thousandths fixed point multiplies into a 64-bit intermediate to avoid overflow and then divides here.

addresses.name: __allmul
addresses.signature: __int64 __stdcall __allmul(__int64 a, __int64 b)
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT 64-bit multiply (llmul.asm). a at [esp+4..0xB], b at [esp+0xC..0x13]; result in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). Sign-agnostic: the low 64 bits of the product are the same for signed and unsigned operands, so MSVC emits this one body for both, and the sign lives at the CALL SITE - a 'cdq' before the push means the 32-bit operand was signed, a 'xor edx,edx' means it was not. Fast path when both high words are zero (0xB99B00, a single mul), otherwise the three partial products AHI*BLO + ALO*BHI + ALO*BLO. 1144 direct call sites.

addresses.name: EnterGame_SetInGame
addresses.comment:
**The only instruction in the executable that writes `CCurrentGameState +0xDA4` a nonzero value**: `mov byte ptr [ecx + 0xDA4], 1`, with `ecx` loaded from `g_CCurrentGameState` two instructions earlier.

It sits near the end of `CInGameIdler::Enter` (`0x25A2B0`), after the session has been built - the log lines above it are `Countries initialized<`, `provinces initialised<`, `information caches setup<`, `supply logic defined<`, ` processed weather <`, ` processed intel setup <` - and before the in-game GUI is built (`menubar`, `chat_list`, `mapmode_1`..`mapmode_10`).

Unconditional on its path: the block at `0x25D120` is the join of the inlined get-or-create of the game state, entered from `0x25D082(taken)`, `0x25D114(taken)` and `0x25D11E(flow)`, and the block above it at `0x25D075` is reached from all three arms of the camera setup. **So the attrition gate opens in every game**, which is what the live tooltip measurement already showed.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::Enter
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CInGameIdler::Enter(void)
addresses.comment:
Slot 3 of `CInGameIdler`'s virtual table, and the whole of entering a running game: it looks up the `unitlist_start` / `unitlist_offset` gui types (`Missing unitlist_start or unitlist_offset gui type.`), runs `LOAD_GFX`, `LOAD_EVENTS` and `ADAPTING_HISTORY`, logs the six `eu3idler.cpp` setup stages, **sets `gamestate->in_game` at `0x25D126`**, then builds the in-game interface.

`CFrontEnd` overrides the same slot at `0x2EEF00`, where it logs `entering frontend...` and **clears** the same byte at `0x2EFE58` - which is what makes slot 3 the screen's enter hook rather than anything more specific.

Spans `0x25A2B0`..`0x261BB8`, about 0x7900 bytes, which is why `image.functionStart`'s default 0x2500 limit reports `?` for the write inside it.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::Leave
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CInGameIdler::Leave(void)
addresses.comment: Slot 4 of `CInGameIdler`'s virtual table, the counterpart to slot 3: it frees the idler's lists and then **clears `gamestate->in_game` at `0x262337`**. `CFrontEnd` overrides the same slot at `0x2F0140`.

addresses.name: LeaveGame_ClearInGame
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [eax + 0xDA4], 0` in `CInGameIdler::Leave`, with `eax` the game state just stored back into `g_CCurrentGameState` at `0x262325`. The counterpart to `EnterGame_SetInGame`.

addresses.name: FrontEnd_Enter_ClearInGame
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [eax + 0xDA4], bl` in `CFrontEnd`'s slot 3 (`0x2EEF00`, the function that logs `entering frontend...`), with `eax` the game state stored into `g_CCurrentGameState` at `0x2EFE40`. Returning to the main menu closes the gate again.

addresses.name: ParseObjectReference
addresses.signature: void __cdecl ParseObjectReference(CParseContext* parse@ECX, void* reference@ESI)
addresses.comment: **Reads the `{ type = N id = N }` block a save writes for an object reference into the 0x28-byte reference a command keeps.** It calls `ParseObjectId` (0x67B250) for the pair and then fills the reference: `+0` the cached object pointer, set to 0 because the block names no object yet; `+4` type; `+8` id; `+0xC` an `Hoi3CString` assigned from the parse context's own name at `+0x32C`. It takes no stack argument - the parse context arrives in ECX and the reference in ESI (`mov ecx,[ebp+8]` and `lea esi,[this+0x3C]` at the call site, a bare `ret` here), the same register-argument style as the rest of the loader primitives. 61 call sites, every one of them a command's `LoadKey` case for a key whose value is an object: `unit` is token 0x256 and `parent` 0x84, and a command keeps one such reference per key at `+0x3C`, `+0x64` and so on, 0x28 apart. **It stores nothing when the parse context's error handler at `+0x35C` has latched** - handler non-null and both its bytes at `+4` and `+5` set jumps straight to the epilogue and leaves the reference as it was, although `ParseObjectId` has already consumed the tokens. The mirror image is the command's `SaveContents`, e.g. `CMoveCommand`'s at 0x1D9160: `SaveWriteKey(0x256)` then the pair out of `+0x40` and `+0x44` - the string at `+0x4C` is never written to the save. The same reference is built from a live object by 0x2DD70 (unnamed): type from `CUnit +0x10`, id from `+0x14`, the string from the object's `+0x1C`, and the object pointer cached at `+0`.

addresses.name: sscanf
addresses.signature: int __cdecl sscanf(const char* buffer, const char* format, ...)
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT `sscanf`, statically linked. The body is only the public wrapper: it loads the buffer into esi and calls the file-scope helper at 0x796466 with (INPUTFN=_input_l 0x7A1379, format, locale=NULL, va_list=&arg3), which builds a FILE on its own stack over the string (_flag=0x49 = _IOREAD|_IOMYBUF|_IOSTRG, _ptr=_base=buffer, _cnt=min(strlen(buffer), INT_MAX)) and runs the scan engine over it. **This is the single most-called unnamed function in the image, 168 direct call sites**, and it is how every loader turns a lexed token into a number: 152 of those sites push exactly three arguments and clean 0xc, with the middle one a literal format - `%i` 102 times, `%f` 28, `%u` 18, `%c` 8, and one each of `%x`, `%lld` and `%d.%d.%d.%d` - and the return is tested against zero, which is sscanf's count of fields assigned. The string argument is almost always `parse + 0x22C`, the lexer's current token text.

addresses.name: v_sscanf_l
addresses.comment: The static helper behind sscanf, CRT source `v_sscanf_l`. Rejects a null string or a null format with errno=EINVAL (0x16) and _invalid_parameter_noinfo, then fakes a FILE on its stack over the string - _flag 0x49, _ptr=_base=string, _cnt=min(strlen(string), INT_MAX) - and tail-calls the INPUTFN it was handed. Exactly one caller, sscanf at 0x7964D4.

addresses.name: _input_l
addresses.signature: int __cdecl _input_l(FILE* stream, const char* format, _locale_t locale, va_list arglist)
addresses.comment: The CRT's scanf engine - the format walker shared by every scanf-family entry point. 0x200 bytes of stack frame, /GS cookie, and the format loop compares against '%' , '*' and the length modifiers. Referenced exactly once in the whole image, as the INPUTFN constant sscanf hands to its helper, so in this binary it is reached only through sscanf.

addresses.name: strlen
addresses.signature: size_t __cdecl strlen(const char* s)
addresses.comment: MSVC's hand-written strlen - byte loop to a dword boundary, then the 0x7EFEFEFF / 0x81010100 zero-byte-in-a-word trick. Called by the sscanf helper to size the fake FILE's _cnt.

addresses.name: atoi
addresses.signature: int __cdecl atoi(const char* nptr)
addresses.comment: `(int)strtol(nptr, NULL, 10)`. **291 direct call sites, the second most-called unnamed function in the image**, and the other half of how a loader reads a number: where sscanf is used for a value that must be validated, atoi is used where a bad token can silently read as 0. The body here is a four-byte alias - `mov edi,edi; push ebp; mov ebp,esp; pop ebp; jmp 0x7969DB` - because the linker folded two source functions with identical code, keeping one body and one thunk; 0x7969DB is that body.

addresses.name: atol
addresses.signature: long __cdecl atol(const char* nptr)
addresses.comment: `strtol(nptr, NULL, 10)` - the body that atoi at 0x7969F1 jumps into, and separately the target of 8 direct calls of its own.

addresses.name: strtol
addresses.signature: long __cdecl strtol(const char* nptr, char** endptr, int base)
addresses.comment: CRT `strtol`: forwards to the shared signed/unsigned converter at 0x7A2B19 as strtoxl(locale, nptr, endptr, base, flags=0), passing the process locale (0x16F5A14) while the locale-changed flag at 0x174CBF4 is still zero. Reached from atoi/atol; the sibling wrapper at 0x7A300C passes the same shape to a different, 64-bit body (0x7A2D6F) and is the _strtoi64 of the pair.

addresses.name: CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel
addresses.signature: void __stdcall ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel(CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment: The daily supply and fuel draw for one unit. Asks CUnit::SupplyConsumption (0x1BB560) and CUnit::FuelConsumption (0x1BB7A0) what the unit wants, takes what it can get, and writes CUnit::supply_received_percentage (+0xFC) and CUnit::fuel_received_percentage (+0x100) as taken*1000/wanted (1000 when fully supplied, -1 when nothing was wanted, 0 when nothing was available). The country it bills is the expeditionary_owner (+0x28C) where CUnit +0x290 is set, the owner (+0x124) otherwise, through CCountryTag::GetCountry (0x2610). Two paths, chosen on g_CCurrentGameState +0xC9C: >0 draws straight out of CCountry::GetPool(country) (0xF4DE0 - pool_in_exile at +0x9F8 when use_own_pool, the capital province's pool at +0x15C otherwise), the inline copy of that function appearing four times; <=0 walks the supply network - the unit's supply source province, its supply_depot_id (+0x48) into g_CMap +0x2200, and draws that province's pool.supplies (+0x164) and pool.fuel (+0x168) pro rata against the province's need.supplies (+0x24C) and need.fuel (+0x250). Where the depot is controlled by another country a lend-lease conversion runs: the amount is scaled by a rate built from CDefines +0xCC and the receiving country's CGoodsPool at +0x7DC is credited, the supplier's at +0x86C, and both countries' pools are moved. Fuel is only taken when the unit is moving (movement_order_remaining_provinces_count > 0) or is naval and 0x1CDC30 says no; a land or air unit standing still burns none. The last act, for the player's own units only, is to set the byte at +0x1BC on both objects hanging off CUnit +0x164 (+0x13C and +0x140) when either received percentage has fallen below Define50 - the out-of-supply marker on the counter.

addresses.name: CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall UpdatePlanForceNeeds(CUnit* unit, void* difference, void* groupDifference, void* needed, void* wanted)
addresses.comment: Recomputes, per subunit type, what this unit's order of battle is short of against its plan. The three vector<int> arguments are always &unit->+0x5C, &unit->+0x6C and &unit->+0x7C at both call sites; all three are indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index and sized to the subunit definition database's count ((db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4), grown and zero-filled on the first call and, on later calls, with the second and third zeroed at 0x1BD40C while the first is overwritten wholesale. It then walks up higher_oob_unit_ptr to the top of the OOB and, unless that top unit has plan+0x8 (CUnit +0x204) set with oob_level 0, calls ComputePlanWantedSubUnits (0x4E1D00) to build the wanted composition out of the unit's plan (CUnit +0x1FC) and the owner's available subunit types; with the fifth argument null it fills the plan's own buffers at plan+0x18/+0x70/+0x80/+0x84, with it non-null it fills locals instead. The wanted list is the local one where 0x4E1D00 produced one and unit->+0x26C (which is plan+0x70) otherwise. CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType (0x1BD7E0) then counts what the unit actually has, and: difference[i] = wanted[i] - have[i]; groupDifference[GenericType(i)] += difference[i] for every non-zero entry, where GenericType is 0x1ADF70 folding a subunit type onto a representative one; then, over a copy of groupDifference, needed[i] = min(difference[i], groupNet) for each positive deficit, drawing that group's remaining net down as it goes - so a surplus of one type inside a group cancels a deficit of another. Returns true if any entry of needed was set. Runs once a day from CUnit::UpdateDaily for units at oob_level 0 and for HQs at level 1..3 whose +0x198 is set; the level 1..3 units with +0x198 clear have the three vectors cleared instead, and level >=4 is skipped entirely.

addresses.name: CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType(CUnit* this, void* counts, int reserved)
addresses.comment: Counts this unit's subunits by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index into a vector<int>, recursing through the OOB. Where the vector is empty it is first grown to the subunit definition database's count and zero-filled; then counts[regiment->sub_unit_definition_ptr->type_index]++ over CUnit::regiments (+0x38), then the same call on every entry of CUnit::children (+0x1E4). The second argument is pushed as 0 at both call sites and never read.

addresses.name: CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds
addresses.signature: void __stdcall RefreshPlanForceNeeds(CUnit* unit@EAX)
addresses.comment: The out-of-line copy of the gate CUnit::UpdateDaily inlines at 0x1BB273. On a unit with oob_level >= 4 it does nothing; with oob_level 0, or with +0x198 set, it calls CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds(unit, &unit->+0x5C, &unit->+0x6C, &unit->+0x7C, 0); otherwise it clears all three vectors. Called from CSetPlanForcesCommand slot 6 (twice) and CSetPlanAttributesCommand slot 6.

addresses.name: std::string::fromCString
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __cdecl std::string::fromCString(Hoi3CString* this@ESI, const char* text@EDX)
addresses.comment: MSVC's `std::basic_string<char>::basic_string(const char*)`, statically linked and given a register calling convention by LTCG: the string is in ESI and the C string in EDX, nothing is on the stack, and `this` comes back in EAX. The body is the textbook two steps. First `_Tidy()` on an *uninitialised* object - `[esi+0x14] = 0xF` (_Myres), `[esi+0x10] = 0` (_Mysize), `[esi] = 0` (_Buf[0]), the same 0x18-byte layout `std::string::assign` at 0xA160 already reads. Then `assign(_Ptr, _Traits::length(_Ptr))`: a four-instruction inline strlen (`lea edi,[eax+1]` / `mov cl,[eax]; inc eax; test cl,cl; jne` / `sub eax,edi`) whose result is pushed with the pointer before `mov ecx,esi; call 0xA160`. **6732 direct call sites**, far more than any other unnamed function left, and it is how every loader, log line and error message turns a literal into a string - the caller is invariably `mov edx,<literal>; lea esi,<fresh local>; call`, followed by the EH state byte being stepped for the new object. There is no null check on EDX, which is what separates the constructor from an assignment.

addresses.name: LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct
addresses.signature: void __stdcall LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct(LogRecordIosBase* iosBase)
addresses.comment:
The body of `~LogRecord` - the destructor of the ostringstream-derived temporary every log line in the game is built into, inlined at 679 call sites. **Its argument is not the record: it is `record + 0x78`**, the `std::basic_ios` virtual base, and every field is reached at a negative displacement from it, so a reader has to subtract 0x78 to get back to the object. `LogRecordIosBase` is a deliberately separate type for that sub-object rather than `LogRecord*`, because a `LogRecord*` here would render `record+0x50` as `-0x28` into the wrong struct.

It (1) writes the basic_ios vftable 0x15FCE94 through the vbtable at `record+0`, (2) calls `std::ostringstream::str` (`0x65BD10`) to pull the message out of the stringbuf at `record+4`, (3) copies that into a second local string with `std::string::assign`, (4) makes the sink call `(*(*[record+0x50]))[1](channel=[record+0x74], file=record+0x54, line=[record+0x70], message=&text)` - slot 1 of the sink at `record+0x50`, which FINDINGS-script.md already records as `LogSink::Write(channel, file, line, message)` with exactly that field layout, (5) frees both temporaries and the file string at `record+0x54`, and (6) tears the stream back down, vftable 0x15FC550 for the ios base, 0x15F2B34 on the stringbuf at `record+4` before 0x6D1360 and 0x10CD90 destroy it, and 0x15A7B94 last. It does **not** run the final `ios_base` destructor; the caller does, which is why `LogRecord::Flush` at 0x24B0 is only `lea esi,[eax+0x78]; push esi; call this; mov [esi],0x15A7B8C; call 0x794BAE` and why all 679 inline sites repeat that same two-step tail. This is the reason the two targets share so many *::LoadKey callers without sharing all of them: 0x65A7A0 builds the message, this one emits it.

addresses.name: std::endl
addresses.signature: std::ostream* __cdecl std::endl(std::ostream* os)
addresses.comment:
**`std::endl`** - MSVC's `basic_ostream<char>::put(widen('\n')); flush(); return os`, out of line. `__cdecl`, one stack argument, bare `ret`, answers the stream in eax so it chains.

The body is two halves. The `put('\n')` half is the call to `0x9B50`, which is `__stdcall` and cleans the argument itself - which is why there is no `add esp,4` after it at any call site. The `flush()` half is inlined here and is instruction for instruction the body of `std::ostream::flush` at `0x65BB20`: `if (!(rdstate() & (failbit|badbit)) && rdbuf()->pubsync() == -1) state = badbit;` then `if (state) clear(rdstate() | state | (rdbuf() ? 0 : badbit), false)` through `std::ios_base::clear` at `0x20B0`.

**681 direct call sites, and they are the game's log.** The idiom is `LogRecord::Make(file, line, channel) << "text" << ... << endl` - `0x2410` builds the record, `0xA64A00`/`0xA64A30` are its own inserters, `0x21D30` writes the C strings and this ends the line. `*::LoadKey` dominates the caller list because that is where the engine complains about a key it did not understand. MSVC inlined the same pair at about 120 further sites (`0x16E92` is one: `push esi; call 0x409B50` followed by a private copy of the flush body), so the real number of `<< endl` in this executable is higher than the call count.

The stream is reached through a virtual base: `[[os]+4] + os` is the `basic_ios`, whose fields this touches are `+0xC` `_Mystate` and `+0x38` `_Mystrbuf`.

addresses.name: std::operator<<Chars
addresses.signature: std::ostream* __cdecl std::operator<<Chars(std::ostream* os, const char* text)
addresses.comment:
**`std::operator<<(std::ostream&, const char*)`** - the free inserter for a C string, out of line. `__cdecl`, `os` at `[ebp+8]`, the string at `[ebp+0xC]`, bare `ret`, answers `os` in eax. The `Chars` suffix distinguishes it from the other `operator<<` overloads, the way `std::string::appendChars` is distinguished from `appendString` in these findings.

It is the standard algorithm, in order: `strlen` inline (0x421D61, and the same inline `strlen` opens `std::string::assign`'s caller at 0x4022A0); `pad = width() > len ? width() - len : 0`, computed as a full 64-bit compare and subtract because `streamsize` is `__int64` here, against `_Wide` at basic_ios `+0x20`/`+0x24`; then the sentry - `rdbuf()->_Lock()`, and if `_Mystate == 0` and `_Tiestr` (`+0x3C`) is set, `_Tiestr->flush()` through 0xA5BB20; if the sentry is not ok, `badbit`. When it is ok, `(_Fmtfl & 0x1C0) == 0x40` - `adjustfield == left` - decides whether the padding goes after the text (0x421F44) or before it (0x421E22); the fill character is `_Fillch` at `+0x40` and each one goes out through the sputc fast path or `overflow`. The text itself goes through `sputn` (0x22170) and a short write is `badbit`. Then `width(0)` - `_Wide` zeroed at 0x421EA4 - `setstate(state)` through `std::ios_base::clear`, and the sentry's destructor: `uncaught_exception()` (0x794AE9), `_Osfx` (0xA260), `rdbuf()->_Unlock()`.

**845 direct call sites**, for the same reason as `std::endl`: this is what writes every literal in the game's log lines, and `*::LoadKey` is over-represented because that is where parse complaints are written.

basic_ios is a virtual base, reached as `[[os]+4] + os`; the fields used are `+0xC` `_Mystate`, `+0x14` `_Fmtfl`, `+0x20` `_Wide` (64 bit), `+0x38` `_Mystrbuf`, `+0x3C` `_Tiestr`, `+0x40` `_Fillch`.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::clear
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::ios_base::clear(std::ios_base* this, int state, bool reraise)
addresses.comment:
**`std::ios_base::clear(iostate, bool)`**, the bottom of every stream error path. `_Mystate` (`+0xC`) = `state & 0x17` (MSVC's `_Statmask`); if nothing in the new state is in `_Except` (`+0x10`) it returns; if `reraise` it rethrows with `_CxxThrowException(0, 0)`; otherwise it throws `std::ios_base::failure` carrying `ios_base::badbit set` (0x15B4E4C), `ios_base::failbit set` (0x15B4E64) or `ios_base::eofbit set` (0x15B4E7C), in that priority order, through `_CxxThrowException` with the `_ThrowInfo` at 0x164B158.

`this` is the `basic_ios` (== the `ios_base` subobject), so callers reach it as `[[os]+4] + os`. The `basic_ios::clear` wrapper is inlined at every call site as the two instructions `cmp dword ptr [ecx+0x38], 0 / or eax, 4` - the 'no rdbuf means badbit' rule - which is why the callee never looks at the buffer itself.

addresses.name: std::ostream::flush
addresses.signature: std::ostream* __thiscall std::ostream::flush(std::ostream* this@ESI)
addresses.comment:
**`std::basic_ostream<char>::flush()`**: `if (!(rdstate() & (failbit|badbit)) && rdbuf()->pubsync() == -1) setstate(badbit); return *this;`. `pubsync` is the streambuf's virtual at `+0x34`; the `-1` answer is the only failure it recognises.

**`this` arrives in ESI, not ECX** - the compiler gave this one a convention of its own, as it did `std::string::operator=` (eax) and `LogRecord::Flush` (eax). Every caller sets esi and nothing else: 0x40A296 (`_Osfx`), 0x409BA8 and 0x421DD8 (the two sentry constructors, flushing `_Tiestr`). Bare `ret`, the stream comes back in eax.

Its body is what `std::endl` at 0x2240 has inlined; the two are the same 25 instructions.

addresses.name: std::ostream::_Osfx
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::ostream::_Osfx(std::ostream* this)
addresses.comment: MSVC's `basic_ostream<char>::_Osfx()`, the end-of-operation hook the `sentry` destructor runs: `if (flags() & unitbuf) flush();`, wrapped in a catch-all (the SEH funclet at 0x40A2AC swallows anything the flush throws). `unitbuf` is `_Fmtfl & 2` at basic_ios `+0x14`; the flush is 0xA5BB20 with `this` handed over in esi. `this` in ecx as usual, no stack arguments, bare `ret`.

addresses.name: std::streambuf::sputn
addresses.signature: __int64 __thiscall std::streambuf::sputn(std::streambuf* this, const char* text, __int64 count)
addresses.comment: Seven instructions: hand `(text, count)` to the buffer's virtual at `+0x24` - slot 9, `xsputn` - and answer what it answers, a 64-bit count in edx:eax. `ret 0xC`, so `__thiscall` with a pointer and a `streamsize`. `std::operator<<Chars` compares the result against the length it asked for and sets `badbit` when they differ.

addresses.name: std::putNewline
addresses.signature: std::ostream* __stdcall std::putNewline(std::ostream* os)
addresses.comment:
**The `put(widen('\n'))` half of `std::endl`, kept out of line**: construct the sentry (`rdbuf()->_Lock()`, flush `_Tiestr`, ok = `_Mystate == 0`), write 0x0A through the buffer's put pointer or, when there is no room, through `overflow`; `badbit` if either the sentry was not ok or `overflow` answered -1; `setstate`; destroy the sentry; answer the stream.

**`__stdcall`** - it cleans its own argument, `ret 4`, which is why no call site has an `add esp,4` after it. 120 direct call sites: 0x2240 (`std::endl` itself) and about 119 places where the compiler inlined `endl`'s flush half but left this call standing, 0x16E92 among them.

The name is descriptive, not a symbol the library exports. It is not `basic_ostream::put`: the character is the constant 0xA, baked in at both 0x9BF2 and 0x9BFF, and there is no character parameter.

addresses.name: __allrem
addresses.signature: __int64 __stdcall __allrem(__int64 dividend, __int64 divisor)
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT signed 64-bit remainder (llrem.asm). With the two saved registers on the stack the dividend is at [esp+0xC..0x13] and the divisor at [esp+0x14..0x1B]; remainder in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). **The remainder takes the dividend's sign alone**, which is what tells it apart from __alldiv at 0x799980: the two bodies are otherwise the same shape, but __alldiv has `inc edi` on both the dividend branch (0xB9998D) and the divisor branch (0xB999A9) and negates when exactly one operand was negative, while this one has `inc edi` on the dividend branch (0xB99A3C) and **none** on the divisor branch at 0xB99A56, so the flag counts only the dividend - and the tail tests it with `jns` rather than __alldiv's `jne`. It is signed, not __aullrem, which has no sign handling at all. 7 direct call sites.

addresses.name: __allshl
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT 64-bit left shift (llshl.asm). Value in edx:eax, count in cl, result in edx:eax, nothing on the stack, bare ret. Three cases: count >= 64 answers zero (0xB99B4A), count >= 32 moves eax into edx and shifts it by count&31 with eax zeroed (0xB99B40), otherwise `shld edx, eax, cl` then `shl eax, cl` (0xB99B3A). Sign-agnostic - a left shift is the same body for signed and unsigned, which is why MSVC emits one body for both. 4 direct call sites.

addresses.name: ComputePlanWantedSubUnits
addresses.signature: void __stdcall ComputePlanWantedSubUnits(void* plan, CUnit* unit, void* area, std::vector<int>* wanted, int* ownStrength, int* areaStrength, bool useArea)
addresses.comment: Builds the order of battle a plan asks for. Called only from CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (rva 0x1BD240), twice, and it is what fills CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted. In order: (1) grows `wanted` to GetNumberOfSubUnits() entries and zeroes every one of them (0x8E1DB3..0x8E1E39, the loop bound is (db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4); (2) resolves about a dozen roles to concrete subunit types by taking the database's cached role definitions at db+0x2C, +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C, +0x40, +0x50, +0x58, +0x6C, +0x7C, +0x80 and +0x84 (those eleven and no others; 0x1ADF70 reaches six more of the same block, +0x44, +0x78, +0x98, +0xA0, +0xA8 and +0xAC) and keeping each only if the owner's availability byte array says so - `country->+0xDF8->+0x27C[definition->type_index] != 0` and then the second test at rva 0x1A3BC0 - falling back to db+0x34 otherwise (0x8E1E3F..0x8E2075); (3) collects the unit's own regiments through rva 0x1BD930 and accumulates, into *ownStrength, each one's strength (CRegiment +0x5C) over its maximum times its organisation over CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation, counting them by category with the 0..6 classifier at rva 0x1A8540 (0x8E20C4..0x8E22A2); (4) walks the plan's province list at [area], and for each province its 0x14-byte border records at +0xD4 ->+0x90..+0x94, skipping type 3, accumulating into *areaStrength (0x8E2387..0x8E26E0); (5) turns that frontage into counts using the plan type at plan+0xC (2, 3 and 4 each select a different global) and several defines, and finally does `wanted[definition->type_index]++` once per requested regiment for each role (0x8E2FE0, 0x8E3027, 0x8E31B6, 0x8E31E2). `useArea` switches the source of the scope: with it set the caller supplies `area` and the regiment collection is filtered by it; with it clear the unit's whole OOB is used and `area` is the plan's own province list. Returns nothing - eax is zero on every path and neither call site reads it.

addresses.name: CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute(void)
addresses.comment:
Slot 6 of `CSetPlanAttributesCommand` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`). It resolves the command's `unit` reference and writes the six battle-plan attributes it carries onto that unit's embedded `CUnitPlan` (`CUnit +0x1FC`), each with a sentinel meaning "not set by this command":

| command field | key | sentinel | lands on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x64` byte | `active` | none | `CUnitPlan::SetActive` (`0x4DEB10`) |
| `+0x68` | `stance` | `== 5` skips | plan `+0xC` = `CUnit +0x208` |
| `+0x6C` | `air_stance` | `== 3` skips | plan `+0x10` = `CUnit +0x20C` |
| `+0x70` | `naval_stance` | `== 3` skips | plan `+0x14` = `CUnit +0x210` |
| `+0x74` | `our_power` | `< 0` skips | plan `+0x80` = `CUnit +0x27C` |
| `+0x78` | `their_power` | `< 0` skips | plan `+0x84` = `CUnit +0x280` |

Only the `stance` branch calls `CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds` (at `0x1E78B4`) - changing the ground stance is what changes what the plan needs; the air and naval stances and the two power estimates do not.

**It re-resolves the unit for every field it writes** - six separate `FindPersistentById` lookups off `this->+0x40`/`+0x44` - rather than resolving once, which is why the body is four times longer than what it does. Each lookup has a failure arm that falls through to `xor eax, eax` and then stores through the null pointer anyway (`0x1E79EB` writes `[0 + 0x280]`); the game survives only because a command whose target has gone is rejected by `IsValid` before slot 6 is reached.

addresses.name: CSetPlanForcesCommand::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSetPlanForcesCommand::Execute(void)
addresses.comment:
Slot 6 of `CSetPlanForcesCommand` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`). It resolves its `unit` reference, hands the `min` vector it carries at `+0x64` to `CUnitPlan::SetMinForces` (`0x4DF0F0`), which replaces plan `+0x70` - `CUnit +0x26C`, already named `plan_subunit_wanted` - and then calls `CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds` so the shortfall per subunit type is recomputed against the new target.

The two calls to `RefreshPlanForceNeeds` (`0x1E8928` and `0x1E8934`) are the two arms of the second lookup, not two refreshes: the second passes `eax = 0`, the null arm of a resolve the compiler inlined twice. So it refreshes once, and would dereference null if the unit had gone - which `IsValid` prevents.

addresses.name: CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::Execute(void)
addresses.comment:
Slot 6 of `CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`), and the third and last body in the image that reaches `CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds`.

One province list at `+0x64` and one flag at `+0x74` decide which of the plan's two province lists it replaces:

    if (this->fallback_line)   CUnitPlan::SetFallbackLine(plan, &this->provinces)   // plan +0x28, returns here
    else                       CUnitPlan::SetOpsArea(plan, &this->provinces)        // plan +0x18
                               CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds(unit)
                               if (unit->owner == the local player's country
                                   && this->unit_ref matches the local session)
                                       gamestate->+0xBE8 slot 32(...)               // 0x1E649F

So a fallback line costs nothing - it is a line, not an area to hold - while an operations area changes what the plan needs and refreshes it. The tail is the only part of the three plan commands that touches the GUI, and it is gated on the unit belonging to the player at this client.

addresses.name: CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand
addresses.signature: CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand* __stdcall CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand(CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand* self, void* unit, void* provinces)
addresses.comment:
**Not slot 6, and in no virtual table**: this is `CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand`'s constructor, and the reason it looked like the third `RefreshPlanForceNeeds` caller is that `image.functionStart` attributes `0x1E629D` to it - there is no `int3` padding between its `ret 0xC` at `0x1E617D` and the real owner, `CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::Execute`, at `0x1E6180`.

It inlines the `CCommand` base constructor rather than calling it - `CCommand`'s vftable at `0x15B4F74` goes in first and is overwritten with its own at `0x15C931C` - then fills `+0x2C`/`+0x30` with 0x70A, the tickstamp word at `+0x34` with 0xFFFF, the identity at `+0x38` with 0, builds the `unit` reference at `+0x3C` out of its second argument and copies the province list into `+0x64`. `this` arrives on the stack rather than in ecx and the object comes back in eax; the five callers all `operator new(0x78)` first, which is the class's size.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::SetActive
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnitPlan::SetActive(CUnitPlan* this@ESI, bool active)
addresses.comment:
Writes the plan's `active` byte at `+0x8` (`CUnit +0x204`), and **when switching it off, resets the whole plan first**: the objective, path, ops-area and fallback lists at `+0x18`, `+0x28`, `+0x38`, `+0x48`, `+0x5C` and `+0x70`/`+0x74` are emptied, `stance` (`+0xC`) goes back to 2, `air_stance` and `naval_stance` to 0, both power estimates (`+0x80`, `+0x84`) and `+0x88`/`+0x8C` to 0, and the byte at `+0x9` to 0. Switching it on writes nothing but the byte.

The compiler gave it a register convention: the plan arrives in esi, the flag on the stack.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::SetMinForces
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnitPlan::SetMinForces(CUnitPlan* this@EAX, void* min)

Replaces the plan's minimum force composition - the `vector<int>` at `+0x70`/`+0x74`, which is `CUnit +0x26C`, already named `plan_subunit_wanted` - with the one it is given. The `min` key of a `unit_plan` in the save, and what `CSetPlanForcesCommand` carries.

addresses.name: std::ostream::writeCString
addresses.signature: std::ostream* __cdecl std::ostream::writeCString(std::ostream* os@ESI, const char* text@EDX) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**`os.write(text, strlen(text))` for a NUL-terminated string**, and the `<<` that 427 call sites use to put a C string into the game's log. `strlen` is open-coded as the four-instruction byte scan at `0xA64A10`; the length and a zero high dword are then pushed with the pointer and the stream and `std::ostream::write` (`0x664A30`) is called. It answers the stream in `eax` so the idiom chains: `LogRecord::Make(file, line, channel) << "text" << ... << endl`.

**The convention is one the optimiser invented, not `__cdecl` as written on a page.** Both arguments arrive in registers - the stream in `esi` (never saved, never reloaded: the epilogue is `mov eax, esi`) and the string in `edx` (`mov eax, edx` is the first thing the body does) - and the function ends in a bare `ret` having consumed nothing from the stack. `0x434389` is a plain example: `mov edx, 0x15B65D0 ('Bad messagetype'); mov esi, eax; call 0xA64A00; push eax; call std::endl`. This is the same re-signing that gave `std::string::fromCString` (`0x65A7A0`) its `this@ESI, text@EDX` and `std::ostream::flush` (`0x65BB20`) its `this@ESI`.

**It is not `std::operator<<Chars` (`0x21D30`), and the difference is real.** `0x21D30` is MSVC's `_Insert_string`: it reads `ios_base::_Wide` at `+0x20/+0x24`, computes the padding, emits `_Fillch` from `+0x40` and finishes with `width(0)`. This one does none of that - it goes straight to `write`, so a stream with a non-zero `width()` formats differently through the two. **What I could not settle** is whether that makes it a second `operator<<(ostream&, const char*)` from a translation unit built against a different `<ostream>`, or an engine-local unpadded fast inserter; the name records what it does rather than deciding that.

The four call sites that do not load `edx` from a string literal are the reason this wrapper exists at all: where the length is not a compile-time constant the compiler cannot fold it, so it calls the scanner instead of `write` directly.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor
addresses.signature: void __cdecl std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor(std::ios_base* base)
addresses.comment:
**Confirmed: this is the `ios_base` destructor**, specifically the out-of-line static body that MSVC's `virtual ~ios_base()` consists of a single call to. The earlier report guessed right.

    if (_Stdstr == 0 || --_Stdstr_refs[_Stdstr] <= 0) {
        _Tidy();                                  // 0x794B15
        if (_Ploc) { _Ploc->~locale(); free(_Ploc); }
    }

The guard is the standard-stream reference count. `ios_base +8` is the slot index into an eight-entry table of standard streams at VA `0x174C818` with a parallel byte refcount array at VA `0x174C840`; this function decrements that byte and returns without tearing anything down while it is still positive, so `cout`/`cerr`/`clog` survive every `ios_base::Init` but the last. `std::ios_base::_Addstd` (`0x794B59`) is the only other code in the image that touches either table, and it increments exactly the byte this decrements.

When it does tear down: `_Tidy()` releases the `_Arr` and `_Calls` lists (`+0x28`, `+0x2C`), then `_Ploc` at `+0x30` gets `std::locale::~locale` (`0x2EE40`, `this` in `ecx`) followed by `free` (`0x795F9B`, which is what `operator delete` folded to here).

**How the 700 call sites read.** Every one of them is a derived class destroying its `ios_base` base, and each writes the `ios_base` virtual table `0x15A7B8C` into the object immediately before the call - textbook base-subobject destruction with the vfptr reset. `LogRecord::Flush` (`0x24B0`) is the example the handover named:

    lea esi, [eax+0x78]          ; the ios_base subobject inside the record
    push esi; call LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct
    push esi; mov [esi], 0x15A7B8C
    call 0x794BAE

`__cdecl`, one stack argument at `[ebp+8]`, bare `ret`, no return value. It is *not* itself virtual and sits in no class's virtual table; the virtual destructor that calls it is the scalar deleting destructor at `0x2210`, which is unnamed and left for the next wave.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Tidy
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::ios_base::_Tidy(std::ios_base* this)
addresses.comment:
`ios_base::_Tidy()` - runs the registered callbacks with `erase_event` and then frees both of `ios_base`'s owned lists:

    _Callfns(erase_event);                 // 0x794AEE, with the literal 0
    for (p = _Arr;   p; p = next) free(p); _Arr = 0;      // +0x28
    for (p = _Calls; p; p = next) free(p); _Calls = 0;    // +0x2C

Both loops read the `_Next` pointer at offset `0` of the node before freeing it, which is the `_Iosarray` / `_Calls_t` layout. `__thiscall`, no stack arguments, bare `ret`. Recorded here because it is the only callee of `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` that was not already named and it is what fixes `+0x28` and `+0x2C` as the two list heads.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Addstd
addresses.signature: void __cdecl std::ios_base::_Addstd(std::ios_base* base)
addresses.comment:
The increment side of the standard-stream reference count that `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`) decrements. Under `_Lockit(_LOCK_STREAM)` - the literal `2` passed to `0x79504A` - it scans the eight-entry pointer table at VA `0x174C818` from index 1 for a free slot or for itself, stores the index in `ios_base +8`, stores the pointer in the table and increments the byte at `0x174C840 + index`. `__cdecl`, one stack argument, bare `ret`.

Recorded here rather than left on the frontier because it is the evidence that `ios_base +8` is the standard-stream index and that the byte array at `0x174C840` is a refcount - without it the guard at the top of `0x794BAE` is unreadable.

addresses.name: LogRecord::Construct
addresses.signature: LogRecord* __stdcall LogRecord::Construct(LogRecord* record@ESI, int line@ECX, int channel@EAX, LogSink* sink, Hoi3CString* file) @EAX
addresses.comment: The register-convention forwarder LTCG left between `LogRecord::Make` and the constructor at `0x6646E0`: it takes the record in esi, the line in ecx and the channel in eax, the sink and the file on the stack, and pushes all five in the order the `__stdcall` constructor wants (`record, sink, file, line, channel`). Returns the record in eax. `ret 8` - it cleans only the two it was given on the stack.

addresses.name: LogRecord::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.signature: LogRecord* __thiscall LogRecord::ScalarDeletingDestructor(LogRecordIosBase* this, int flags) @EAX
addresses.comment: MSVC's `??_G` for the record: `this` arrives as `record+0x78` (the `basic_ios` virtual base, the same thing `FlushAndDestruct` takes), it recovers the record with `lea edi,[ecx-0x78]`, runs `LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct` and then `~ios_base` (`0x794BAE`), and frees the record only when bit 0 of `flags` is set. `ret 4`, record back in eax. Sits in no virtual table - `vtable.py --holding 0xA64790` finds none - so nothing dispatches to it; it is the out-of-line copy the compiler emitted anyway.

addresses.name: std::ostringstream::ostringstream
addresses.signature: std::ostringstream* __stdcall std::ostringstream::ostringstream(std::ostringstream* stream, int mode, int isMostDerived)
addresses.comment:
`std::basic_ostringstream<char>`'s constructor, shared by the plain stream and by `LogRecord`, which is why it looks the virtual base offset up instead of using a constant: `esi = stream + *(int*)(*stream + 4)` is the `basic_ios`, so the same body works whether that lives at `+0x50` (a plain ostringstream) or at `+0x78` (a LogRecord). When `isMostDerived` is non-zero it also writes its own vbtable `0x160285C` at `+0` and the `ios_base` vftable `0x15A7B9C` at `+0x50`; `LogRecord::LogRecord` passes 0 because it has already written its own. Then `ios_base::_Init` (`0xC7FA0`), `basic_ios._Mystrbuf = stream+4`, `_Tiestr = 0`, `_Fillch = widen(' ')`, the `basic_ios` vftable `0x15FC550`, the stringbuf constructor at `0x10F0E0` with vftable `0x15F2B34`, and finally the stringbuf's `_Seekhigh = 0` and `_Mystate = mode|ios::out` at `stream+0x40`/`stream+0x44`. `ret 0xC`.

**This is what fixes the class's field boundaries:** for a plain ostringstream the virtual base sits at `+0x50`, so the vbptr plus the `basic_stringbuf` occupy exactly `0..0x4F`, and `LogRecord`'s own four fields are what push its `basic_ios` out to `+0x78`.

addresses.name: std::ostringstream::str
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __cdecl std::ostringstream::str(std::ostringstream* stream@ECX, Hoi3CString* out@EAX) @EAX
addresses.comment: `ostringstream::str()`, register convention: the stream in ecx, the string to fill in eax. All it does is `add ecx,4` to reach the `basic_stringbuf` and call `0x520940`, then answer the out string. Bare `ret`, nothing on the stack. `LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct` calls this to get the accumulated message before handing it to the sink.

addresses.name: std::string::concat
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __cdecl std::string::concat(Hoi3CString* out, Hoi3CString* left, Hoi3CString* right) @EAX
addresses.comment: The out-of-line body of `std::operator+(const std::string&, const std::string&)`. It tidies `out` to the empty state (`_Myres = 0xF`, `_Mysize = 0`, `out[0] = 0`), reserves `left.length + right.length` through `0x1D50`, then `appendString(out, left, 0, -1)` and `appendString(out, right, 0, -1)`. addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Init
addresses.signature: void __cdecl std::ios_base::_Init(std::ios_base* base@ECX)

`ios_base::_Init()`: zeroes `+8`, `_Except` (`+0x10`), sets `_Fmtfl = 0x201` (`skipws|dec`) at `+0x14`, `_Prec = 6` at `+0x18`/`+0x1C` (a `streamsize` is `__int64` here), `_Wide = 0` at `+0x20`/`+0x24`, `_Arr = _Calls = 0` at `+0x28`/`+0x2C`, calls `std::ios_base::clear(0, false)` for `_Mystate` at `+0xC`, and finally allocates a four-byte `locale` into `_Ploc` at `+0x30`. `ecx` is the receiver, nothing is on the stack, bare `ret`.

addresses.name: TokenToFixedPoint
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall TokenToFixedPoint(CToken* token, int* out) @EAX
addresses.comment:
Turns a `CToken`'s text into the engine's thousandths fixed point: `*out = atoi(text) * 1000 + fraction`, where `fraction` is the digits after the first `.` read as a number and then padded with zeros to exactly three places - `1.5` gives 1500, `1.25` gives 1250, `2` gives 2000, and a token with no `.` at all gives a fraction of 0. The sign comes from `text[0]`: when it is `-` and `atoi` returned 0 the fraction is negated anyway, so `-0.5` comes out -500.

The `imul 1000` / `__allmul(x,1000)` / `__alldiv(x,1000000)` round trip in the middle is a 64 bit overflow guard on a fraction with more than three digits, not a second scaling - `lea edx,[eax+0x189373]; cmp edx,0x39580D` picks the 32 bit path only when `eax*1000` cannot overflow, and both paths hand the same fraction back. The fast path's `0x431BDE83` with `sar edx,0x12` is the standard divide-by-1000000 magic (2^50/10^6 = 1125899906.8).

**188 direct call sites, all loaders**, and the argument is `parse + 0x228` (`CParseContext::value`, the CToken) at every one looked at. It takes the token, not the context, so it reports nothing: a token that is not a number simply gives 0. It answers `out` in eax so the caller can read the value straight back - `call; mov eax,[eax]; mov [ebx+0xC4],eax` at 0x4CDE8B, and `call; movd xmm0,[eax]; cvtdq2ps; divsd [0x160A300]` (1000.0) at 0x4B1F93, which is the float the loader actually wanted.

addresses.name: ParseFixedPoint
addresses.signature: void __stdcall ParseFixedPoint(CParseContext* parse@EAX, int* out@EDI)
addresses.comment:
The fixed point reader of the `*::LoadKey` family, beside `ParseInt` (0x67B470), `ParseBool` and `ParseString`: `*out` gets the value token as thousandths. Both arguments are in registers, so there is nothing on the stack and the function ends in a bare `ret`.

It takes one of two readings, decided by the tokenizer's virtual slot 2 - `mov ecx,[parse+0x1C]; mov eax,[ecx]; call [eax+8]`, on the field project.json already calls `CParseContext::tokenizer`. That slot is `_purecall` in the tokenizer base (vftable 0x15FD1F0, slots 1 and 2 both 0xB961D5) and a compile time constant in each subclass, so it is a kind flag, not a computation: the tokenizer used everywhere for files (vftable 0x15FD1FC, 78 construction sites) answers **false** through `xor al,al; ret` at 0x192360, and the rarer one (vftable 0x15FD208, 4 sites, all reached from the 0xB3xxxx network module) answers **true** through `mov al,1; ret` at 0x692590.

True takes the text as already scaled - `sscanf(parse->value.text, "%i", out)` straight into `*out`. False sends `&parse->value` to 0x6696A0, which is the checked form of `TokenToFixedPoint`: `sscanf("%i")` for the whole part, `strstr(text, ".")` for a fraction, the first three fraction digits zero-padded, and the whole thing multiplied by 1000 - so the `1.5` a script file writes becomes 1500. Either reading failing ends in `ReportParseError(parse@ESI)`, which esi already holds.

**76 direct call sites**, the switch arm shape being `mov eax,[ebp+8]; lea edi,[<field>]; call` with the caller's `ret 8` right after (0x414FB4, 0x4CD030).

addresses.name: Date_SetFromString
addresses.signature: void __stdcall Date_SetFromString(int* date@ESI, const char* text)
addresses.comment:
Sets a date tick from the text `year.month.day.hour`, in place, joining `Date_Year`, `Date_DayOfYear`, `Date_DayOfMonth` and `Date_DayOfWeek` as the writing half of that family. **782 direct call sites**, the most-called unnamed function in the image after the parse helpers, and the text handed to it is `parse + 0x22C` (`CParseContext::value.text`) at every site inspected.

It is `sscanf(text, "%d.%d.%d.%d", &year, &month, &day, &hour)`, then month and day are decremented to 0 based, then the tick is rebuilt on the epoch `CLASSES.md` records: `tick = 24 * sign(year) * (365*|year| + dayOfYear(old tick)) + 43800000 + hourOfDay(old tick)`, where 0x29C55C0 = 43800000 and 0x538AB8*8 is the same number. The month is then added by 0x4C420 and the day of the month by 0x4C360 - both walk the month length table at rva 0x1313294 - and finally the hour of day is replaced by the parsed one. Callers hand it a date holding exactly the epoch (`mov [esp+0x64],0x29C55C0; lea esi,[esp+0x64]` at 0x4CE4A2), so the old day-of-year and hour-of-day it preserves are both zero and the result is exactly the date in the string.

**The sscanf return is never tested.** A string that is not a date leaves year 0 and, because the decrements are unconditional, month -1 and day -1, so the tick walks backwards off the epoch and nothing is reported - the same silence `FINDINGS-...` records for unknown keys.
