addresses.comment:
Looks a name up in the engine's own string hash table and answers the stored pointer, or null. **206 direct call sites.**

The table is `{int count; unsigned bucketCount; void** buckets;}` at +0/+4/+8 and a node is `{void* value; Node* next;}`. The hash is the engine's string hash, `h = (h + c) * 61` over the length of the key (`imul eax,eax,0x3D`, the same three bytes inlined at 23 places in the image), reduced by `div [table+4]`. Each node in the bucket is compared by taking `value + 8` as an `Hoi3CString` and running the 4-bytes-at-a-time compare at 0x15F70 over `min(keylen, storedlen)` characters, with the lengths broken as the tie - so **the key is a member of the stored object, at +8**, and nothing is copied into the table.

That +8 is what fixes this instantiation of what is otherwise a template body: the insert half at 0x5C87C0 is the same table and the same hash with the key at value+4. The table itself is a member of whatever owns it (`esi+0x10` of a global at 0x4CDCE7, `vf[0x44]() + 0x6BCF0` at 0x406B5A), and the value is used as a polymorphic object straight afterwards (`mov edx,[eax]; mov ecx,eax; call [edx+0x48]`), so this is the by-name index the loaders go through when a script names a thing.

No class on the name deliberately: the body is shared by several owners, it is in no virtual table, and which class the values belong to is not settled here.

addresses.name: std::iostream_category
addresses.signature: std::error_category* __cdecl std::iostream_category() @EAX
addresses.comment:
**Two instructions - `mov eax, 0x16F5204; ret` - and it is not half of building the exception.** It is `std::iostream_category()`: the address it answers is the static `_Iostream_error_category` singleton, whose vfptr at `+0` is `0x15A7A84` and whose RTTI type descriptor reads `.?AV_Iostream_error_category@std@@`. Its `name()` (slot 1, `0x794A66`) is `return *(const char**)(this+4)`, and `this+4` = `0x16F5204+4` holds `0x15A7A74`, the address of the literal `"iostream"`.

The three call sites are the three throw paths of `std::ios_base::clear` (`0x20B0`) and each uses the result as the `_Cat` half of an `error_code`:

    call  std::iostream_category         ; edi = the category
    mov   [esp+0xC], 0x15B4E4C           ; "ios_base::badbit set"
    lea   ecx, [esp+0x10]                ; the exception object
    call  std::exception::exception      ; 0x795991
    mov   [esp+0x20], esi                ; error_code._Val  = 1  (io_errc::stream)
    mov   [esp+0x24], edi                ; error_code._Cat  = this
    mov   [esp+0x14], 0x15A7BD8          ; vfptr <- std::ios_base::failure
    call  _CxxThrowException

So `ios_base::clear` throws `failure(msg, make_error_code(io_errc::stream))`, exactly as `<xiosbase>` documents, and the `failure` layout is {vfptr, `_Mywhat`, `_Mydofree`, `_Mycode._Val`, `_Mycode._Cat`}. `__cdecl`, no arguments, bare `ret`, pointer back in eax. The `_Generic_error_category` and `_System_error_category` singletons sit immediately after it, at `0x16F5208` and `0x16F520C`, with tables `0x15A7A5C` and `0x15A7AA8`; their accessors and virtuals are left on the frontier.

addresses.name: std::exception::exception
addresses.signature: std::exception* __thiscall std::exception::exception(std::exception* this, const char** what) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**`std::exception::exception(const char* const& _What)`** - the base constructor of every standard exception in the image, not something built for `ios_base::failure`. It writes the `std::exception` vftable `0x15A7C88` at `+0`, zeroes `_Mywhat` at `+4` and `_Mydofree` at `+8`, then calls `_Copy_str` (`0x795933`) with `*what`.

**The parameter is a pointer to a `const char*`, not a `const char*`** - `mov eax,[ebp+8]; push [eax]` - which is MSVC's `exception(const char *const &)` signature verbatim, and is why every call site first parks the literal in a stack slot and passes that slot's address. Recording it as `const char*` would make every caller decompile with a bogus extra dereference.

`__thiscall`, `ret 4`, the object back in eax. 297 direct callers, of which the three in `std::ios_base::clear` are the ones the handover was looking at; the rest are every `throw std::runtime_error(...)` / `bad_alloc` / `bad_cast` in the game. The derived constructors are one instruction longer and sit right after it: `0x7959ED` (`bad_cast`, vftable `0x15A7CA8`), `0x795A16` (`bad_typeid`, `0x15A7CB4`), `0x402060` (`runtime_error`, `0x159FDA0`).

addresses.name: std::uncaught_exception
addresses.signature: bool __cdecl std::uncaught_exception() @AL
addresses.comment:
A five-byte `jmp 0x79CD77` and nothing else - `std::uncaught_exception()` tail-calling the CRT's `__uncaught_exception`. The handover's description is confirmed.

It has 16 callers and every one reads the result the same way, `test al,al` followed by a jump around a call: that is the `basic_ostream::sentry` destructor, `if (!uncaught_exception()) _Osfx();`. `std::ostream::write` (`0x664A30`) is the example the previous wave named - `0xA64B3B: call 0xB94AE9; test al,al; jne 0xA64B4B; mov ecx,edi; call 0x40A260`, and `0xA260` is already recorded as `std::ostream::_Osfx`.

No arguments, `bool` in al. Written `__cdecl` because the caller consumes nothing; the jump target's own `ret` is bare.

addresses.name: __uncaught_exception
addresses.signature: bool __cdecl __uncaught_exception() @AL
addresses.comment: The CRT side of the above: `return _getptd()->_ProcessingThrow != 0`. Three instructions after the call - `call 0x7A0FFE; xor ecx,ecx; cmp [eax+0x90], ecx; setne al; ret`. `0x7A0FFE` is the per-thread data getter (59 callers across the CRT), and `+0x90` into that block is the in-flight-throw counter. Recorded here because `std::uncaught_exception` (`0x794AE9`) is nothing but a jump to it and cannot be read without it. No arguments, bare `ret`, `bool` in al.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Callfns
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::ios_base::_Callfns(std::ios_base* this, int event)

addresses.name: std::locale::Destruct
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::locale::Destruct(std::locale* this)
addresses.comment:
Confirms the handover's reading of the body, with one correction to the name's spelling. This is `std::locale::~locale()` with `facet::_Decref()` inlined into it:

    if (_Ptr) {                       // the _Locimp* at locale +0
        _Lockit lock(_LOCK_LOCALE);   // 0x79504A with the literal 0
        if (0 < _Ptr->_Myrefs && _Ptr->_Myrefs != (size_t)-1) --_Ptr->_Myrefs;
        dead = _Ptr->_Myrefs == 0 ? _Ptr : 0;   // the neg/sbb/not/and at 0x42EE69
        ~_Lockit();                   // 0x795072
        if (dead) dead->vftable[0](1);          // scalar deleting destructor
    }

So a `locale` is one pointer wide, which is why `ios_base::_Init` allocates exactly four bytes into `_Ploc`; the refcount is at `_Locimp +4`; and `-1` is the sentinel that keeps the classic locale alive forever.

`__thiscall`, no stack arguments, bare `ret`. Four callers: `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`), which destroys `_Ploc` at `+0x30` and then frees it, and three in `0x50E742`/`0x50ED2E`/`0x50ED54`.

**The name is spelled `Destruct`, not `~locale`.** project.json holds exactly one `~` name (`CSubUnitDataBase::~CSubUnitDataBase`) and the convention the log family already established for this is a word - `LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct`, `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor`. Whoever prefers the tilde should rename it once, everywhere.

addresses.name: std::_Lockit::_Lockit
addresses.signature: std::_Lockit* __thiscall std::_Lockit::_Lockit(std::_Lockit* this, int kind) @EAX

addresses.name: std::_Lockit::Destruct
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::_Lockit::Destruct(std::_Lockit* this)
addresses.comment:
The matching `~_Lockit()`: read the kind back out of `+0` and, if it is below 4, leave the same critical section. `0xB958E8` forwards to the `LeaveCriticalSection` import. Seven instructions, no prologue at all - `this` in ecx, no stack arguments, bare `ret`, nothing returned. 47 callers, the same count as the constructor.

Spelled `Destruct` rather than `~_Lockit` for the same reason as `std::locale::Destruct` above.

addresses.name: std::stringbuf::str
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __cdecl std::stringbuf::str(std::stringbuf* buf@ECX, Hoi3CString* out@ESI) @EAX

addresses.name: std::ios_base::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.signature: std::ios_base* __thiscall std::ios_base::ScalarDeletingDestructor(std::ios_base* this, int flags) @EAX
addresses.comment:
Confirms the handover in full. MSVC's `??_G` for `ios_base`, and **the virtual-table slot that `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`) sits behind**:

    mov  [esi], 0x15A7B8C        ; the ios_base vftable
    push esi; call 0x794BAE; add esp,4
    if (flags & 1) free(esi);
    return esi;

`__thiscall`, `ret 4`, the object back in eax. **It has no direct callers at all** - every use is a virtual dispatch, which is what one expects of a slot-0 destructor and is the complement of `_Ios_base_dtor`'s 700 direct calls.

**It is slot 0 of two tables**: `std::ios_base`'s own (`0x15A7B8C`, RTTI `.?AVios_base@std@@`) and `std::basic_ios<char>`'s (`0x15A7B9C`, RTTI `.?AV?$basic_ios@DU?$char_traits@D@std@@@std@@`, which project.json spells `std::anon::anon::std::D::DU__char_traits::__basic_ios`). Both tables have exactly one slot. The body belongs to `ios_base` - it writes `ios_base`'s own vftable, not `basic_ios`'s - and `basic_ios` derives from `ios_base` in project.json's class record, so the derived table holds the inherited body. Both slots are recorded under `vftable_slots`.

The neighbouring vftable `0x15A7B94` is `std::basic_ostream<char>`'s at object offset 8 and its slot 0 is a different body (`0x50E270`), so it is not part of this and is left on the frontier.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan(CUnitPlan* this@EAX)
addresses.comment:
The battle plan's constructor, and **the whole of its layout in one place**. A leaf: the object arrives in EAX, nothing is pushed, and it ends in a bare `ret`.

It writes the vftable `0x15C8BFC` at `+0x0`, the save-token id `0x18D` at `+0x4` (CPersistent's own field), zeroes the word at `+0x8` (`active` and `allow_hq_reorg`), sets `stance` (`+0xC`) to 2 and `air_stance`/`naval_stance` (`+0x10`/`+0x14`) to 1, zeroes five CList heads at `+0x18`, `+0x28`, `+0x38`, `+0x48` and `+0x5C` (each first/last/count and a flag byte, 0x10 bytes), the loose dwords at `+0x58` and `+0x6C`, the `vector<int>` at `+0x70`/`+0x74`/`+0x78`, and the four dwords `+0x80`..`+0x8C`. `+0x7C` is the one dword it does not touch.

The last field written is `+0x8C`, so **CUnitPlan is 0x90 bytes**, which is exactly the room CUnit leaves between `+0x1FC` and `expeditionary_owner` at `+0x28C`.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::~CUnitPlan
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnitPlan::~CUnitPlan(CUnitPlan* this)
addresses.comment:
The plan's destructor: rewrites the vftable, frees the `vector<int>` at `+0x70` and clears `+0x70`/`+0x74`/`+0x78`, destroys the list at `+0x5C` and the one at `+0x48`, and walks the singly-linked nodes of the lists at `+0x38`, `+0x28` and `+0x18` freeing each through its `+0x8` link, resetting each head/tail/count triple as it goes. `this` is in ECX and it ends in a bare `ret`, so it takes nothing on the stack.

Called once, at `0x1B5799`, with `ecx = unit + 0x1FC` - CUnit's destructor destroying the plan it holds by value.

addresses.name: CUnit::ConstructPlanInPlace
addresses.comment: `lea eax, [edi + 0x1FC]; call CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan` inside CUnit's constructor (`0x1B5010`). **This is what settles that `CUnit +0x1FC` is a CUnitPlan held by value and not a pointer**: nothing is allocated, the plan is built in place at that offset, and the very next store is `expeditionary_owner` at `+0x28C`. The matching destruction is at `0x1B5799`.

addresses.name: CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute(void)
addresses.comment:
Slot 6 of `CSetGamePlayOptions` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`), and **the only thing in the image that writes either gameplay option**:

    gamestate->difficulty   = this->options[0]          // +0xC98
    if (this->options.size() >= 2)
        gamestate->arcade_mode = this->options[1]        // +0xC9C

The vector it carries is at `+0x3C`/`+0x40` and is what `CSetGamePlayOptions::LoadKey` (`0x2D5EC0`) fills from the save's `setgameplayoptions` key; the save writes it back under token `0x60D` at `0x2D5E90`. Since the command is only ever run when the game is set up or a save is loaded, both options are fixed for the length of a campaign.

It ends by touching the globals at `0x171042C`/`0x1710430` and `0x1A857F0`/`0x1A857F4`, which was not followed up.

addresses.name: g_CBuildingDataBase
addresses.comment:
The one `CBuildingDataBase`, 0x30 bytes, built lazily exactly as `g_CSubUnitDataBase` is: every user does `if (!g) g = new 0x30 bytes, init`. The init at rva `0x5BD30` is shared with 198 other databases and lays out the first 0x18 bytes - `+0x00`..`+0x0B` a name -> `CBuilding*` hash map (count at `+0x00`, `0x1FF` buckets at `+0x04`, the bucket array allocated and zeroed at `+0x08`) and `+0x0C`/`+0x10`/`+0x14` a `vector<CBuilding*>`. Everything from `+0x18` on is this class's own and the init does not touch it.

**Five of those six slots are cached `CBuilding*` for well-known roles**, filled by the loader at rva `0xB769B` (the defaults, all five pointed at the built-in 'nobuilding') and rva `0xB78AB` (the modifier ladder): `+0x1C` air_base, `+0x20` naval_base, `+0x24` anti_air, `+0x28` underground, `+0x2C` industry. The setup at `0x968B8`..`0x96A50` turns four of them into a province's building shortcuts,

    province->+0x308 = province->buildings[ db->+0x24->index ]
    province->+0x304 = province->buildings[ db->+0x1C->index ]
    province->+0x300 = province->buildings[ db->+0x20->index ]
    province->+0x30C = province->buildings[ db->+0x28->index ]

where `index` is `CBuilding +0x54` and `buildings` is `CProvince +0x310`.

**`+0x18` is the sixth slot and is dead.** It is the first dword the class adds on top of the shared 0x18-byte base, so it is a member rather than padding, but no instruction in the image writes or reads it: the init stops at `+0x14`, the loader's defaults set exactly the five role slots, and the ladder has exactly five branches. The object is `malloc`ed and never zeroed, so whatever stands at `+0x18` is heap garbage, not a building.

addresses.comment: The only combatant kind with a constructor the compiler did not inline. Everything travels in registers: `push eax; push esi; call CCombatant::CCombatant` forwards the flag and the object, ecx falls through untouched to the base. It then writes `[esi] = 0x11C4DFC` and zeroes three CLists - +0xB0/+0xB4/+0xB8/byte +0xBC, +0xC0.., +0xD0.. - and byte +0xE0, and returns this in eax. CLandCombatant::LoadKey (0x169040) names all three: +0xB0 is `front` (key 0x396), +0xC0 `reserves` (0x398) and +0xD0 `retreat` (0x1A6); it also sets byte +0xE0 to 1 on every call. The destructor at 0x168E40 walks and frees the nodes of all three through their +8 next pointers. The object is 0xE4 bytes.

Sets +0x04 = 0x18D, +0x08 = 0x11C0694 (the CSelectable base table) then 0x11C4F34 (CLandCombat's own), byte +0x0C = 0, +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 = 0 (attacker, defender, province all null at this point), +0x1C = -1 (day), +0x20..+0x40 = 0, +0x00 = 0x11C4EE4. addresses.name: CCountryTag::GetCountry
addresses.signature: CCountry* __thiscall CCountryTag::GetCountry(CCountryTag* this)
addresses.comment: **The tag -> country lookup the whole image goes through: 1295 direct call sites.** Five instructions, no branch, no call: `g_CCountryDataBase->countries_first[this->id]`. `mov eax,[ecx]` reads the four tag characters and `mov [esp],eax` stores them in a stack slot nothing reads again - the dead half of a by-value CCountryTag copy the optimiser flattened - so only `this->id` at +4 is used. It does not range-check the id and it does not check that g_CCountryDataBase is non-null.

addresses.name: floorf
addresses.signature: float __cdecl floorf(float x)
addresses.comment: **The `float` overload of `floor` from <math.h>**, emitted out of line: `return (float)floor((double)x)`. It widens the stack float to a double, calls `floor` (rva 0x8084B0) and narrows the result back, answering in st(0). Not a game function and nothing to do with clamping by itself - see `_ftol2_sse` for what it is paired with.

addresses.name: floor
addresses.signature: double __cdecl floor(double x)
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT `floor`, the SSE2 body, with an x87 fallback at 0xC09778 chosen by the `__use_sse2` style flag at VA 0x1BEC898. Takes the double on the x87 stack via the caller's push and answers in st(0). This is what `floorf` (rva 0x1FD0) calls.

addresses.name: _ftol2_sse
addresses.signature: int __cdecl _ftol2_sse(double value@ST0) @EAX
addresses.comment: **MSVC CRT `_ftol2_sse`, the float-to-integer conversion helper** - not a floor helper. It takes its argument on the x87 stack (nothing is pushed by the caller, which is why the signature has to say `@ST0`) and answers a truncated 32-bit integer in eax, via `cvttsd2si` when the `__sse2_available` flag at VA 0x1BEC9C0 is set. When it is not, it falls through to the x87 body at 0xC088A6, which is `_ftol2` proper and produces the full 64-bit result in edx:eax; that address has 26 direct callers of its own. The second entry point at 0xC0888C (`_ftol2_sse_excpt`, unreferenced here) is the control-word-checking variant. Paired with `floorf` at the sites the previous wave was describing: `CCountry::GetConvoyBuildTime`, `GetConvoyBuildCost` and `GetCategoryBuildDiscount` all do `floorf(10.5f)` then `_ftol2_sse()` and keep the larger of that and the computed value, which is the *at least 10* clamp - so the clamp reading was right about the effect and wrong about these two functions: neither is a floor helper, one is `floor` for floats and the other is `(int)`.

addresses.name: CStrategicRedeploymentOrder::RouteUnit_Thunk
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CStrategicRedeploymentOrder::RouteUnit_Thunk(CStrategicRedeploymentOrder* this) @AL
addresses.comment:
CStrategicRedeploymentOrder vftable **slot 13** - the virtual that dispatches to the re-route. Five instructions and nothing else: `push edi; mov edi,ecx; call CStrategicRedeploymentOrder::RouteUnit; pop edi; ret`. It exists because the compiler gave the body a register calling convention (the order in edi) and the table needs an ordinary `__thiscall` entry. The bool comes straight back in al.

Slot 13 is `_purecall` on COrder itself, so every concrete order supplies its own: CMoveOrder 0x187B00, CAirOrder 0x18A790, CSupportAttackOrder 0x187FB0. Those are not named here - only this one is known to route.

addresses.name: CBuildingDataBase_RoleByModifierId
addresses.no_signature: a single instruction inside a larger function, not a function entry, so it has no calling convention of its own
addresses.comment: The building-role ladder in the building-database loader. eax = building->+0xC, the CModifier the building's one modifier key mapped to, then five compares of the modifier id at CModifier +0x24: 0x2E MODIFIER_AIR_CAPACITY -> db +0x1C, 0x2D MODIFIER_NAVAL_CAPACITY -> db +0x20, 0x4B MODIFIER_LOCAL_AA -> db +0x24, 0x0F MODIFIER_IC -> db +0x2C, 0x66 MODIFIER_LOCAL_UNDERGROUND -> db +0x28. In vanilla and in BlackICE that is air_base, naval_base, anti_air, industry and underground. It is an if/else ladder with no break, so where two buildings carry the same modifier the last one parsed takes the slot. The defaults are set at rva 0xB769B, which points all five slots at the built-in 'nobuilding'.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase_RoleByKey
addresses.no_signature: a single instruction inside a larger function, not a function entry, so it has no calling convention of its own
addresses.comment: Start of the 33-way key chain in the sub-unit loader at rva 0x1AE1C0. Each step compares the definition's key against one hardcoded literal - the contiguous block 0x15C7750..0x15C794C, infantry_brigade through carrier - and on a match stores the definition pointer into one fixed slot of CSubUnitDataBase between +0x2C and +0xAC. The cached block is 33 slots, not 34: nothing in this function or anywhere else writes +0x28 through the database.

addresses.name: CProvince_StorePort
addresses.no_signature: a single instruction inside a larger function, not a function entry, so it has no calling convention of its own
addresses.comment: mov [ecx+0x354], eax - the only place a CProvince's CPort is set. ecx is the land province looked up out of the map's province array, eax a new 0x1C-byte CPort whose +0x18 holds the adjacent sea province id. Runs at map load, once per land-to-sea adjacency.

addresses.name: RunDailySupplyPass
addresses.signature: void __stdcall RunDailySupplyPass(CCurrentGameState* state)
addresses.comment: Builds the four per-province arrays CSupply::DailySupplyPass takes and calls it. Returns at once when CCurrentGameState::arcade_mode (+0xC9C) is above zero. Allocates four count*4 arrays on the stack (count = (provinces_end - provinces_begin)/4), memsets them to zero, and for every province whose CProvinceTemplate +0x13D is set fills capacity from SupplyCapacity, supplies and fuel need from SupplyNeed and the per-step loss from SupplyLoss. The loop keeps a moving pointer into the fuel-need array in edi - which is also SupplyNeed's second out parameter - and reaches the other three arrays through precomputed deltas off it. One caller, 0x282D7E inside 0x282630, which takes the game state as its own argument. Named for what it does; no class, like SupplyCapacity, SupplyNeed and SupplyLoss beside it.

addresses.name: NavalBaseCapacity
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall NavalBaseCapacity(CMapProvince* province, int* out@ESI)
addresses.comment: How much a province's naval base can move in a day, in thousandths, written through an out pointer in ESI and also returned. Computes `naval_base->level_current * defines->supply(+0xAC)(+0x274) / 1000`, caching that define in the global at 0x1BEBAB8 behind the flag at 0x1BEBABC, then scales it by `(1000 + controller->modifier.NAVAL_BASE_EFFICIENCY + controller->+0xDF8(+0x7C)) / 1000`. The daily supply pass uses it in phase 3 as the ceiling on what a depot can ship home by convoy. Twenty callers in all, so the name describes what it computes rather than any one use.

addresses.name: CConvoy::GetEfficiency
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CConvoy::GetEfficiency(CConvoy* this, int* out)
addresses.comment: The fraction of a convoy route that is actually running, in thousandths, written through out and also returned. Defaults to 1000, then becomes `transports (+0x98) * 1000 * 1000 / (transports wanted * 1000)` where a helper at 0xC7320 supplies the wanted figure, and is multiplied by +0xAC / 1000 - an unnamed field, most likely the lend-lease efficiency the defines call LL_CONVOY_EFF_IMPACT - when is_lend_lease (+0xA1) is set. The daily supply pass multiplies a depot's NavalBaseCapacity by it once per convoy that ends at the depot.

addresses.name: CBuilding::CBuilding
addresses.signature: CBuilding* __stdcall CBuilding::CBuilding(CBuilding* this, Hoi3CString name, int unread, int index)
addresses.comment:
Builds one building definition. Writes CBuilding's own vftable 0x11C09F8 at +0, takes its name as an Hoi3CString by value - 0x1C bytes at [ebp+0xC], which is why the ret is 36 and not 12 - and stores the last argument into index at +0x54.

Recorded mainly so the building-database loader types itself: without a return type the buildings come back as int* and the role ladder's five modifier comparisons stay bare numbers however well CModifier and CBuilding are typed.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::CreateCombat
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCombatManager::CreateCombat(CCombatManager* manager, CMapProvince* province, int kind, CUnit* attacker, CUnit* defender)
addresses.comment:
The live combat factory - where a combat starts in a running game, as opposed to CCombatManager::LoadKey's path out of a save. `ret 0x14`, five stack arguments, nothing in ecx.

A jump table at 0x431604 on `kind - 1` covers 1..6 and every arm is the same three instructions: `operator new(0x44)`, the kind's own constructor, `edi = the new combat`, `jmp 0x43141F`. 1 CLandCombat (0x17B480), 2 CNavalCombat (0x17B720), 3 CAirCombat (0x17BB50), 4 CGroundBombing (0x2FE20), 5 CLandBombing (0x2FE70), 6 CNavalBombing (0x2FEC0). A failed allocation sets edi = 0 and joins the same tail.

The common tail, with edi the combat and esi the manager:

    CCombatManager::AddCombat(manager, combat)      0x2FFC0
    combat->slot 6 ()                               CreateCombatants
    combat->SetProvince(province)                   slot 16
    if (kind == 4)                                  ground bombing only
        push the province's controller tag+id (province +0x334/+0x338, 8 bytes)
        into combat->defender->countries (+0x54/+0x58/+0x5C)
    combat->attacker->slot 12 (attacker);  0x5BFE80;  if (!combat->slot 8 ()) 0x5C7970(attacker, 1)
    if (defender)
        combat->defender->slot 12 (defender); 0x5BFE80; if (!combat->slot 8 ()) 0x5C7970(defender, 0)
    for each unit in province->units (+0x2B8)
        skip it if it is the attacker or the defender, and, for a bombing,
        only offer it when slot 8 and the unit's own tests agree
        combat->AddUnit(unit)                       slot 18
    if the attacker's +0xB0 object passes slot 0x6C, walk province +0x354's list
        the same way and offer those units too
    if (combat->slot 8 ())   province->+0x2FC = combat, if it was null
    else                     CMapProvince::AddCombat(province, combat)   into province +0x2EC

Slot 8 is `xor al,al; ret` on CCombat and `mov al,1; ret` on all three bombings, so the last two lines read: a bombing goes in the province's single +0x2FC slot, an ordinary combat onto the province's +0x2EC list. Both bodies are linker-folded, so neither is named here.

**The default arm is dead code, and the reading `(manager, province, kind, attacker, defender)` stands.** The arms all jump to 0x43141F; 0x43141C is three bytes of its own - `mov edi,[ebp+0xC]` - reached only by the `ja` at 0x43137F, that is only when `kind` is outside 1..6. Both callers are exhaustive: CCombatManager::StartCombat sets its kind slot to 1, 2 or 3 on every path that reaches the call, and CCombatManager::StartBombing to 4, 5 or 6, checked off cfg.py's edge lists into 0x430883/0x43093F and 0x430467/0x430474. And the arm is not a second calling convention: arg2 is the province by three independent reads - SetProvince stores it in CCombat +0x18 and its terrain in +0x24, the kind-4 block reads its controller tag at +0x334, and both callers read +0xD4, +0x2B8 and +0x2FC off the same value - so running that arm would call CCombat virtuals on a CMapProvince. It is what MSVC emitted for a `combat` variable left undefined when the switch matched nothing.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::AddCombat
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCombatManager::AddCombat(CCombatManager* manager@ESI, CCombat* combat@EAX)
addresses.comment: Links a new 0x10-byte node { combat, previous, next, byte } into the manager's live-combat list (first at +0x08, last at +0x0C, count at +0x10). It calls the combat's slot 8 first and pushes to the front when that is true - the three bombings - and to the back otherwise. A failed `operator new(0x10)` stores a null node pointer and still bumps the count. Called only from CCombatManager::CreateCombat and CCombatManager::LoadKey.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::StartCombat
addresses.signature: int __stdcall CCombatManager::StartCombat(CCombatManager* manager, CMapProvince* province, CUnit* unit) @EAX
addresses.comment:
Decides whether `unit` starts an ordinary combat in `province` and, if so, which kind, then calls CCombatManager::CreateCombat. Returns the kind it created - 1 land, 2 naval, 3 air - or 0 for none; the kind lives in one stack slot that is zeroed at 0x4307C4 and is also the return value on every early exit.

It walks the province's units (+0x2B8) for an enemy, then: the enemy unit's slot 17 true gives **3**; otherwise the province's terrain record (+0xD4) with a nonzero byte at +0x22 gives **1**; otherwise **2**, but only when the attacker's own slot 11 result passes 0x431840 and its +0x40 is at least 1. Before creating, 0x4A6010 refuses a second combat of the same kind in the province.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::StartBombing
addresses.signature: int __stdcall CCombatManager::StartBombing(CCombatManager* manager, CMapProvince* province, CUnit* unit) @EAX
addresses.comment:
The bombing half of the same decision, with the same three arguments and the same return - the kind it created, 4 ground bombing, 5 land bombing, 6 naval bombing, or 0 for none.

**4** when the province's terrain byte (+0xD4, +0x22) is set, the bomber's +0xB0 object passes slot 0x68, and 0x42F1B0 says the province's controller (+0x334/+0x338) is hostile to the bomber's owner (+0x124) - that is, a raid on the province itself, with no enemy unit needed. Otherwise it walks the province's units for a target and takes **5 or 6** from the target's slot 16: `setne cl; add ecx,5` at 0x43045D, so a target that answers true is 6 and one that answers false is 5. Either way it gives up if province->+0x2FC already holds a bombing.

addresses.name: CCombat::SetProvince
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCombat::SetProvince(CCombat* this, CMapProvince* province)
addresses.comment: Six instructions: `this->province (+0x18) = province; this->terrain (+0x24) = province->+0xD4->+0x0C`. Slot 16, inherited unchanged by all six combat kinds. This is the call that gives CCombatManager::CreateCombat's second argument its type, and it is what puts the province the CCombatHistoryEntry constructor later reads +0xD0 off.

addresses.name: CCombat::AddUnit
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CCombat::AddUnit(CCombat* this, CUnit* unit) @AL
addresses.comment:
Slot 18. Offers a unit to a combat that already exists and lets the combat pick the side:

    a = this->attacker->slot 17 (unit)
    d = this->defender->slot 17 (unit)
    if (d && !a)   attacker->slot 12 (unit); 0x5BFE80; if (!this->slot 8 ()) 0x5C7970(unit, 1); return true
    if (a && !d)   defender->slot 12 (unit); 0x5BFE80; if (!this->slot 8 ()) 0x5C7970(unit, 0); return true
    return false

so a unit joins the side the *other* side is hostile to, and a unit both sides or neither side object to is refused. The defender branch has two extra gates for bombings - the unit's own slot 17 and the global test at 0x5CDC30. CCombatManager::CreateCombat calls this for every bystander in the province; the same body is slot 18 in all six combat classes.

addresses.name: CMapProvince::AddCombat
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CMapProvince::AddCombat(CMapProvince* province@ESI, CCombat* combat@stack:4)
addresses.comment: Appends the combat to the province's combat list - first at +0x2EC, last at +0x2F0, count at +0x2F4, 0x10-byte nodes { combat, previous, next, byte } - unless a node already holds it. A failed `operator new(0x10)` stores a null and still bumps the count. Two callers: CCombatManager::CreateCombat's tail and 0x16E360, both under the same `if (!combat->slot 8 ())`.

addresses.name: CMapProvince::HasCombatOfKind
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CMapProvince::HasCombatOfKind(CMapProvince* province@EAX, int kind@EDI) @AL
addresses.comment: Walks province->combats (+0x2EC) and returns true as soon as one combat's slot 11 equals `kind`. Eleven instructions, bare `ret`, both arguments in registers. CCombatManager::StartCombat calls it to refuse a second land, naval or air combat of the same kind in one province.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::CBomberCombatant
addresses.signature: CBomberCombatant* __stdcall CBomberCombatant::CBomberCombatant(CBomberCombatant* this, CCombat* combat@ECX) @EAX
addresses.comment:
`ret 4` - `this` on the stack, the combat in ecx untouched so that CCombatant::CCombatant can store it at +0x3C. It runs the base with the attacker flag hardwired to 1, writes its own vftable 0x11C45DC, and then builds three vectors of its own:

    +0x10B4  one int per **building definition**, from g_CBuildingDataBase
    +0x10C4  seven ints
    +0x10D4  seven ints
    +0x10E4  int, 0

The first loop is the same lazy-singleton-and-fill the base constructor does for the subunit database, but on a different global: it creates g_CBuildingDataBase inline if it is null (0x30 bytes, 0x1FF buckets) and then pushes one zero per entry of that database's definition vector, count `([db+0x10] - [db+0x0C]) / 4`. So a bomber combatant carries a tally indexed by building type - which is what a strategic raid needs and what nothing else in the combatant family has. The second loop pushes seven zeros into each of +0x10C4 and +0x10D4 and is a plain `for (i = 0; i < 7; ++i)`, not a database count.

The object is 0x10E8 bytes and, like CAirCombatant and CNavalCombatant, leaves +0xB0..+0x10B3 untouched - see CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets for what that region is.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets(CNavalCombatant* this, CNavalCombatant* out, CSubUnit* attacker)
addresses.comment:
**This is what the ~0x1000 unwritten bytes are.** The function clears `out->+0x10B0` to 0, walks `this->units` (+0x40) and each unit's subunits (CUnit +0x38), and for every subunit that passes its filters does

    out->[0xB0 + count * 4] = subunit;  ++out->+0x10B0

So a naval, air or bomber combatant carries a fixed array of **1024 `CSubUnit*` at +0xB0 with its count at +0x10B0**: 0xB0 + 1024 * 4 = 0x10B0, and the count dword ends at 0x10B4, which is exactly where all three classes' own fields start. It is scratch - the count is reset on every call, nothing initialises it at construction and no LoadKey or SaveContents touches it - which is why the constructors leave the region alone. 0x1675D0 then picks one entry with `random % count` (`idiv [ebx+0x10B0]` at 0x5678CC) as the target of one attack.

CLandCombatant does not have it: that class is 0xE4 bytes and uses +0xB0 for its `front` list. There is no bounds check on the append.

addresses.name: CAirCombatant::CollectTargets
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CAirCombatant::CollectTargets(CAirCombatant* out@stack:4, CAirCombatant* enemy@EAX)
addresses.comment: The air twin of CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets and the second witness for the +0xB0 array. `ret 4`, the source combatant in eax: it clears `out->+0x10B0`, walks `enemy->units` (+0x40) and their subunits, and appends each candidate at `out->[0xB0 + count*4]`. It takes no attacking subunit, so the filtering is simpler than the naval one. 0x16D620 picks from the result with `random % count` and 0x16D500 walks the whole array.

addresses.name: LoadDefines
addresses.signature: void __stdcall LoadDefines(CDefines* defines)
addresses.comment: Fills `CDefines` from the parsed `common/defines.lua`. One unrolled run of 396 loads, each of them `mov <reg>, [defines + <block>]`, `push "<KEY>"`, `call` the reader, `mov [<reg> + <offset>], eax` - so **every define is looked up by name and stored at an offset compiled into this function**. A mod cannot move a define by reordering the file; a key the file does not define goes unreported and stores 0, because the reader's type check fails; a key the file defines that this function never pushes is never read at all, which is what BlackICE's PRIDE_SUNK_DISSENT_IMPACT, WHITESEA, WHITESEA_BLOCKER and GFX_RAINIMPACT_LIMIT are. The eight blocks hang off CDefines +0x9C, +0xAC, +0xBC, +0xCC, +0xDC, +0xEC, +0xFC and +0x10C. `reversing/definesMap.py` reads the whole map back out of this function.

addresses.name: ReadDefineThousandths
addresses.signature: int* __cdecl ReadDefineThousandths(int* out, void* block, const char** key)
addresses.comment: Looks `key` up in a parsed defines block and writes `(int)((value + 0.0005) * 1000)` to `*out`, or 0 where the key is missing or the entry is not a number - the type tag is compared against 3. Returns `out`, which is why every call site reads the value back with `mov eax, [eax]`. This is where thousandths come from: every numeric define in defines.lua is stored x1000, rounded.

addresses.name: ReadDefineInt
addresses.signature: int __cdecl ReadDefineInt(void* block, const char** key)
addresses.comment: The unscaled sibling of `ReadDefineThousandths`: same lookup, same type check against 3, but it returns the number as a plain int. Used only for the `map` block of defines.lua, whose entries are province ids.

addresses.name: CSubUnit_GetMaxStrength_ReservesPenaltyValue
addresses.comment: `mov ecx,[edx+0x268]` - the reserve penalty itself: entry 77 of the owner's global modifier values, RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE, in thousandths. edx came from `mov edx,[eax+0xda8]` one instruction earlier, which is CCountry +0xD90 global_modifier plus CModifier +0x18 values. The next instruction adds 1000 to it, so -500 here halves a reserve subunit's max strength.

addresses.name: ProvinceSeaHopCheck_OwnerIdTest
addresses.comment: `cmp dword ptr [edi+0x330], 0` - **not a field of its own**: +0x330 is the `id` half of the CCountryTag at CProvince +0x32C, so this is `province->owner.id != 0`, the province is owned by somebody. CCountryDataBase::GetTag hands back `---` with id 0 where there is none. It is the second of four tests in this gate: the path node's +0x22 byte at 0x1CEE9A, this one, `+0x354` (the CPort*) at 0x1CEEAD and `naval_base->level_max(+0x20) > 0` at 0x1CEEBC.

addresses.name: ProvinceNavalBaseCheck_OwnerIdTest
addresses.comment: `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x330], 0` - the same test as the sea-hop gate's, on the same field: +0x330 is the `id` half of CProvince +0x32C `owner`, so it asks whether the province is owned at all. The function it opens (0xA7EE0, reached from 0x81AC1 and 0x81AD0) writes `province->naval_base->level_current` (+0x24) through the out pointer in edi unconditionally, and then **zeroes it again** at 0xA7F6C only where every gate passes: owner.id non-zero, the port at +0x354 non-null, `naval_base->level_max` (+0x20) > 0, a match on the adjacent sea province through the path node at +0xD4, and a true from the call at 0xA7F61. Any gate that fails leaves the level standing.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan_Ctor_ZeroesUnnamed58
addresses.comment:
`mov [eax+0x58], ecx` in CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan, with ecx zero - and, with the `mov [eax+0x6c], ecx` at 0x4DEA34, **the only write to either field in any CUnitPlan method**. The constructor lays the object out as: vftable, 0x18D at +4, the two bytes at +8, stances 2/1/1 at +0xC/+0x10/+0x14, four CLists (+0x18, +0x28, +0x38, +0x48), **an unnamed dword at +0x58**, a fifth CList at +0x5C, **an unnamed dword at +0x6C**, the `min` vector's three pointers (+0x70, +0x74, +0x78), then +0x80..+0x8C. It never touches +0x7C at all.

What is known about the three: the destructor frees nothing at any of them, so none is a pointer the plan owns; CUnitPlan::SetActive (the reset, 0x4DEB10) clears every list, the vector and +0x80..+0x8C and leaves all three alone; the applier at 0x1D0F00 copies active, stance, ops_area, objectives, path, path2, min, our_power and their_power from one plan to another and copies none of them; and LoadKey (0x4DF720) and SaveContents (0x4DF160) never mention them, so nothing about them reaches a savegame or the network. They are runtime-only, unread by the class itself, and cannot be named from the executable alone.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit(CUnitPlan* source@EAX, CUnit* unit)

In order: CUnitPlan::SetActive(dest, source->active), `unit->plan_stance(+0x208) = source->stance`, then CopyOpsArea, CopyObjectives, CopyPath, CopyPath2 and SetMinForces from the source's +0x18, +0x38, +0x48, +0x5C and +0x70, then our_power and their_power into CUnit +0x27C/+0x280. **What it does not copy is as informative as what it does**: the fallback line (+0x28), embark and debark (+0x88/+0x8C) and the three unnamed fields (+0x58, +0x6C, +0x7C) are all left as the reset left them. addresses.name: SaveWriteFixed
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteFixed(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@EDI, int thousandths@stack:4)
addresses.comment: **Not SaveWriteInt.** Writes `<key>=<n>.<nnn>` and a newline for a value the game holds in thousandths: SaveWriteKey, then a CToken, then SaveWriteToken(tok_newline). In a text save it hands the int to MakeFixedToken, which formats it `%d.%03d` as tok_fixed (0xD); in a binary save (writer->binary set) it formats the raw int `%d` as tok_int (0xC) instead, so no precision is lost either way. The writer arrives in EDI, not ESI as in the plain-int sibling at 0x678CA0 - the compiler picked a register per function, so the call sites decide.

addresses.name: SaveWriteBool
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteBool(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, bool value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: Writes `<key>=yes` or `<key>=no` and a newline. SaveWriteKey, then a tok_bool (0xE) CToken whose text is `%s` of the literal `yes` at VA 0x15C1914 or `no` at 0x15C1918, then SaveWriteToken(tok_newline). There is no binary branch: the word goes out as a tok_bool either way, and it is SaveWriteValue that decides how a tok_bool is encoded.

addresses.name: SaveWriteString
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteString(Hoi3CString* value@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@stack:4)
addresses.comment: Writes a **quoted string value and a newline - it writes no key**, so the caller does SaveWriteKey first and this is the right half of `owner="NOR"`. In a text save it builds `"` + the string + `"` with std::string::operatorPlus and the one-character literal at VA 0x15E14F8, formats it `%s` into a tok_word (0xF) CToken and calls SaveWriteValue; in a binary save it copies the string unquoted into the same tok_word and writes that. Then SaveWriteToken(tok_newline) on both paths. The most-called member of the family: 281 direct calls.

addresses.name: SaveWriteInt
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteInt(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, int value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: The real `<key>=<int>` writer, and the sibling 0x678B70 was mistaken for: SaveWriteKey, a tok_int (0xC) CToken formatted `%d`, SaveWriteValue, SaveWriteToken(tok_newline). No binary branch - an integer is an integer in both formats. Only four call sites, because most integer keys are written by hand as SaveWriteKey + SaveWriteValue inside the SaveContents itself.

addresses.name: SaveWriteUInt
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteUInt(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, unsigned int value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: SaveWriteInt's unsigned twin: identical body but `%u` at VA 0x15FD128 and the CToken type word tok_uint (0x14) rather than tok_int (0xC). One call site in the image.

addresses.name: SaveWriteKeyString
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteKeyString(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, Hoi3CString* value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: The two halves of `<key>="<text>"` in one call: SaveWriteKey followed by SaveWriteString. Seventeen call sites; everywhere else the SaveContents calls the two separately because it has to build the string first.

addresses.name: SaveWriteKeyToken
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteKeyToken(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, SaveToken value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: Writes `<key>=<word>` where the value is itself a save token written by its own text - an enum member spelled out, the way `automate_trade=yes` or a named mode is. SaveWriteKey, SaveWriteToken(value), SaveWriteToken(tok_newline).

addresses.name: SaveWriteNamedFixed
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteNamedFixed(Hoi3CString* key@EAX, CSaveWriter* writer@EDI, int thousandths@stack:4)
addresses.comment: SaveWriteFixed for a key that is not a token: the key is a runtime string, so it open-codes what SaveWriteKey does - indent by depth-1, write the name as a tok_word, write tok_equals - and then writes the value exactly as SaveWriteFixed does, `%d.%03d` as tok_fixed in a text save and `%d` as tok_int in a binary one, followed by a newline. This is how a save writes rows keyed by a moddable name rather than by a built-in token.

addresses.name: MakeFixedToken
addresses.signature: CToken* __cdecl MakeFixedToken(int* value@EAX, CToken* out@ESI) @EAX
addresses.comment: Builds a tok_fixed (0xD) CToken in the caller's buffer from a thousandths integer: divides by 1000, formats `%d.%03d`, and handles a value between -999 and 0 by writing the sign separately (`-%d.%03d` at VA 0x15FD138) so that -1 comes out `-0.001` rather than `0.-001`. This is the one place the game's thousandths convention becomes text. Returns the buffer in EAX.

addresses.name: CSupply::ResetSupplyOrder
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSupply::ResetSupplyOrder(CCurrentGameState* state@EAX)
addresses.comment: Refills provinces_by_supply_order (+0x54) from the province vector (+0xB8C..+0xB90), one pointer per province in province-id order. The whole body is a single copy loop. Called at 0x282CF8 immediately before the qsort at 0x282D18 that puts the array in farthest-from-depot order, and at 0x27E537 right after +0x54's storage is allocated at 0x27E52A as count*4 bytes.

addresses.name: CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork(CCurrentGameState* state@ESI)
addresses.comment: Recomputes every province's supply_depot_distance. Clears the dirty flag at CCurrentGameState +0x50, then sweeps the province vector: supply_depot_hops (+0x50) is zeroed, and supply_depot_distance (+0x4C) is set to 100000 where the province already carries a depot label and its template's +0x13D is set, and to 0 otherwise. A second sweep calls CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0) for every province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id - that is what makes a province a depot. It never writes supply_depot_id; that is CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0). Reached from CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x25C611, after the loop there has given every unlabelled province a depot, and from 0x282630 at 0x2826E8 and 0x282CEF, each guarded on CCurrentGameState +0x50.

addresses.name: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSupply::SpreadFromDepot(CCurrentGameState* state@stack:4, int depot@stack:8, int depotIndex@EDX)
addresses.comment: The distance relaxation, one depot at a time. Sets the depot's own supply_depot_distance to 0, then works a FIFO queue of 0x10-byte nodes over the template's ProvinceEdge vector (+0x90..+0x94, stride 0x14, neighbour id at edge+4). A neighbour is considered only if its template's +0x13D is set and its supply_depot_id already equals `depot` - the label partitions the map and this only fills in distances inside one partition. The step cost is infrastructure-weighted, not a hop: infra = provinceModifier[MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE] * (1000 + [MODIFIER_LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE] + [MODIFIER_GLOBAL_INFRASTRUCTURE]) / 1000, clamped below by a lazily computed constant at rva 0x17EA400 (from the float 10.5 at rva 0x120A680) and above by 1000; then step = max(4000 - 4*infra, 1000) / 1000, an integer 1..4, multiplied by the neighbour's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. The neighbour is relaxed only when its current distance is strictly greater, and it then also gets supply_depot_hops = parent's hops + 1. The queue is a CList by value on the stack - three dwords and a byte cleared together at 0x689C0F - and its nodes are CListNode<CMapProvince*>; the `locals` on this record are what make the body read in terms of the province rather than `*(iVar3 + 0x4c)`.

locals.name: frontier
locals.comment: head of the queue of provinces still to relax

locals.name: frontierTail
locals.comment: last node, so a push can link onto it

locals.name: frontierCount
locals.comment: how many are queued; the loop runs until it reaches zero

addresses.name: CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending
addresses.signature: int __cdecl CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending(CMapProvince** a, CMapProvince** b)
addresses.comment: The qsort comparator for provinces_by_supply_order. Returns +1 when b's supply_depot_distance is the larger, 0 when equal, -1 otherwise - a descending sort on +0x4C, so element 0 is the province farthest from its depot. This is the derivation of the 'farthest first' in CCurrentGameState::provinces_by_supply_order's name, which CSupply::DailySupplyPass's single forward sweep depends on.

addresses.name: SupplyOrder_CallQsort
addresses.comment: qsort(state->provinces_by_supply_order, provinceCount, 4, CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending) - the one place the supply order array is sorted. The instructions after it read back element 0's supply_depot_distance into CCurrentGameState +0x58, clamp it to 500, and where it exceeded 500 re-run CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot on that farthest province.

addresses.name: CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot(CProvince* this)
addresses.comment: Assigns this province's supply_depot_id - the supply network's label - and marks the network dirty. Does nothing unless the owner's country id (+0x330) is non-zero and the area at +0x2B4 answers true to its virtual slot 0 (CNullOwnerArea does not). The area gets first refusal: where area+0x70 is non-null and either (area+0x70)+8 is above 1 or area+0x69 is 1, a non-zero (area+0x70)+0x10 becomes the label. Otherwise the label comes from CCountry::FindSupplyDepot (0xF2B00) called on the controller's country. Afterwards out_of_supply_days (+0x20) is incremented when the label came out 0 and zeroed when it did not, and g_CCurrentGameState +0x50 is set to 1 so the next tick rebuilds the distances. Called per province from CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x25C557 for every province still carrying label 0, from 0x282D3B on the farthest province when its distance exceeded 500, and from 0x9EF5B, 0xA3546 and 0xB8279.

addresses.name: CCountry::FindSupplyDepot
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CCountry::FindSupplyDepot(CCountry* this, CProvince* province, void* visited, CCountry* origin)
addresses.comment: Answers the province id that a province should draw supply from, or 0. Returns the origin country's acting_capital_province_id (CCountry +0xE24) once the province's area matches that of the origin's own acting capital, and otherwise recurses into the countries reached through the area's list at +0x34 and through +0xF34/+0xF38 on the country, carrying the same origin and a visited list so the walk terminates. `origin` defaults to `this` when it is passed null. This is what makes two provinces share a supply_depot_id: they resolve to the same acting capital.

addresses.name: CEU3BitmapFont::Load
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CEU3BitmapFont::Load(CEU3BitmapFont* this)
addresses.comment:
**Loads the font**, virtual slot 5. Builds `gfx/fonts/` + `fontName` + `.tga`, loads that texture, then calls CEU3BitmapFont::LoadGlyphs for the `.fnt` beside it.

**It and LoadGlyphs have no padding between them**, so reversing/image.py's functionStart answers 0x6F9EA0 for addresses in either. The frames tell them apart: this one reserves 0x58 bytes and the parser 0x1B4, and the parser addresses [ebp - 0x1C0], which this frame could not hold.

addresses.name: CEU3BitmapFont::LoadGlyphs
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CEU3BitmapFont::LoadGlyphs(CEU3BitmapFont* font)
addresses.comment:
**Reads `gfx/fonts/<fontName>.fnt` into the font's glyph table.** The file is an AngelCode BMFont descriptor in plain text, and this **never reads its key names**: it matches only the first token of a line - `char` at 0x6FA2E3, `kerning` at 0x6FA4AC - and then takes the numbers after it in file order, one atoi each.

`char` gives id, x, y, width, height, xoffset, yoffset, xadvance, in that order, into a fresh 0x820 byte CEU3BitmapFontGlyph stored at `font + id * 4 + 0x94`. An id of 0x20 has its height forced to zero at 0x6FA3BD whatever the file says. `kerning` gives first, second, amount, and appends {second, amount} to the glyph named first.

That the parse is positional is why `xadvance` appears nowhere in the executable, and why the numbers in the .fnt are the ones the renderer advances by.

No `this`: the font arrives as the single stack argument and the ECX the caller had is unused, so it is __stdcall despite living on the class.

addresses.name: CEU3BitmapFont::GetStringWidth
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CEU3BitmapFont::GetStringWidth(CEU3BitmapFont* this, const char* text, int length)
addresses.comment:
**How wide a string draws, in pixels**, virtual slot 10. A negative `length` means to the NUL.

Each byte adds its glyph's xadvance and then the kerning pair between it and **the literal next byte** - the game does not skip an escape to find the next drawn character. A glyph the font does not list adds nothing.

The escapes: 0xA7 and the byte after it are skipped, but only where the virtual at +0x4C says this font handles them; 0x40 takes three bytes and adds an icon width from the virtual at +0x68; 0xA3 takes a [A-Za-z_] name and adds one from +0x64; 0xA4 adds a flat 8; `{` adds 8 and takes two bytes.

A newline ends a line rather than the string, and the return is the widest line.

BiceLib's Text::Font follows all of this except the icon escapes, which it measures as ordinary glyphs because nothing it writes contains one.

addresses.name: UpdateMapCamera
addresses.no_signature: Four stack arguments - it ends `ret 0x10` - **and** two objects in registers: the camera arrives in ESI and the mouse in EDI, both read before the prologue has finished. Under custom storage every parameter has to be placed or none does, and two of the four stack arguments have not been identified, so placing the rest would be a guess dressed as a fact.
addresses.comment:
**Moves the map camera, once a frame.** ESI is the camera (a MapCamera, which lives at CInGameIdler +0x1938), EDI the object the mouse position is asked of, and the first stack argument the one key states are asked of.

In order: dragging with the middle button, which works through the map projection rather than the screen; the arrow keys, tested as VK_LEFT, VK_UP, VK_RIGHT and VK_DOWN through the key object's +0x24; **the four screen edge tests at 0x23CE97** (see MapEdgeScrollTests); then clamping the result to the camera's limits.

Read for the parts named; the zoom and rotation arithmetic around them has not been followed.

addresses.name: MapEdgeScrollTests
addresses.comment:
**Where the map starts scrolling because the mouse is against the edge of the screen**, and where BiceLib stops it.

Four tests in a row, one per edge, each the same shape: ask EDI for the mouse position, compare one coordinate against one of the camera's edges give or take six pixels, and move the camera if it is past it.

    mov  edx, [edi]              ; the mouse object's vftable
    mov  edx, [edx + 0x4C]       ; its "where is the mouse"
    lea  eax, [esp + 0x24]
    push eax
    mov  ecx, edi
    call edx
    mov  ecx, [esi + 0x328]      ; edge_top, then bottom, left, right
    add  ecx, 6
    cmp  [eax + 4], ecx
    jge  <past it>

They run from here to **0x23CFB5**, where the camera is clamped, with nothing else in between - so a five byte jump from the first to the last removes all four and leaves the keyboard and the drag alone. The two instructions it replaces are exactly five bytes.

**Every branch that enters the range lands on this first byte** - five of them, with the only others being each test skipping itself - which is what makes jumping over the whole run safe. Checked with `reversing/cfg.py --lands-in 0x63ce97 0x63cfb5`.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::GetMapCamera
addresses.signature: MapCamera* __thiscall CInGameIdler::GetMapCamera(CInGameIdler* this)
addresses.comment: Virtual slot 28. The whole body is `lea eax, [ecx + 0x1938]; ret` - the camera is held by value inside the idler, so this hands back its address rather than a pointer it stores.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::CentreOnProvince
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CInGameIdler::CentreOnProvince(CInGameIdler* this, CMapProvince* province)
addresses.comment:
**Puts the camera on a province**, virtual slot 48. What the unit panel's `unit_location_button` ends up calling, and so what its `w` shortcut does.

Takes the map position off the province's **path node** (`CMapProvince +0xD4`), whose x and y are at its +0x5C and +0x60, converts both to float, and writes them to the camera got from GetMapCamera. It writes `x` and `y` and then copies each into `x_settled` and `y_settled`, which is what makes the move immediate rather than something the camera eases into.

fields.name: max_supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: the largest supply_depot_distance on the map, taken from element 0 of provinces_by_supply_order right after the sort and clamped to 500. It is not the end pointer of the +0x54 vector - +0x54's storage is a plain new[] at 0x27E52A and its length is recomputed from the province vector everywhere it is walked. Where the raw value exceeded 500 the game also re-runs CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot on that farthest province, which is how a province cut off at 100000 gets a fresh depot label.

fields.name: supply_network_dirty
fields.comment: set to 1 whenever CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot changes a province's supply depot label, and cleared by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork; the two rebuild sites in 0x282630 are both `cmp byte [state+0x50], 0; je` around the call

fields.name: arcade_mode
fields.comment:
The lobby's **Game Mode**: 0 Normal, 1 Arcade. Element 1 of the save's `setgameplayoptions` vector, written only by `CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute` (0x2D5D20), so it is set once when the game is started or loaded. CCurrentGameState's constructor defaults it to 0.

**This is the switch between the two supply models.** `CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel` tests it at 0x1BBA3A: above zero the unit draws straight from the owner's capital pool (`CProvince +0x15C`), at or below zero it walks the supply network. Twenty-odd other sites read it the same way. Measured live it reads 0, and every save in `BlackICE GitHub/save games` writes `{ 2 0 }`, so the network path is the one that runs in an ordinary campaign.

fields.name: difficulty
fields.comment: The campaign's difficulty, 0..4 (`VERY_EASY`, `EASY`, `NORMAL`, `HARD`, `VERY_HARD` in the localisation). Element 0 of the save's `setgameplayoptions` vector, written only by `CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute` (0x2D5D20) and so fixed for the game. CCurrentGameState's constructor defaults it to 2, Normal, and every save read here carries `setgameplayoptions = { 2 0 }`.

fields.name: in_game
fields.comment:
Nonzero while the in-game screen is the live one: set to 1 at `0x25D126`, the end of `CInGameIdler::Enter`'s session build, and cleared by `CInGameIdler::Leave` (`0x262337`), by `CFrontEnd`'s enter (`0x2EFE58`) and at `0x2ED9AF`. Zeroed by every construction of the game state.

**This is the attrition gate.** `CUnit::UpdateDaily` tests it at `DailyTickEndGate` (`0x1BB3E8`) and skips both `ApplyAttrition` and `CheckTransportOverload` when it is zero - so it is not a development-era "enable attrition" switch, and attrition does run. About twenty other places test it before touching live game data (`0x255AB7` reaches `strategic_warfare`, `0x4349B2` reaches the player tag), which is the sense the name is taken from: a game is running.

One byte. The last field of the class: the object is allocated `0xDA8` bytes and the constructor tail writes a word at `+0xD9C`, a dword at `+0xDA0` and this byte, so `+0xDA5..+0xDA7` are padding.

Not saved: no access to it lives in the save or load code, and no key in a `.hoi3` save corresponds to it.

**Confirmed in a running game**, not only traced: sampled every frame it read 0 at the main menu with the pointer already live, 1 once a campaign was up - while the clock was still not reporting in play, which is the write landing before the in-game GUI is built - and 0 again on returning to the menu. See `Reversing/Watch.hpp`.

The length is never stored here - every walker recomputes it from provinces_end - provinces_begin.

fields.name: current_experience
fields.comment: **one 64-bit value, not two words**: the loader reads `current_experience` with `%lld` into these eight bytes and CLeader::AddExperience adds to them with `add`/`adc` and compares them against the threshold as a pair. The game's 48.15 fixed point, and a career total rather than a per-level count. **The high half can be reached**: the skill-10 threshold is unreachable by design, so a leader parked there keeps accruing, passing 2^31 after another 5536 experience points. **Read live**: zero high halves on 8000 leaders and a largest total of 809977445, 38% of the way to 2^31

Nothing in the image decrements +0x70, and the only path that lowers it is ResetToStarting, which resets to the definition rather than below it

fields.name: unknown_2a80
fields.comment: An int the constructor defaults to **400**. FINDINGS-fieldmap.md puts default.map's `tree` key here, which would make it a list rather than an int, so the two do not agree and the field is left unnamed rather than named off the weaker of them.

fields.name: by_name
fields.comment: The engine's own string hash table, `{int count; unsigned bucketCount; void** buckets;}` at +0x2A50/+0x2A54/+0x2A58 - the same shape StringHashFind (rva 0x5C7D60) walks. The constructor sets 0x1FF buckets and allocates and zeroes them; **what it indexes is not established here**, but every other instance of this table in the image is a by-name index for a loader, and CMap loads the terrains, continents and regions.

fields.name: unknown_2620
fields.comment: A 0x400-byte table the constructor fills with 0xFF - the 'nothing here yet' fill, beside the zero-filled one at +0x2220. It ends at +0x2A20, where the next run of zeroed words begins. Unidentified.

fields.name: unknown_2220
fields.comment: A 0x400-byte table the constructor zeroes in one memset. Paired with the 0x400 bytes at +0x2620, which it fills with 0xFF instead - a value/validity pair, on the usual reading, but **what they are indexed by is not established here** and 256 dwords fits neither the provinces nor the countries.

fields.name: provinces_end
fields.comment: One past the last province - the `provinces` vector at +0x2200 is a std::vector, and this is its second word. The province count is (this - provinces) / 4.

The constructor runs the CRT vector-constructor iterator over them; the element destructor (rva 0x4A30D0) walks the chain from `first` freeing each node through node+8, so they are used, not vestigial. What indexes them - 512 of what - is **not settled here**; nothing in the constructor says.

fields.name: combats
fields.comment: Every ordinary combat going on in this province - first at +0x2EC, last at +0x2F0, count at +0x2F4, 0x10-byte nodes. CMapProvince::AddCombat appends to it and CMapProvince::HasCombatOfKind walks it. Bombings do not go here: CCombatManager::CreateCombat puts a combat on this list only when the combat's slot 8 is false, and in the same `else` writes +0x2FC when it is true, so +0x2FC is the province's *bombing* slot and this is the list of the rest.

Written only by CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0). A province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id is a depot, and is where the distance relaxation starts.

fields.name: supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: not a hop count - the infrastructure-weighted cost of the cheapest path to the depot, 0 at the depot itself and 100000 while cut off. Each step adds max(4000 - 4*infrastructure, 1000)/1000 - an integer 1..4, worst where infrastructure is lowest - times the entered province's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. Written only by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x289B20, the reset) and CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0, the relaxation). The plain hop count is +0x50.
