fields.name: unknown_24
fields.comment: a per-province traversal cost. CSupply::SpreadFromDepot multiplies it by an infrastructure-derived factor of 1..4 to get the step it adds to supply_depot_distance, and 0xB615E does the same thing without the factor - edi = neighbour->template->+0x24 + accumulated, compared against CProvince +0x10 - so it is a distance charged for entering a province, not an edge length (ProvinceEdge already carries its own distance at +0xC). Its actual value was not sampled from a running game, so whether it is normally 1 is open.

fields.name: sea_province_id
fields.comment:
On a land province (`is_land` set), the id of the one sea province it connects to, as an index into `CMap::provinces` (`+0x2200`); 0 where there is none. Meaningless where `is_land` is clear, and nothing reads it there.

It is the single gate on a fleet crossing the coast. `CPathFind::MayStep` (0x1A2700) and `CPlannedPathFind::MayStep` (0x1A2D30) let a naval unit step out of a land province only to the province this names, and into a land province only from it; a step between two land provinces is refused outright. The helper at `0xA7D70` uses it the other way, replacing a land province by `map->provinces[sea_province_id]` until both ends of a pair are sea, which is also what fixes the target as a sea province: the loop terminates only when the province it lands on has `is_land` clear.

fields.name: is_land
fields.comment: Non-zero on a land province, zero on a sea zone. 245 places in the image read it through a province's `path_node_ptr` (+0xD4), which is why it looked fundamental and unnameable; three of them fix which way round it is. `CPathFind::MayStep` refuses a **naval** step between two provinces that both have it set, and where exactly one has it, that template's `sea_province_id` (+0xA4) must name the other province. `CProvince::IsFrontProvince` (0xA56B0) skips any neighbour that does not have it. `CSafeNavalPathFind::StepCost` only looks for hostile buildings around the destination when the destination does **not** have it - i.e. only when a fleet is entering open sea. `CheckTransportOverload` puts a carried unit ashore only where it is set.

fields.name: terrain
fields.comment: the province's terrain

fields.name: edges_begin
fields.comment: vector of edges to neighbours, begin

fields.name: edges_end
fields.comment: vector of edges to neighbours, end

fields.name: unknown_flag_13d
fields.comment: tested by the supply pass, the Simplified Terrain loop and the supply network builder; 1 in every province seen; not a land/sea flag. In CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork a province with it clear has its supply_depot_distance forced to 0 rather than to the 100000 'not reached yet' value, and in CSupply::SpreadFromDepot such a neighbour is skipped outright - so a province with it clear is never relaxed and never takes part in supply. Still unidentified.

fields.name: crossed_province
fields.comment: The province a kind-1 edge crosses, as an index into CMap::provinces. The helper at rva 0x1A2600 refuses the step when that province's controller is hostile to the unit's owner, or when a foreign unit that is not retreating is standing in it - a strait or crossing that can be blocked.

fields.name: kind
fields.comment: What sort of edge this is. Only two values are tested here: CPathFind::MayStep and CPlannedPathFind::MayStep refuse an edge whose kind is 3 outright, and the helper at rva 0x1A2600 acts only on kind 1, which is a crossing through the province named at +8. The full set of values is not known.

fields.name: to_province
fields.comment: neighbour province id, index into CMap::provinces; edge is 20 bytes

fields.name: distance
fields.comment: distance in thousandths

fields.name: target_province
fields.comment: target province id

fields.name: mode_68
fields.comment: picks between two ways of routing; set by every player move

fields.name: safe
fields.comment: route with CSafePathFind

fields.name: very_safe
fields.comment: route with CVerySafePathFind

fields.name: unit
fields.comment: the unit being redeployed

fields.name: target_province
fields.comment: the province it is going to

fields.name: effect
fields.comment: effect

fields.name: definition_ptr
fields.comment: building definition

fields.name: province_ptr
fields.comment: back to the province

fields.name: level_max
fields.comment: maximum level x1000

fields.name: level_current
fields.comment: current level x1000

fields.name: effect_size
fields.comment: what the building does per level, x1000, and it is only ever one thing: whichever modifier key the definition carries. ic = 1 on industry is 1000, fort_level = 0.4 on land_fort is 400, and a building with no such key is zero. The modifier it belongs to is the definition at +0xC

fields.name: effect
fields.comment: the modifier definition effect_size belongs to; its name is the std::string at +4 - FORT_LEVEL, MODIFIER_IC, MODIFIER_LOCAL_AA, or NONE where the building has no modifier key at all

fields.name: name
fields.comment: building key, e.g. air_base

fields.name: displayName
fields.comment: localised name shown by the game

fields.name: index
fields.comment: index into a province's building array

fields.name: cost
fields.comment: buildings.txt `cost`, x1000: the mod's `cost = 4.5` reads 4500

fields.name: time
fields.comment: buildings.txt `time`, in days, and not scaled

fields.name: capital
fields.comment: buildings.txt's `capital = yes`. Two things read it: the production screen only looks for a build button named after a building that has it, and a construction that finishes with no province only does anything for a flagged building - it makes a CBuildingDeployment and puts it in the country's deployment queue, instead of raising the level in a province. **Read live**: set on 47 of 60 buildings, the exceptions being the forts, infra and BlackICE's request_* entries

fields.name: port
fields.comment: buildings.txt `port`

fields.name: max_allowed_level
fields.comment: maximum allowed level, whole levels

fields.name: on_completion
fields.comment: buildings.txt `on_completion`, a std::string: the practical or theory finishing one feeds

fields.name: technology_category_ptr
fields.comment: the category whose level discounts this building's cost

fields.name: completion_size
fields.comment: buildings.txt `completion_size`, x1000

fields.name: damage_factor
fields.comment: buildings.txt `damage_factor`, x1000

fields.name: onmap
fields.comment: buildings.txt `onmap`

fields.name: visibility
fields.comment: buildings.txt `visibility`

fields.name: show_for_province
fields.comment: buildings.txt `show_for_province`; true unless the file says otherwise

fields.name: prerequisites
fields.comment: buildings.txt `prerequisites`: a `{ ... }` block whose every word becomes a std::string on a list (tail at +0xb0, count at +0xb4). **Nothing reads it** - inside CBuilding's own code the only references are the branch that fills it and the two that empty it, and none of the 44 places that fetch the building database goes on to read it. Neither buildings.txt uses the key, and read live all 61 buildings have it empty

fields.name: prerequisites_last
fields.comment: the tail of the prerequisites list, which nothing reads

fields.name: prerequisites_count
fields.comment: how many prerequisites there are; always zero in practice

fields.name: not_if_x_exists
fields.comment: buildings.txt `not_if_x_exists`: a `{ ... }` block whose every word becomes a std::string on a list (tail at +0xd0, count at +0xd4). **Nothing reads it** - inside CBuilding's own code the only references are the branch that fills it and the two that empty it, and none of the 44 places that fetch the building database goes on to read it. Neither buildings.txt uses the key, and read live all 61 buildings have it empty

fields.name: not_if_x_exists_last
fields.comment: the tail of the not_if_x_exists list, which nothing reads

fields.name: not_if_x_exists_count
fields.comment: how many are in the not_if_x_exists list; always zero

fields.name: confirm
fields.comment: buildings.txt `confirm`

fields.name: orientation
fields.comment: buildings.txt `orientation`

fields.name: repair
fields.comment: buildings.txt `repair`; true unless the file says otherwise

fields.name: building
fields.comment: building being placed

structs.name: CTrigger

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null.

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list.

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape.

structs.comment:
**One condition in the event script language, and the base of all 163 of them.** Its virtual table is the thing worth having: slot 6 is Evaluate.

The size is read from its heirs rather than from an allocation: of the 163 triggers, **129 read `this+0x40`** inside their own Evaluate, and the ones that do are reading their own value there - CAlwaysTrigger's whole Evaluate is `mov al, [ecx+0x40]; ret 4`, and CTagTrigger takes a tag pair from 0x40 and 0x44. So a derived trigger's own data starts at 0x40 and CTrigger is that big.

fields.name: pending_organisation_damage
fields.comment:
**Organisation damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths, spread evenly over the subunits by CUnit::TakeDamage rather than by size.

**It is damage attempted, not damage dealt.** CSubUnit::SettleDamage clamps it to the organisation the subunit actually has (`cmovg` at 0x1ABAE1) before subtracting, so in a one-sided fight most of a tick's total is thrown away. Anything reporting organisation damage has to count the clamped amount at 0x1ABAE7, not this field.

fields.name: pending_strength_damage
fields.comment: **Strength damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths. CUnit::TakeDamage adds to it per landed shot, CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight reads it to tell whether the unit is already finished, and CSubUnit::SettleDamage subtracts it from `strength` and clears it. **Not clamped** - unlike the organisation half.

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the save's `id` pair, written after the id. **Read live**: 41 on what a scenario started with, 4713 on what the game has built since

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the regiment's id, the first half of the save's `id` pair

fields.name: strength_ceiling
fields.comment: set to the regiment's strength when it is built and afterwards only raised to it, never lowered; CUnit slot 24 totals it. Not what the regiment has left - that is +0x5C. saved as `highest`

fields.name: builder
fields.comment: who built it, saved as `builder`, and only where the id half of the tag is set

fields.name: experience
fields.comment: x1000, saved as `experience`

fields.name: sub_unit_definition_ptr
fields.comment: this regiment's definition, with its country's tech applied. saved as `type`, by writing the definition's own name

fields.name: strength
fields.comment: what the regiment has left, in the scale of its definition's max_strength; the supply consumption scales by it, CUnit slot 21 averages it. saved as `strength`

fields.name: organisation
fields.comment: organisation x1000, saved as `organisation`

fields.name: home
fields.comment: where it was raised; the save writes that province's id under `home`, and the loader turns the id back into this pointer. **Read live**: a CMapProvince by its own RTTI, and null on a regiment that was never given one

fields.name: name
fields.comment: historical regiment name, saved as `name`

fields.name: technologies
fields.comment: **the technology levels this regiment was raised with**, one node per entry of its definition's `technologies`, built by CSubUnit::SetType. The save writes a line per node keyed by the technology's own name - `infantry_activation={5 0.000}` - and the loader looks the key up in the technology database, which is what says these are technologies. **Read live**: every node's first word is a CTechnology; none on a CWing, 9 to 52 on a regiment

fields.name: sunk_by_type
fields.comment: type half of the `sunk_by` object id

fields.name: sunk_by_id
fields.comment: what sank this ship, saved as `sunk_by`, and only where the pair is not the game's "no object" one. **Read live**: set on 1123 of 3736 ships

fields.name: is_reserve
fields.comment: saved as `is_reserve`; CRegiment::GetMaxStrength scales the definition's max_strength by RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE where it is set. **Read live**: 1184 of 4000 regiments

fields.name: pride
fields.comment: the pride of the fleet, saved as `pride`. **Read live**: 31 of 3736 ships

fields.name: unit_ptr
fields.comment: the CUnit this regiment belongs to; how the per regiment supply and fuel functions reach the unit's order. **Read live**: a CArmy on every regiment

fields.name: current_distance
fields.comment: how far the regiment is from the enemy in its battle, x1000, saved as `current_distance` - and only where the unit's `combats` list has something in it. **Read live**: zero on all 4000 regiments

fields.name: extra_consumption
fields.comment: every point is another 1% of supply and fuel: the consumption functions add it x10 to a potency whose base is 1000. A cached total - the levels in `technologies` added up, which CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies recomputes. **Read live**: it is that sum on all 10254 sub units in a running game

fields.name: historical_model
fields.comment: which historical model it was raised as, saved as `historical_model`; -1 where it is none. **Read live**: -1 on 3940 of 4000

fields.name: technology
fields.comment: which technology this is the regiment's level of

fields.name: level
fields.comment: the level the regiment has of it; the save's first number, and what CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies adds into extra_consumption

fields.name: progress
fields.comment: x1000, the save's second number. **Read live**: zero on land regiments and set on some ships

fields.name: key
fields.comment: unit type key as in the mod files

fields.name: type_index
fields.comment: sub unit type index, used to index per-type combat vectors

fields.name: is_air
fields.comment: an aircraft type; GetBuildTime gives it AIR_BUILD_SPEED (87)

fields.name: is_ship
fields.comment: unknown

fields.name: is_capital
fields.comment: bool, capital ship

fields.name: is_transport
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: is_sub
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: is_rocket
fields.comment: a rocket type; GetBuildTime gives it ROCKET_BUILD_SPEED (89), and tests this before is_air, which a rocket also has

fields.name: is_tank
fields.comment: an armour type; GetBuildTime gives it TANK_BUILD_SPEED (90)

fields.name: is_buildable
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: can_be_pride
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: technology_category_ptr
fields.comment: the category whose ability discounts this type's build cost - infantry_brigade points at infantry_practical, carrier at carrier_practical

fields.name: technologies
fields.comment: the technologies bearing on this type; end at +0x48. 45 to 56 of them on a loaded definition

fields.name: technologies_end
fields.comment: one past the last technology

fields.name: terrain_adjusters
fields.comment: the terrain modifiers, a vector of CUnitAdjuster **indexed by terrain id**, ending at +0x58. **Read live**: 45 entries on every definition, 28 of them non-zero on an engineer_brigade, and they are the unit file's terrain blocks exactly - 16 is `urban`, 17 `plains`, 18 `woods`, 32 `mountain`

fields.name: terrain_adjusters_end
fields.comment: one past the last terrain adjuster

fields.name: night
fields.comment: the `night` block of the unit file, held by value. **Read live**: 0.7 attack on a commando_brigade, 0.5 on a paratrooper_brigade, -2.0 movement on a naval_corps_hq_brigade, each exactly what that file says

fields.name: fort
fields.comment: the `fort` block. **Read live**: `{0.55, 0.55}` on an armor_brigade, `{0.9, 0.15}` on an engineer_brigade

fields.name: river
fields.comment: the `river` block. **Read live**: `{-0.5, 0.35, -0.75}` on an armor_brigade, `{1.35, 0.1, 0.35}` on an engineer_brigade

fields.name: amphibious
fields.comment: the `amphibious` block. **Read live**: `{-1.1, -1.1}` on an armor_brigade, `{-0.3, -0.5}` on an engineer_brigade

fields.name: other_adjusters
fields.comment: a second vector of CUnitAdjuster, ending at +0xC8 and walked by the same code as the terrain one. **Read live**: empty on every definition in this mod

fields.name: other_adjusters_end
fields.comment: one past the last of them

fields.name: supply_consumption
fields.comment: base figure for one sub unit

fields.name: fuel_consumption
fields.comment: base figure for one sub unit

fields.name: carrier_size
fields.comment: how many carrier air groups the ship carries, x1000 like the rest of the definition. IsCarrier (0x94650) is this being above zero, so a ship with none is not a carrier to the game

fields.name: sprite
fields.comment: unit picture

fields.name: unit_group
fields.comment: which combined arms group the type is in: a one based index into common/combined_arms.txt's own order, 0 for none

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like. See CPersistent.hpp

fields.name: attack
fields.comment: saved as `attack`, x1000, by the game's own CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey

fields.name: defence
fields.comment: saved as `defence`, x1000, by the game's own CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey

fields.name: movement
fields.comment: saved as `movement`, x1000, by the game's own CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey

fields.name: attrition
fields.comment: saved as `attrition`, x1000, by the game's own CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey. **Read live**: `urban` on an engineer_brigade is `{0.46, 0.4, -0.35, 1}`, which is that unit file's urban block to the digit

fields.name: id
fields.comment: terrain id

fields.name: name
fields.comment: terrain name; length at +0x38

fields.name: movement_cost
fields.comment: x1000, from the terrain's `movement_cost` - mountain 1.6, plains 2.0, ocean 1.0, urban 1.25, woods 1.45, all matching `map/terrain.txt`. **Parsed and then never used**: the game does not take it into account, so a unit's speed in a terrain is its own per-terrain modifier on max_speed and nothing else

fields.name: is_water
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: temperature
fields.comment: x1000, from the terrain's `temperature`. **Read live**: -10000 on mountain, which declares `-10`, and zero on the four terrains compared that declare none - one positive sample

fields.name: precipitation
fields.comment: x1000, from the terrain's `precipitation`. **Read live**: 10000 on mountain, which declares `10`, and zero on the four that declare none

fields.name: name
fields.comment: trait name

fields.name: effect_values
fields.comment: what each effect is worth, in thousandths

fields.name: effect_kinds
fields.comment: which of the 31 effects each one is - CTrait::Effect in the header, numbered as CTrait::LoadKey's jump table numbers them

fields.name: effect_types
fields.comment: the terrain each terrain_* effect names, empty for the rest. The stride is 0x1C against a string's 0x18, and **read live** the four spare bytes hold fragments of the parser's buffer - they are padding nothing writes

fields.name: effect_count
fields.comment: how many of the sixteen are used

fields.name: allowed_land
fields.comment: from `allowed_leader`; all three are set outright when the key is absent

fields.name: allowed_sea
fields.comment: from `allowed_leader`

fields.name: allowed_air
fields.comment: from `allowed_leader`

fields.name: count
fields.comment: number of entries

fields.name: traits_begin
fields.comment: trait vector begin; index 0 is a CNullTrait

fields.name: traits_end
fields.comment: trait vector end

fields.name: defences_used
fields.comment: **How many shots this unit has already defended against this tick.** CUnit::RollToHit compares it against the slots its defence value bought and increments it on each one spent; past that the unit falls back to CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF. Reset per tick somewhere not yet found.

fields.name: combat_modifiers_count
fields.comment: How many modifiers are on the list. **The one to watch** when looking for what adds to it: the head at +0xDC is only written by a push onto an empty list, while every addition has to touch this.

fields.name: combat_modifiers_last
fields.comment: The list's last node - the `last` of the CList at +0xDC.

fields.name: combat_defend_modifier_b
fields.comment: **The other defend multiplier**, thousandths, written by slot 19 beside +0xF4 and compared against 0x3E8 the same way (0x32ACF6).

fields.name: combat_attack_modifier_b
fields.comment: **The other attack multiplier**, thousandths, written by CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (slot 19) once a tick. The game compares it against 0x3E8 and skips the block when equal (0x32ABC6), which is only worth doing for a factor of one.

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every modifier's defend side**, the same shape as +0xEC and filled by the same function. The tooltip prints `+0xF0 * +0xF8 / 1000` as its Defend Modifier (0x32AE8A).

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every modifier's attack side**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1C3040) multiplies each one in as it is added - `product = product * (delta + 1000) / 1000` - and CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers seeds it with 1000, an empty product. The battle tooltip prints `+0xEC * +0xF4 / 1000` as its Attack Modifier (0x32AE39).

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment: **The combat modifiers acting on this unit, on land only**, a CList: first here, last at +0xE0, count at +0xE4, all three cleared together by CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers (0x1C2FE0). One node per modifier; the node's record holds the id at +0 and the attack and defend values at +4 and +8, which the tooltip prints as `x%/y%` when they differ. 0x164060 turns the id into its BM_* key.

fields.name: plan_their_power
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x84, the `their_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the opposition's strength. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel.

fields.name: plan_our_power
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x80, the `our_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the owner's strength for it. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel.

fields.name: plan_naval_stance
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x14, the `naval_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it.

fields.name: plan_air_stance
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x10, the `air_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it.

fields.name: plan_stance
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0xC, the `stance` key. Defaults to 2 when the plan is switched off. The one plan attribute whose change makes CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute call CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds; 5 is the command's "not set" sentinel.

fields.name: plan_active
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x8. Whether the unit's battle plan is switched on; CUnitPlan::SetActive (0x4DEB10) resets the whole plan when it goes to zero.

fields.name: plan_subunit_wanted
fields.comment: The composition the plan asks for, per subunit type - the array 0x4E1D00 fills from the plan and the owner's available subunit types. Sits inside CUnit::plan at plan+0x70.

fields.name: plan_subunit_needed
fields.comment: Per subunit type, the part of the deficit that the group as a whole is still short of - min(difference[i], whatever is left of that group's net difference), taken in index order. This is the list the plan machinery asks for.

fields.name: plan_subunit_group_difference
fields.comment: The same differences summed onto one representative subunit type per group (0x1ADF70 does the folding: carrier air, capital ship, transport/submarine, and so on). Zeroed at the top of each pass and accumulated at 0x1BD544.

fields.name: plan_subunit_difference
fields.comment: Per CSubUnitDefinition::type_index: what the plan wants of that type minus what the unit's OOB actually has. Signed - a negative entry is a surplus. Written wholesale by CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (0x1BD240) and cleared by CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds for an HQ that has no plan.

fields.name: is_selected
fields.comment: the unit is selected - one byte; +0x5 to +0x7 are other fields

fields.name: type
fields.comment: type

fields.name: id
fields.comment: unit id

fields.name: regiments
fields.comment: the unit's own regiments; a CList<CSubUnit*> base in RTTI

fields.name: upgrade_prio
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: upgrade_active
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: reinforcements_active
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: disengage
fields.comment: saved as `disengage`. **Read live**: zero on 696 of 750 units and a small number on the rest

fields.name: order_ptr
fields.comment: the unit's current order

fields.name: CSubUnitDefinitionPtr
fields.comment: sub unit definition

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: a date, saved as `end_date`. **Read live**: the epoch value on most units, so unset

fields.name: combat_cooldown
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `attack_delay`, which agrees with this name

fields.name: supply_received_percentage
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `supplies`, which agrees with this name

fields.name: fuel_received_percentage
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `fuel`, which agrees with this name

fields.name: combats
fields.comment: the combats this unit is in. The sub unit writer only writes `current_distance` where this has something in it. **Read live**: 168 of 2000 armies, and what the nodes hold is a CLandCombat

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: the owner

fields.name: leader_ptr
fields.comment: commanding leader

fields.name: current_province_ptr
fields.comment: province the unit is in

fields.name: supplied_from_province_ptr
fields.comment: **CUnit::LoadKey reads it under the key `previous`**, putting a province here, which fits a previous province better than a supply source - and +0x138 and +0x13C are the movement pointers. The BiceLib name is left as it is; which is right has not been settled

fields.name: movement_progress
fields.comment: saved as `movement_progress`, x1000. **Read live**: zero or a part of the way

fields.name: retreat
fields.comment: saved as `retreat`. **Read live**: 11 of 750 units retreating

fields.name: in_game_idler_ptr
fields.comment: the in game idler

fields.name: name
fields.comment: the unit's name

fields.name: arrow_state
fields.comment: saved as `arrow_state`. **Read live**: zero on every unit

fields.name: dig_in_level
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `dig_in`, which agrees with this name

fields.name: higher_oob_unit_ptr
fields.comment: parent unit in the order of battle

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the units directly below this one

fields.name: oob_level
fields.comment: 0 theatre .. 4 division, 5 navy

fields.name: plan
fields.comment: The unit's battle plan, **held by value, not by pointer** - CUnit's constructor builds a CUnitPlan in place here at 0x1B5232 and its destructor destroys it in place at 0x1B5799. 0x90 bytes, so it runs to +0x28B and expeditionary_owner at +0x28C is the next field. Every plan field already recorded on CUnit is this object's offset plus 0x1FC: +0x204 plan_active = plan +0x8, +0x208 plan_stance = +0xC, +0x20C plan_air_stance = +0x10, +0x210 plan_naval_stance = +0x14, +0x26C plan_subunit_wanted = +0x70, +0x27C plan_our_power = +0x80, +0x280 plan_their_power = +0x84. The save writes it under `plan` by calling slot 1 on it, which works because +0x1FC is the embedded object's own vftable pointer.

fields.name: carrying
fields.comment: the units a fleet is carrying: CheckTransportOverload sums their definitions' transport_weight over this list and compares it with the fleet's own transport_capacity

fields.name: expeditionary_owner
fields.comment: who the unit is on loan from, saved as `expeditionary_owner`. **Read live**: `---` on 740 of 750, and ITA, HUN, SLO and POL on the rest

fields.name: layer_mask_ec
fields.comment: ANDed with +0xF0 by the renderer

fields.name: layer_mask
fields.comment: layer mask written by every map mode setter

fields.name: map_style
fields.comment: style the water shader picks its technique from; 16, 18, 19 colour the sea

fields.name: debug_saves
fields.comment: 0 rotates three autosave files; N saves a dated file every Nth month

fields.name: autosave_frequency
fields.comment: 0 never .. 5 five-yearly

structs.name: Hoi3CString
structs.comment:
**MSVC's std::basic_string<char>**, under the name BiceLib gives it in HoiDataStructures.hpp. `stringData` is the small-string union - the characters themselves up to fifteen, a pointer to them past that - `length` is `_Mysize`, and `maxLength` is `_Myres`, which starts at 0xF for exactly that reason. Its methods are named as what they are: std::string::assign, appendChars, appendString, fromCString, concat, clear, operator= and operatorPlus.

The name stays `Hoi3CString` rather than becoming `std::string`: it is a real type in BiceLib's own headers, used by ten game classes and read by the DLL at runtime, so the findings and the code that consumes them have to agree. Ghidra also does not take `::` in a structure's name the way it does in a function's, where it means a class namespace.

**0x18 - the three fields, and nothing after them.** This read 0x1C for a while, reasoning from the gap between string fields in about twenty classes. That gap is real, but it is a *stride* rather than a size: those classes leave four bytes after each string, which is what CTrait.hpp means by indexing its Hoi3CString[16] with an explicit 0x1C instead of a sizeof.

What settles it is a string passed **by value**, which measures the size directly. CKillLeaderEffect::GetText and CLoadOOBEffect::GetText both `ret 40` where the sibling shape without the string is 16 - a difference of exactly 24. CBuilding::CBuilding cannot tell the two apart, because 4+24+4+4 and 4+28+4 both reach its ret 36.

fields.name: goods_cost
fields.comment: the goods_cost block of defines.lua. CDefines::Load loads this pointer into a register and stores each entry of the block through it at a compiled-in offset, keyed by name. 7 entries, SUPPLIES at +0x0 to RARE_MATERIALS at +0x18. No struct is recorded for it yet; `python definesMap.py --block goods_cost` prints the map.

fields.name: map
fields.comment: the map block of defines.lua. CDefines::Load loads this pointer into a register and stores each entry of the block through it at a compiled-in offset, keyed by name. 10 entries, SUEZ at +0x0 to GIBRALTAR_BLOCKER at +0x24, and these are read by rva 0x460D0 as plain ints, not scaled - they are province ids. The mod's WHITESEA and WHITESEA_BLOCKER are not among them and are never read. No struct is recorded for it yet; `python definesMap.py --block map` prints the map.

fields.name: id
fields.comment: Which modifier this is. The constructor at rva 0x56D50 takes it in edx and writes it here, and it is what everything that asks about a modifier compares - CBuildingDataBase's role ladder at rva 0xB78AB is five of these in a row, deciding which building is the naval base, the air base, the anti-air, the underground and the industry. Typed as the ModifierId enum so those read as names; the enum is built by reversing/modifierIds.py out of the global initialiser, which is the only place the 107 names exist.

fields.name: persistent_meta
fields.comment: 0x18D

fields.name: values
fields.comment: the values, one entry per ModifierType and indexed by it; CModifier::GetValue reads [this+0x18][type*8]. Typed as a structure of named entries so a read is a field rather than an index. **The index is the definition's registration order, which is CModifier::id only up to 101.** The global initialiser builds 108 definitions in array order but stamps ids that are not in that order at the end: entries 102..107 are LAND_INTEL_BOOST (id 103), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST (id 104), LOCAL_UNDERGROUND (id 102), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST a second time (id 104 again), STRATEGIC_RESOURCE_EFFICIENCY (id 105) and LOCAL_UNIT_SPEED (id 106). So an index below 102 can be read straight off reversing/modifierIds.py, and one at or above 102 has to be read off this structure instead - while a comparison against CModifier +0x24 `id` is the other way round.

fields.name: type
fields.comment: the token's kind, itself a token id: 1 `=`, 3 `{`, 4 `}`, 0x10 a newline, 0x11 a tab, 0x12 a space, 0x13 the end of input, and on the write side 0xC tok_int, 0xD tok_fixed (`%d.%03d`, a thousandths value), 0xE tok_bool (`yes`/`no`), 0xF tok_word (a name, and a quoted string), 0x14 tok_uint, 0x18F long_float. In a binary save this is what gets written, as two bytes, and tok_newline, tok_tab and 0x12 are dropped instead.

fields.name: text
fields.comment: the token as text, which is what a text save carries

fields.name: depth
fields.comment: how deep in braces the writer is, starting at -1 so the outermost object writes none. CPersistent::Save raises it and lowers it again.

fields.name: stream
fields.comment: the stream written to; its vftable holds write-text at +0x14 and write-bytes at +0x20

fields.name: binary
fields.comment: set for a binary save: token ids go out as two bytes each, and the indenting and newlines are skipped

fields.name: messages_count
fields.comment: How many messages are in the list; cleared when it is freed. Nothing reads it on the way out, which is why a file full of unknown keys is silent.

fields.name: messages_last
fields.comment: Last node of the parse messages list; cleared with the other two when the list is freed.

fields.name: messages_first
fields.comment: First node of the parse messages list; a node is two Hoi3CStrings at +0 and +0x20 with the next pointer at +0x40. CParseContext::FreeMessages is handed this field's address - the destructor passes `this+4` - and frees the chain.

fields.name: error_handler
fields.comment: Null in the ordinary constructor (0x67A460); set from the caller's EDI by the second one (0x67A520), whose six call sites are all in the 0xB3xxxx network module. `ReportParseError` (0x67A960) sets the byte at its `+4`, calls its slot 0 with the parse context and, where that returns true, sets `+5` as well and queues no message. `ParseObjectReference` (0x1EC150) reads the same three and stores nothing when all three are set, so once the handler has taken an error the block is still consumed but its value is dropped. project.json already describes `+4` in ReportParseError's comment; this names the field it hangs off.

fields.name: session_name
fields.comment: The name the context was made with - the third argument of `CParseContext::CParseContext` (0x67A460), which takes it in EDX and assigns it here; the destructor (0x67A630) frees it with the usual `capacity >= 0x10` test, size at `+0x33C` and capacity at `+0x340`. Two constructor call sites pass the literal `UNNAMED_SESSION` (0x1002AF, 0x231700), which is where the name comes from. Exactly two places read it: `CCommand::LoadKey` (0x67BCD0) copies it into the command's own string at `+8` when that is still empty, and `ParseObjectReference` (0x1EC150) copies it into every object reference it fills. Nothing writes it after construction and neither copy is ever saved, so it is a runtime label for which stream a command or a reference came out of. **The `session` reading is inferred** from the default literal; what is checked is that it is a string and who its five users are.

fields.name: tokenizer
fields.comment: the tokenizer; its current CToken is at +0xC and a flag saying one is ready at +0x110

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the key just read. Its type is the token id CPersistent::Load hands slot 4, which is what a class switches on.

fields.name: separator
fields.comment: the `=` between the key and the value

fields.name: value
fields.comment: the value just read, which slot 4 converts out of its text

fields.name: supply_depot_hops
fields.comment: the plain hop count to the depot, as against the weighted cost at +0x4C. Zeroed for every province by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork and set to the parent's value plus one each time CSupply::SpreadFromDepot relaxes a neighbour. CSupply::DailySupplyPass never reads it; the only other reader found is 0xDB3CC.

fields.name: combats
fields.comment: The same field as CMapProvince +0x2EC; project.json carries both structures with the same offsets because Ghidra has no inheritance between them.

fields.name: port
fields.comment: the province's map port - the link to the sea province beside it - or null where it has none. Built at map load from the land/sea adjacency, not from buildings.txt; the naval base building is the separate thing at +0x300, and the sea hop tests both.

fields.name: underground
fields.comment: buildings[underground.index]: the province's underground, cached at rva 0x96A5F out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x28.

fields.name: anti_air
fields.comment: buildings[anti_air.index]: the province's anti-air, cached at rva 0x968C7 out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x24.

fields.name: air_base
fields.comment: buildings[air_base.index]: the province's air base, cached at rva 0x9694F out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x1C.

fields.name: naval_base
fields.comment: buildings[naval_base.index]: the province's naval base, cached at rva 0x969D7 out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x20. Never null once the province has been reset - the array holds one CProvinceBuilding per defined building - so readers test its level at +0x20, not the pointer.

fields.name: underground_action
fields.comment: The underground action here, saved as `underground_action`; **2 is the default and is not written**, which is the only field of the province with a non-zero skip value. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the same in both.

fields.name: revolt_risk
fields.comment: Revolt risk, thousandths, saved as `revolt_risk` and only when positive. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the same in both.

fields.name: strategic_resource
fields.comment: The strategic resource here, as a **pointer to the entry in the strategic-resource CNameDataBase**, not a number. Null when the province has none. The entry carries its key as an Hoi3CString at +0x30 and answers a bool from virtual slot 14, which is what decides whether the key is written at all.

fields.name: last_convoy_attack
fields.comment: a date, saved as `last_convoy_attack` once it is set

fields.name: out_of_supply_days
fields.comment: saved as `out_of_supply_days`, and only above zero

fields.name: nationalism
fields.comment: saved as `nationalism`, and only when it is not null

fields.name: victory_points
fields.comment: victory points. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: supply_depot_id
fields.comment: province id of the depot it draws from, and the supply network's label: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot only relaxes a neighbour that already carries the same value, and CSupply::DailySupplyPass only moves goods between provinces that do. Written only by CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0), from the province's area or, failing that, from CCountry::FindSupplyDepot on the controller - which answers the supplying country's acting capital. A province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id is a depot, and is where the distance relaxation starts. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: not a hop count - the infrastructure-weighted cost of the cheapest path to the depot, 0 at the depot itself and 100000 while cut off. Each step adds max(4000 - 4*infrastructure, 1000)/1000 - an integer 1..4, worst where infrastructure is lowest - times the entered province's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. Written only by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x289B20, the reset) and CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0, the relaxation). The plain hop count is +0x50. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: country
fields.comment:
The country this brigade definition belongs to. SetName writes +0x8 and +0xC as two separate dwords from two separate arguments and hands +0x8 to the tag lookup at 0x402610, which is a CCountryTag - four tag characters then an id, filling exactly the eight bytes to id_type at +0x10.

This read `display_name`, an Hoi3CString, until the wave of 2026-09-24. A string here is 0x1C bytes and would have swallowed +0xC, +0x10, +0x14 and the name at +0x18 - and measuring the gap after every Hoi3CString field in this file gives 0x1C in around twenty places across unrelated classes, with this the only one that gave 0x8. Both the code and the layout said the same thing; nothing had asked either.

structs.name: LogRecord

fields.name: vbptr
fields.comment: The virtual base pointer, 0x15FCE98, whose vbtable reads {0, 0x78} - which is what puts the basic_ios base at +0x78 rather than the +0x50 a plain ostringstream keeps it at.

fields.name: sink
fields.comment: The LogSink this line goes to; FlushAndDestruct calls slot 1 of its vftable, which is the recorded LogSink::Write. Typed void* because LogSink has no layout here yet.

fields.name: file
fields.comment: The source file the line was logged from. An Hoi3CString, not a `const char*`: the constructor assignStrings into it, and every call site runs its literal through std::string::fromCString first.

fields.name: line
fields.comment: The source line, read at [ios-8] for the sink call.

fields.name: channel
fields.comment: Which log channel the line belongs to, read at [ios-4].

structs.comment:
The temporary every log line in the game is built into: `LogRecord::Make(file, line, channel) << "text" << ... << endl`. It is a std::basic_ostringstream<char> with four fields of its own added, which is why its basic_ios virtual base sits at +0x78 instead of +0x50.

**Two gaps, deliberately.** +0x04..+0x4F is the std::basic_stringbuf (0x4C bytes, vftable 0x15F2B34, with _Seekhigh at +0x40 and _Mystate at +0x44), and +0x78 is the std::basic_ios virtual base (0x44 bytes, vftable 0x15FCE94). Neither type is modelled here, and a byte blob would claim a layout nobody has read, so they are left undefined and described instead.

The size of 0xBC is **inferred**: basic_ios' last written member is _Fillch at +0x40, giving at least 0x41 and 0x44 by alignment. Every LogRecord in the image is a stack local, so no allocation size settles it.

structs.name: CUnitPlan
structs.comment:
A unit's battle plan, held **by value** at CUnit +0x1FC - CUnit's constructor calls this class's constructor on `this + 0x1FC` and its destructor mirrors it, and 0x90 is exactly the gap to expeditionary_owner at +0x28C.

The layout was read three ways that agree: the constructor field by field, CUnitPlan::LoadKey's sixteen cases, and CUnitPlan::SaveContents writing the same token for the same offset. Three offsets are left out because nothing identified them - +0x58, +0x6C, and +0x7C, which is the one field the constructor never initialises.

The same vector CUnit reaches as plan_subunit_wanted at +0x26C. **It is twelve bytes, +0x70..+0x7B** - _Myfirst, _Mylast, _Myend, with no stored allocator - so **+0x7C is a separate dword**, and it is the one field CUnitPlan's constructor never initialises.

structs.name: CSubUnitDataBase
structs.comment:
Every subunit definition the game loaded, reached through g_CSubUnitDataBase. It has no virtual table, which is why the RTTI never named it and three passes left it as DAT_ - the name came from luabind, which registers the class and so forced a type_info the RTTI export does not index.

+0x2C..+0xAC holds 33 cached role definitions the constructor does not initialise, and which nothing has identified; they are left out rather than guessed at.

fields.name: by_name
fields.comment: a 0x1FF-bucket hash map from a definition's key to the definition.

fields.name: definitions_begin
fields.comment: the start of the definition array; GetSubUnitByIndex indexes it.

fields.name: definitions_end

structs.name: CEU3BitmapFontKerning
structs.comment: One kerning pair of a glyph: how much the pen moves by when this glyph is followed by `second`. Nearly always -1 in the fonts shipped; garamond_16 has 199 of them across all glyphs.

fields.name: second
fields.comment: the character code that has to follow for this pair to apply

fields.name: amount
fields.comment: pixels added to the advance, almost always negative

structs.name: CEU3BitmapFontGlyph
structs.comment: One character of a bitmap font, as CEU3BitmapFont::LoadGlyphs builds it from a `char` line of the .fnt. The first seven fields are that line's numbers in file order. Fixed size whether or not the glyph has any kerning: (0x81C - 0x1C) / 8 is 256, so the pair array is sized for every possible partner.

fields.name: x
fields.comment: left edge in the font texture

fields.name: y
fields.comment: top edge in the font texture

fields.name: width
fields.comment: how wide the glyph is in the texture, which is not what the pen moves by

fields.name: height
fields.comment: how tall it is; forced to 0 for the space (id 0x20) at 0x6FA3BD whatever the file says, and GetStringWidth reads a zero height as a glyph that draws no ink

fields.name: xoffset
fields.comment: where the glyph is drawn relative to the pen

fields.name: yoffset
fields.comment: the same vertically

fields.name: xadvance
fields.comment: **what the pen moves by** - the number that decides how wide text draws. The .fnt's value reaches here unchanged, since the parse is positional and nothing scales it

fields.name: kerning
fields.comment: pairs in the order the .fnt listed them, only the first kerning_count of them meaning anything

fields.name: kerning_count
fields.comment: how many of the pairs are filled; zeroed as the glyph is made and incremented by each kerning line naming this glyph first

structs.name: CEU3BitmapFont
structs.comment: A bitmap font, one per `bitmapfont` block in interface/core.gfx. Only the two fields the text measuring needed are known.

fields.name: font_name
fields.comment: the `fontName` key, which is the stem of both gfx/fonts/<name>.tga and the .fnt beside it. CEU3BitmapFont::LoadKey takes the key straight onto this+0x78 and both loaders read it from there; 0x78 + 0x18 leaves it ending at 0x90, four bytes short of the glyph table

fields.name: glyphs
fields.comment: one pointer per character code, null where the font has no such glyph. Indexed by the raw byte in GetStringWidth, so 256 entries exactly - and 0x94 + 256 * 4 is 0x494, which is the next field LoadGlyphs writes (0x6FA26D), so the length is measured rather than assumed

structs.name: MapCamera
structs.comment:
Where the map is looked at from, held by value inside CInGameIdler at +0x1938 and reached through CInGameIdler::GetMapCamera. Named for what it holds: it has no vftable, so there is nothing in the RTTI export to name it after.

Only the fields the scrolling touches are known; the zoom and rotation it also carries have not been worked out.

fields.name: edge_left
fields.comment: the screen x the map starts at. The mouse being within six pixels of it scrolls the map west

fields.name: edge_top
fields.comment: the screen y the map starts at; within six pixels scrolls north

fields.name: edge_right
fields.comment: the screen x the map ends at; within six pixels scrolls east

fields.name: edge_bottom
fields.comment: the screen y the map ends at; within six pixels scrolls south

fields.name: x
fields.comment: where the camera is looking, in map coordinates. This is what every kind of scrolling adds to and what the clamp bounds

fields.name: y
fields.comment: the same, north to south

fields.name: x_settled
fields.comment: a second copy of `x`. CentreOnProvince and the camera's own setup both write the position and then copy it into this pair, which is what makes those moves immediate - so this is the value the camera has rather than the one it is heading for. Which of the two the renderer reads has not been checked

fields.name: y_settled
fields.comment: the same, north to south

vftable_slots._about: Slot names BiceLib has established but that cannot be read off the slot's body - the linker folds identical bodies together, so the three unit predicates are one `mov al,1; ret` and one `xor al,al; ret` between them. Keyed by class, then slot. A record on a base class names that slot in every table below it, which is how CPersistent's six virtuals reach all 754 classes that derive from it; a name read off the slot's own body wins over one inherited this way.
